entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, a City of Melbourne planning scheme amendment introducing mandatory and preferred environmentally sustainable design (ESD) standards for new buildings and large alterations, as it applies to a freight-forwarding workspace. C376 is a municipal-level Victorian planning instrument, not a national or freight-sector regulation; it binds land developers, building owners, and planning permit applicants in the City of Melbourne, not freight forwarders as such. Its direct relevance to this workspace is genuinely limited to circumstances where the workspace itself develops, owns, or materially alters a building (for example, a warehouse, depot, or office) within the City of Melbourne municipality that meets the new-building or large-addition thresholds below.

FACT: "will in turn assist the City of Melbourne to achieve its target of net zero emissions by 2040" *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Analytical inference:* this brief treats C376 as a workspace-adjacent instrument rather than a directly binding freight-sector regulation, because the source materials define its obligated parties as developers, owners, and permit applicants, not logistics intermediaries.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Amendment applies to all land in the municipality that is subject to the Melbourne Planning Scheme (Planning Scheme)." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "it does not apply to Commonwealth land, the Port of Melbourne and land within the Transport Zone" *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

*Operational implication:* the amendment applies to essentially all privately held land in the municipality that is subject to the Melbourne Planning Scheme; a workspace-owned or workspace-leased logistics facility, depot, or office within City of Melbourne boundaries falls inside this scope unless it sits on Commonwealth land, the Port of Melbourne, or land in the Transport Zone.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific workspace-held site in the City of Melbourne is subject to the Melbourne Planning Scheme, or falls within one of the named carve-outs, is a site-specific planning question requiring confirmation against the current planning scheme maps and, where relevant, counsel review.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Amendment C376 was unanimously adopted by Council at the 29 July 2025 meeting." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "The amendment has been sent to the Minister for Planning for final approval and gazettal." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

*Operational implication:* the amendment has been adopted by Council but is not yet in force; it becomes operative only on gazettal by the Minister for Planning, which had not been confirmed as at this item's capture date. A workspace with a Melbourne development in the pipeline should track gazettal status directly rather than assume any C376 requirement already binds a current planning application.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Most developments in the Capital City Zone and Docklands Zone will be subject to sustainable transport requirements." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Analytical inference:* C376's compliance chain runs from the planning permit applicant (the developer or building owner) to the responsible authority (City of Melbourne as planning authority); it does not create a compliance obligation running to a freight forwarder acting purely as a tenant, customer, or logistics service provider to a Melbourne-based business.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace itself, or a landlord/developer the workspace contracts with for warehouse or office space in Melbourne, is the party that bears the C376 planning-permit obligations on a given project is a fact-specific question requiring review of the relevant lease, development agreement, or permit application.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The Planning Panel completed its report on 18 October 2024 and recommended that the Amendment should proceed, subject to a number of changes." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "The independent Planning Panel Hearing was held from 19 August to 23 August 2024." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "Buildings are the biggest contributor of carbon emissions in the City of Melbourne, accounting for 66 per cent of all emissions." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Operational implication:* the independent Planning Panel process (submissions, hearing, and report) is the authoritative record of what changed between Council's draft and the adopted DDO73 text; the Panel Report is the primary document to consult for the reasoning behind any specific mandatory or preferred standard.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The amendment has been sent to the Minister for Planning for final approval and gazettal." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

FACT: "Ministerial amendment VC216 was gazetted." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

*Operational implication:* the single pending regulatory event that determines when C376 takes legal effect is Ministerial gazettal; no other approval step remains in the source materials once gazettal occurs. Separately, the earlier state-level Ministerial amendment VC216 already strengthened ESD-related policy in the Victoria Planning Provisions, which is the state policy backdrop C376 operates within, not a further pending step for C376 itself.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace need a planning permit for a Melbourne development?**

FACT: "All developments requiring a planning permit will be subject to new planning policy about environmentally sustainable design" *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific proposed workspace project (new building, or an alteration/addition) triggers a planning permit requirement under the Melbourne Planning Scheme is a site- and project-specific question requiring direct confirmation with City of Melbourne or a planning consultant.

**Q2: Does C376 apply to an existing workspace-occupied building?**

FACT: "The new planning rules will only apply to new planning applications." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Analytical inference:* no. C376's standards apply only to new planning applications; a workspace occupying an existing Melbourne building that is not itself lodging a new building or major-addition planning application is not required to retrofit that building to meet C376 standards.

**Q3: Is the workspace itself ever the permit applicant?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* only if the workspace directly develops, constructs, or materially alters a building in the City of Melbourne would it stand in the position of "applicant" the DDO73 obligations below are written against; where the workspace is a tenant of a third-party-owned facility, the compliance obligation runs to the landlord or developer instead.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: the obligations below are DDO73's own standards on a planning permit applicant (the developer, building owner, or their consultant), reproduced here so a workspace that IS such an applicant (or is assessing a Melbourne facility a counterparty is developing) can see the actual compliance bar. They do not run to a freight forwarder acting purely as a tenant or logistics service provider (Section 4).*

**1. Environmentally Sustainable Design, new buildings up to 5,000 sqm.** FACT: "Should achieve a minimum 50% BESS score." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**2. Energy efficiency, BESS Energy category.** FACT: "Should achieve a minimum 60% score in the BESS Energy category." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**3. Residential energy performance (NatHERS).** FACT: "Residential should also achieve an average of at least 7.5 star NatHERS rating across multiple dwellings, and a minimum of 6.5 star NatHERS rating for each dwelling." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**4. Environmentally Sustainable Design, larger new buildings.** FACT: "Should achieve 5 Star Green Star Buildings." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**5. Urban heat island response.** FACT: "Should provide the equivalent of at least 75% of the development’s total site area as building or landscape elements that reduce the impact of the urban heat island effect." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**6. Urban ecology, Green Factor score.** FACT: "Should be designed and constructed to achieve a minimum Green Factor score of 0.55 using City of Melbourne’s Green Factor Tool." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**7. Integrated water management.** FACT: "Should connect to a precinct scale recycled water source if available. Unless connected to a recycled water source, should install a rainwater tank to support on-site green cover or supply a minimum of 10% of internal water demand." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**8. Waste and resource recovery.** FACT: "Should provide waste and resource recovery facilities that meet the requirements of the City of Melbourne’s Guidelines for Waste Management Plans." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**9. Sustainable Design Assessment, small developments.** FACT: "A Sustainable Design Assessment (SDA) is required for small developments and is a report that details how the small development meets each of the standards and requirements in Schedule 73 to the Design and Development Overlay and can be integrated with a BESS assessment" *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

**10. Sustainability Management Plan, large developments.** FACT: "A Sustainable Management Plan (SMP) is required for large developments and is a report that provides additional detail of how a large development meets each of the standards and requirements in Schedule 73 to the Design and Development Overlay" *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

**11. Green Building Council registration.** FACT: "Yes, to provide adequate evidence that a development meets the required Green Star Buildings rating, the project must be registered with the Green Building Council of Australia." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

**12. Qualified-person reporting requirement.** FACT: "You must engage a suitably qualified person to prepare the report demonstrating compliance with the relevant tools." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

**13. Trigger for applicability (primary compliance deadline).** FACT: "The new planning rules will only apply to new planning applications." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

**14. Enforcement mechanism (penalty/consequence for non-compliance).** FACT: "A permit cannot be granted to vary a requirement expressed with the term 'must' or a requirement that relates to a minimum (mandatory) standard of this schedule." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

**15. Transitional exemption (exceptions/carve-outs).** FACT: "Adding a transitional provision to exempt the requirements of DDO73 from an application made before the commencement of Amendment C376." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

**16. Scope of application.** FACT: "The Amendment applies to all land in the municipality that is subject to the Melbourne Planning Scheme (Planning Scheme)." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

*Operational implication:* obligations 1-12 are the substantive design/reporting standards; obligation 13 is the applicability trigger (a new planning application, not a calendar date, since gazettal itself has no confirmed date in the source materials); obligation 14 is the enforcement consequence for non-compliance (permit refusal for failing a mandatory "must" standard, not a fine or infringement notice); obligations 15-16 are the qualification categories below. All 16 are workspace-adjacent only insofar as the workspace itself is, or contracts with, the permit applicant for a Melbourne building project (Section 4); none binds a freight forwarder acting purely as tenant or service provider.

*Analytical inference:* no per-year phased introduction of these standards is stated; C376's obligations take effect in full on gazettal, subject only to the transitional exemption above. No phase-in is stated in Sections 1.0 to 7.0 of Schedule 73 to the Design and Development Overlay.

Obligations surveyed: 18; workspace-adjacent: 16; extracted as FACT: 16.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Analytical inference:* this format section maps poorly onto a municipal planning instrument, since C376 does not regulate a product in the sense a freight-forwarding workspace would track (there is no C376-compliant SKU, material, or piece of equipment). The closest analogue is the workspace's own building stock: whether a workspace-held Melbourne facility falls into the smaller new-building tier or the larger new-building tier (Section 8) determines which specific BESS, Green Star, and NatHERS thresholds would apply to a future planning application on that site.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any current or planned workspace facility in Melbourne meets the new-building or large-addition thresholds that trigger DDO73 obligations requires a site-specific planning assessment, not a determination this brief can make from the general source materials alone.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "Yes, to provide adequate evidence that a development meets the required Green Star Buildings rating, the project must be registered with the Green Building Council of Australia." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

FACT: "A Green Factor scorecard must be submitted as part of the landscape documentation for all relevant development applications." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Operational implication:* registration and scorecard obligations attach to the planning permit application itself, lodged once, at the design/documentation stage; C376 does not create a recurring registration or periodic reporting cycle in the way an emissions-trading or extended-producer-responsibility scheme would.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "You must engage a suitably qualified person to prepare the report demonstrating compliance with the relevant tools." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

*Operational implication:* the only recurring "system" requirement identifiable in the source materials is engaging a suitably qualified ESD/planning consultant at the design stage of a relevant project; C376 does not require the workspace to build or maintain an ongoing monitoring, verification, or reporting system of its own once a permit is issued, unlike a scheme with post-occupancy compliance obligations.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This does not apply to the requirement at Table 6 where it can be demonstrated to the satisfaction of the responsible authority: • That the use of the Green Factor Tool is not practical." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "Adding a transitional provision to exempt the requirements of DDO73 from an application made before the commencement of Amendment C376." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

*Analytical inference:* the Table 6 exemption is narrow (it applies only to the Urban Ecology/Green Factor standard, on a case-by-case practicality test), and the transitional provision protects only applications already lodged before C376's commencement; neither is a general carve-out a workspace could rely on for a genuinely new post-gazettal project.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "this was ultimately gazetted in Amendment GC81." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "Ministerial amendment VC216 was gazetted." *Source: Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024. https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf

FACT: "Invested $17.1 million of Clean Energy Finance Corporation funds in energy efficiency and renewable energy, including 2244 solar panels installed and 11,816 street lights." *Source: Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design, Amendment Overview, Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/amendment-overview

*Analytical inference:* C376 sits inside a sequence of prior Victorian and Melbourne sustainability instruments (Amendment GC81's mandatory Green Star requirement, the state-level VC216 policy amendment); a workspace tracking Melbourne building-sustainability regulation should treat C376 as the latest, municipality-specific layer on top of that existing state policy, not a standalone scheme.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 15 September 2020: Future Melbourne Committee endorsed draft Amendment C376 and resolved to request Ministerial authorisation to prepare and exhibit the amendment.
- 25 October 2022: authorisation received from the Minister for Planning to prepare and exhibit the amendment.
- 2 March to 17 April 2023: community consultation (public exhibition) period.
- 21 May 2024: Future Melbourne Committee considered all submissions and referred them to an independent Planning Panel.
- 18 October 2024: Planning Panel Report completed and issued.
- 15 July 2025: Future Melbourne Committee considered the Panel Report and recommended Council adopt Amendment C376.
- 29 July 2025: Amendment C376 unanimously adopted by Council.

*Source for timeline entries: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne (https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me); Melbourne Planning Scheme Amendment C376melb, Panel Report, Planning Panels Victoria, 18 October 2024 (https://hdp-au-prod-app-com-participate-files.s3.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com/3517/3034/0868/Melbourne_C376melb_Panel_Report.pdf).*

FACT: "Council endorsed draft Amendment C376 to the Melbourne Planning Scheme and resolved to request authorisation from the Minister for Planning to prepare and exhibit the amendment." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "Authorisation received to proceed 25 October 2022" *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "Community consultation 2 March to 17 April 2023" *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "On 21 May 2024, Council’s Future Melbourne Committee considered all submissions and referred them to an independent planning panel for review." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "The Planning Panel completed its report (PDF 2660 KB) on 18 October 2024." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "The Future Melbourne Committee met on 15 July 2025 and recommended that Council adopt s Amendment C376" *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

FACT: "Amendment C376 was unanimously adopted by Council at the 29 July 2025 meeting." *Source: How does this affect me? | Amendment C376: Sustainable Building Design | Participate Melbourne. https://participate.melbourne.vic.gov.au/amendment-c376/how-does-this-affect-me

*Operational implication:* gazettal by the Minister for Planning is the one remaining step after adoption and is not yet dated in the source materials; the timeline above records every dated milestone reached to the item's capture date.

metadata.what_is_it: A City of Melbourne planning scheme amendment (DDO73) setting mandatory and preferred environmentally sustainable design standards, BESS/Green Star/NatHERS thresholds, and Green Factor landscape requirements for new buildings and large alterations, adopted by Council on 29 July 2025 and pending Ministerial gazettal.
metadata.why_matters: It is a municipal building-design planning instrument, not a freight-sector regulation; it becomes relevant to a freight forwarder only where the workspace itself develops, owns, or materially alters a building in the City of Melbourne that meets the new-building or large-addition thresholds, since the obligations run to the planning permit applicant, not to a tenant or logistics service provider.
key_data: new buildings up to 5000 sqm must achieve minimum 50 percent BESS score
new buildings over 5000 sqm must achieve 5 Star Green Star Buildings
large alterations and additions over 1000 sqm gross floor area are covered
buildings account for 66 per cent of City of Melbourne carbon emissions
amendment adopted 29 July 2025; Ministerial gazettal still pending
metadata.cost_mechanism: No fee, levy, or fine is stated in the captured source materials; the only enforcement mechanism identified is permit refusal, since a permit cannot be granted to vary a requirement expressed with the term must or a mandatory minimum standard of DDO73 (Schedule 73).
metadata.enforcement_body: City of Melbourne as the responsible planning authority under the Melbourne Planning Scheme; no state or federal enforcement body is named in the captured materials for non-compliance with DDO73 itself.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Executive Order 80 (issued October 29, 2018) and Executive Order 246 (issued January 7, 2022) as they apply to the transportation sector in North Carolina, with particular focus on the freight, fleet, and commercial vehicle dimensions of implementation. Both are gubernatorial directives issued under the authority of the Governor of North Carolina; they bind North Carolina state agencies, not private-sector entities, in the manner of an enacted statute. The document synthesizes across the NC Governor's Office, NCDOT, AFDC, NC DOA, and adjacent industry sources cited in the source pool.

FACT: "On October 29, 2018, Governor Cooper issued Executive Order 80" *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

FACT: "On January 7, 2022, Governor Cooper issued Executive Order 246" *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific provision of EO 80 or EO 246 imposes an enforceable obligation on a private freight operator, carrier, or logistics service provider, as opposed to a state agency, requires legal counsel review.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Governor Cooper issued Executive Order 80 , which directed bold action on climate change and the transition to a clean energy economy." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

FACT: "Executive Order 246 established new goals for North Carolina to: Reduce statewide greenhouse gas emissions by 50% below 2005 levels by by 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2050; and Increase the total number of registered, zero-emission vehicles to at least 1,250,000 by 2030 and increase the sale of zero-emission vehicles so that 50 percent of in-state sales of new vehicles are zero-emission by 2030." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

FACT: "GHG emissions must be at least 50% below 2005 levels by 2030; Achieve net-zero emissions by 2050; Register at least 1,250,000 ZEVs by 2030; and, Increase the share of new passenger vehicle sales to 50% ZEVs by 2030." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

FACT: "The transportation sector represents about 36 percent of all greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in North Carolina." *Source: North Carolina ZEV Plan, 2022 Progress Update, NCDOT. https://www.ncdot.gov/initiatives-policies/environmental/climate-change/Documents/zev-plan-progress-update-2022.pdf

*Operational implication:* workspaces operating commercial vehicle fleets in North Carolina, including road freight carriers, last-mile delivery operators, intermodal drayage providers, and freight forwarders managing client fleets, sit in the trajectory of these directives even though the directives bind state agencies directly rather than private operators. EO 80 and EO 246 have produced downstream instruments (the Clean Transportation Plan, the Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking attempt, and the Multi-State MHD ZEV Memorandum of Understanding) that shape the commercial vehicle equipment and charging-infrastructure market in the state.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* workspaces operating medium- and heavy-duty vehicle fleets in North Carolina should confirm the current legal status of the Advanced Clean Trucks (ACT) rule with NC DEQ before making fleet procurement decisions premised on that framework, since the rulemaking directed under a related executive order has been legislatively blocked.

FACT: "In 2023, the General Assembly prohibited the Department of Environmental Quality from moving forward with Advanced Clean Trucks." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

FACT: "On March 28, 2024, Governor Cooper announced that North Carolina had achieved Executive Order 80’s zero-emission vehicle goals two years early." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

*Analytical inference:* the EO 246 goal of 1,250,000 registered zero-emission vehicles by 2030 remains the active statewide target; the EO 80 goal that was achieved early (80,000 registered ZEVs) was a smaller, earlier-horizon target and its early achievement does not by itself indicate the larger EO 246 target is on pace.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

EO 80 and EO 246 are structured as directives to state agencies, not as statutory obligations on private commercial entities. The compliance chain has two distinct layers.

**Layer 1, direct state agency obligations.** FACT: "State-owned vehicle fleets must prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new vehicles and use ZEVs for agency travel when feasible. Cabinet agencies must prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new medium- and heavy-duty (MHD) vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 8,500 pounds." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**Layer 2, commercial sector market-structure effects.** FACT: "North Carolina established a goal that at least 75% of new or replacement state government light-duty cars and trucks with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less must be AFVs or low emission vehicles." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

*Analytical inference:* a workspace acting as freight carrier or fleet operator in North Carolina is not itself directly obligated by EO 80 or EO 246. Its compliance-chain position is as a commercial market participant affected by the state's downstream regulatory instruments, by client ESG requirements that cite EO 246 targets, and by equipment-availability shifts tied to the (currently blocked) Advanced Clean Trucks framework.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether state transportation procurement contracts will incorporate EO 246 ZEV requirements as contract conditions, and whether private carriers delivering to state facilities face fleet-composition requirements as a downstream consequence, requires legal counsel review.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The N.C. Clean Transportation Plan is a guidance document that provides a coordinated strategy for accelerating decarbonization in the transportation sector. The plan outlines how North Carolina can prepare for a clean transportation future and provide equitable outcomes for everyone." *Source: N.C. Clean Transportation Plan, NCDOT. https://www.ncdot.gov/initiatives-policies/environmental/climate-change/Pages/clean-transportation-plan.aspx

FACT: "Enacted: Jan 7, 2022 Technologies: EVs, Hydrogen Fuel Cells" *Source: Clean Transportation Plan entry, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/12830

FACT: "Section 7 of EO 80 directs cabinet agencies to “prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new vehicles and shall use ZEVs for agency business travel when feasible.”" *Source: North Carolina ZEV Plan, 2022 Progress Update, NCDOT. https://www.ncdot.gov/initiatives-policies/environmental/climate-change/Documents/zev-plan-progress-update-2022.pdf

*Operational implication:* Section 7 of EO 80 is the direct-textual authority for the state-fleet ZEV prioritization requirement summarized in Section 4 above; the NC Motor Fleet ZEV Plan it directs is the operational instrument the Department of Administration produces to carry that section out.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "On October 25, 2022, Governor Cooper signed EO 271, which directs the North Carolina Department of Environmental Quality to propose that the Environmental Management Commission adopt an Advanced Clean Trucks (ACT) program to ensure the mass deployment of ZE trucks and buses in the state." *Source: 2024 North Carolina EV Policy Landscape, Electrification Coalition. https://electrificationcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/2024-North-Carolina-EV-Policy-Landscape.pdf

*Operational implication:* EO 271 (October 25, 2022) directed DEQ to propose the Advanced Clean Trucks rule; that rulemaking is currently blocked (Section 3), so the FY2027 to FY2035 sales-share requirements it would have introduced are not in force. A workspace should re-check DEQ's rulemaking status each NC General Assembly session rather than assume the rule remains dormant indefinitely.

FACT: "The rule is proposed to be in effect from 2027 through 2035, and to meet its requirements, NCDOT anticipates needing 25,000 Level 2 and 30,000 DC fast chargers by 2030, and 100,000 Level 2 and 60,000 DC fast chargers by 2035." *Source: North Carolina's Electric Transportation Transition, Advanced Energy. https://www.advancedenergy.org/news/north-carolinas-electric-transportation-transition.*

*Analytical inference:* the infrastructure buildout figures above describe what the ACT rule's implementation would have required; they are a planning reference for the scale of MHD charging infrastructure the state's own analysis anticipated, not a currently binding requirement.

FACT: "Thirteen applications were selected for full or partial funding by the program selection committee in June 2025." *Source: 2025 Climate Strategy Report, NC Department of Environmental Quality. https://www.deq.nc.gov/ncdeq-climate-strategy-report-2025/open

FACT: "however, some communities needed more time to finalize their engineering and design plans, extending the completion date to September 2023." *Source: 2025 Climate Strategy Report, NC Department of Environmental Quality. https://www.deq.nc.gov/ncdeq-climate-strategy-report-2025/open

*Operational implication:* these Volkswagen Settlement and coastal resilience grant milestones are not obligations on the workspace; they are near-term signals of where DEQ-administered EV-infrastructure and resilience funding is landing, relevant to a workspace evaluating North Carolina depot-charging siting or facility resilience.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Do EO 80 and EO 246 directly impose obligations on private commercial freight operators?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the executive orders are directed at state agencies; private-sector implications flow through downstream regulatory instruments (the ACT rulemaking attempt, NEVI-related deployment, and the Multi-State MHD ZEV Memorandum of Understanding), not through the EOs themselves.

**Q2: Is the Advanced Clean Trucks rule in force in North Carolina?**

FACT: "In 2023, the General Assembly prohibited the Department of Environmental Quality from moving forward with Advanced Clean Trucks." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

*Analytical inference:* the rule is not in force as of this brief's own source pool.

**Q3: Are the 1,250,000-ZEV and 50%-new-vehicle-sales EO 246 targets legally binding on private parties?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* these are stated as statewide goals in EO 246; their enforceability against private market actors, as distinct from state agencies, requires legal counsel review.

**Q4: Does the EV annual registration fee apply to commercially registered ZEVs?**

FACT: "The owner of an EV that is exclusively powered by electricity must pay a fee of $214.50 and the owner of a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle must pay a fee of $107.25 in addition to any other required registration fees at the time of initial registration and annual registration renewal." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether this fee applies to commercially registered fleet vehicles requires DMV confirmation.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: EO 80 and EO 246 are gubernatorial directives that bind North Carolina state agencies, not statutes carrying private-party civil or criminal penalties. "Substantive requirements" below states the EOs' own obligations on state agencies (the bound parties under North Carolina law) plus the operational consequences those obligations carry for a freight forwarder as a market participant, and states plainly where no obligation or penalty runs to a private party.*

**1. EO 80 statewide goals (state-agency-directed).** FACT: "Reduce statewide greenhouse gas emissions to 40% below 2005 levels; Increase the number of registered, zero-emission vehicles to at least 80,000; and Reduce energy consumption per square foot in state-owned buildings by at least 40% from fiscal year 2002-2003 levels." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

**2. EO 80 Section 7, state fleet ZEV prioritization (jurisdictional and organizational scope).** FACT: "Section 7 of EO 80 directs cabinet agencies to “prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new vehicles and shall use ZEVs for agency business travel when feasible.”" *Source: North Carolina ZEV Plan, 2022 Progress Update, NCDOT. https://www.ncdot.gov/initiatives-policies/environmental/climate-change/Documents/zev-plan-progress-update-2022.pdf

**3. State-owned fleet ZEV and MHD prioritization.** FACT: "State-owned vehicle fleets must prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new vehicles and use ZEVs for agency travel when feasible. Cabinet agencies must prioritize ZEVs in the purchase or lease of new medium- and heavy-duty (MHD) vehicles with a gross vehicle weight rating greater than 8,500 pounds." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**4. 75% AFV acquisition goal, state government light-duty fleet.** FACT: "North Carolina established a goal that at least 75% of new or replacement state government light-duty cars and trucks with a gross vehicle weight rating of 8,500 pounds or less must be AFVs or low emission vehicles." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**5. Petroleum displacement planning, state-owned fleets.** FACT: "State-owned vehicle fleets must implement petroleum displacement plans to increase the use of alternative fuels and fuel-efficient vehicles." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**6. NC Motor Fleet ZEV Plan content.** FACT: "The Plan identifies the types of trips for which ZEV-use is feasible, recommends infrastructure necessary to support ZEV use, and develops ZEV procurement options and strategies." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**7. EO 246 statewide goals (effective date and primary deadline).** FACT: "Executive Order 246 established new goals for North Carolina to: Reduce statewide greenhouse gas emissions by 50% below 2005 levels by by 2030 and achieve net-zero emissions as soon as possible, but no later than 2050; and Increase the total number of registered, zero-emission vehicles to at least 1,250,000 by 2030 and increase the sale of zero-emission vehicles so that 50 percent of in-state sales of new vehicles are zero-emission by 2030." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

**8. Clean Transportation Plan submission deadline (NCDOT obligation, primary compliance deadline).** FACT: "The North Carolina Department of Transportation (DOT) must develop and submit a state-wide Clean Transportation Plan (Plan) by April 7, 2023" *Source: Clean Transportation Plan entry, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/12830

**9. EV registration tracking and reporting.** FACT: "The North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) will report EV, hybrid electric vehicle, and plug-in hybrid electric vehicle registrations on its performance dashboard." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**10. Multi-State MHD ZEV Memorandum of Understanding.** FACT: "On July 15, 2020, Gov. Cooper joined a bi-partisan group of 15 states and the District of Columbia in signing a Memorandum ​​of Understanding (MOU)" *Source: N.C. Clean Transportation Plan, Transportation Emission Reduction Projects Page, NCDOT. https://www.ncdot.gov/initiatives-policies/environmental/climate-change/Pages/electric-vehicles.aspx

**11. Multi-State MHD ZEV Task Force action plan.** FACT: "In July 2022, the Task Force published a multi-state action plan to support electrification of MHD vehicles." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**12. EV and PHEV annual registration fee (scope limit: private-party cost, not a compliance obligation).** FACT: "The owner of an EV that is exclusively powered by electricity must pay a fee of $214.50 and the owner of a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle must pay a fee of $107.25 in addition to any other required registration fees at the time of initial registration and annual registration renewal." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**13. Alternative-fuel retail sales and use tax exemption (exception, scope limit).** FACT: "The retail sale, use, storage, and consumption of alternative fuels is exempt from the state retail sales and use tax." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**14. Light-duty EV and FCEV emissions inspection exemption (exception).** FACT: "Qualified light-duty EVs and FCEVs are exempt from state emissions inspection requirements." *Source: AFDC Hydrogen Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/HY?state=nc

**15. Charging-station operator public-utility exclusion (exception, conditional).** FACT: "A person who uses electric vehicle supply equipment to resell electricity to the public for the purposes of fueling an electric vehicle is not considered a public utility. Conditions apply." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

**16. Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking, legislatively blocked (the EO-adjacent chain's only enforcement- or consequence-shaped mechanism found in this brief's corpus).** FACT: "In 2023, the General Assembly prohibited the Department of Environmental Quality from moving forward with Advanced Clean Trucks." *Source: Climate, NC Governor's Office. https://governor.nc.gov/issues/climate

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no provision of EO 80 or EO 246 in this brief's own corpus states a fine, civil penalty, or enforcement action running to a state agency for non-compliance, or to any private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary. The only enforcement- or consequence-shaped mechanism found anywhere in this corpus is the General Assembly's 2023 legislative prohibition on DEQ's Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking (obligation 16 above), which originates from Executive Order 271, a related downstream North Carolina climate directive on the same Governor's Office climate page as EO 80 and EO 246, not from EO 80 or EO 246's own text directly. That mechanism runs to a state agency's rulemaking authority (it blocks DEQ, not any private party), and no source in this corpus identifies any penalty applicable to a private-sector entity under EO 80, EO 246, or the blocked ACT rulemaking. Whether the General Assembly's prohibition fully extinguishes DEQ's ACT rulemaking authority or only suspends it pending further legislative action requires legal counsel review.

*Analytical inference:* per-year trajectory is captured above: EO 80 targets a 2025 horizon, EO 246 targets a 2030 horizon (with net-zero by 2050), and the blocked ACT rule would have phased manufacturer ZEV sales shares from 2027 through 2035 (obligation 16 and Section 6); no additional sub-year phase-in schedule beyond these named horizons is stated in this brief's corpus.

No scope limits are stated in Sections 1 to 7 of EO 80 or EO 246, as reflected in this brief's captured source pool.

Obligations surveyed: 16; workspace-adjacent: 16; extracted as FACT: 16.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Analytical inference:* EO 80 and EO 246 are fleet, infrastructure, and emissions-target instruments directed at state agencies; this brief's corpus identifies no product-level compliance standard (equipment certification, labeling, or product design requirement) that applies to a workspace's own products under either order.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The North Carolina Department of Transportation (NCDOT) will report EV, hybrid electric vehicle, and plug-in hybrid electric vehicle registrations on its performance dashboard." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

FACT: "The owner of an EV that is exclusively powered by electricity must pay a fee of $214.50 and the owner of a plug-in hybrid electric vehicle must pay a fee of $107.25 in addition to any other required registration fees at the time of initial registration and annual registration renewal." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

*Operational implication:* the EV and PHEV registration fees apply at initial registration and at annual renewal; a workspace operating a ZEV fleet registered in North Carolina should incorporate this recurring fee line into fleet total-cost-of-ownership planning.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "The Plan identifies the types of trips for which ZEV-use is feasible, recommends infrastructure necessary to support ZEV use, and develops ZEV procurement options and strategies." *Source: AFDC Electricity Laws and Incentives in North Carolina, U.S. Department of Energy AFDC. https://afdc.energy.gov/fuels/laws/ELEC?state=nc

FACT: "The current ZEV fleet assigned to state agencies is 79 vehicles strong and composed of Chevy Bolts, Ford E-Transit Vans and a Ford Lightning." *Source: Zero-Emission Vehicles, NC Department of Administration. https://www.doa.nc.gov/about/sustainability/zero-emission-vehicles

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- October 29, 2018: EO 80 issued; 40% GHG reduction by 2025 and 80,000 registered ZEV goals established.
- September 2019: NCDOT published its Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Plan.
- July 15, 2020: North Carolina joined the Multi-State Medium- and Heavy-Duty ZEV Memorandum of Understanding.
- January 7, 2022: EO 246 issued; 50% GHG reduction by 2030 and net-zero by 2050 goals established, building on EO 80.
- July 2022: the Multi-State MHD ZEV Task Force published its multi-state action plan.
- October 25, 2022: EO 271 issued; DEQ directed to propose the Advanced Clean Trucks rule.
- April 7, 2023: NCDOT's Clean Transportation Plan submission deadline under EO 246.
- 2023: the General Assembly prohibited DEQ from proceeding with Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking.
- June 2025: thirteen Volkswagen Settlement Phase 2 charging-infrastructure applications selected for funding.
- March 28, 2024: Governor Cooper announced EO 80's zero-emission vehicle goal achieved two years early.
- 2030: EO 246 targets due, including 1,250,000 registered ZEVs and 50% zero-emission new vehicle sales.
- 2050: EO 246 net-zero emissions target.

metadata.what_is_it: North Carolina Executive Order 80 (2018) and Executive Order 246 (2022), gubernatorial directives that bind state agencies to statewide greenhouse gas reduction and zero-emission vehicle targets, plus their downstream instruments including the Clean Transportation Plan and the legislatively blocked Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking.
metadata.why_matters: The EOs bind North Carolina state agencies, not private freight operators directly, but they drive downstream instruments (Clean Transportation Plan, ACT rulemaking attempt, Multi-State MHD ZEV MOU) that shape commercial vehicle availability, charging infrastructure buildout, and client ESG reporting expectations on North Carolina freight lanes.
key_data: EO 80 target 40 percent GHG reduction below 2005 levels and 80000 registered ZEVs by 2025
EO 246 target 50 percent GHG reduction below 2005 levels and 1250000 registered ZEVs by 2030
EO 246 net-zero emissions target no later than 2050
EV annual registration fee 214.50 dollars; PHEV annual registration fee 107.25 dollars
transportation sector about 36 percent of North Carolina GHG emissions
metadata.cost_mechanism: No compliance-cost mechanism runs to a private freight operator under EO 80 or EO 246 directly; the EV and PHEV annual registration fees are a fixed per-vehicle state cost applying at initial registration and renewal, and the blocked Advanced Clean Trucks rule would have imposed manufacturer sales-share requirements, not a per-shipment or per-operator cost.

steps.label: 40 percent GHG reduction and 80000 registered ZEV goals for 2025
50 percent GHG reduction and 1250000 registered ZEV goals for 2030, building on EO 80
General Assembly prohibited DEQ from proceeding with Advanced Clean Trucks
50 percent GHG reduction, 1250000 registered ZEVs, 50 percent new ZEV sales
net-zero statewide emissions as soon as possible, no later than 2050

requirement_trajectory.note: no penalty-bearing per-year phase-in schedule is stated for either EO; the blocked ACT rule's own 2027-2035 manufacturer sales-share phase-in is not currently in force

metadata.penalty_range: no penalty running to a private party is stated in this corpus for EO 80 or EO 246; the only enforcement- or consequence-shaped mechanism found is the General Assembly's 2023 legislative prohibition blocking DEQ's Advanced Clean Trucks rulemaking, which runs to that state agency's rulemaking authority, not to a private freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics intermediary
metadata.enforcement_body: the Governor's Office and NCDOT administer EO 80 and EO 246 as directives to state agencies; no source in this corpus identifies an enforcement body acting against a private-sector entity under either order
