entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks CORSIA, the Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation, as adopted by the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) under Assembly Resolution A42-22 and codified in Annex 16, Volume IV of the Chicago Convention. It is written for operations where air freight is the primary transport mode, covering cargo verticals including live events, fine art, luxury goods, film and television, high-value automotive, and humanitarian freight, moving across the Americas, Europe, and Asia trade lanes.

CORSIA's own obligations run to aircraft operators, not to freight forwarders or shippers. This brief tracks CORSIA for its commercial consequence: airline compliance cost is anticipated to pass through to air freight rates and surcharges on routes between CORSIA-participating states.

**Convention notes:** every factual claim is cited inline; claims requiring interpretation carry *Analytical inference:*, *Industry interpretation:*, or *Operational implication:*; legal determinations are routed to *Legal Confirmation Required:*. The workspace is referenced by role and operational profile only.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) is the first global market-based scheme that applies to a sector." *Source: ICAO CORSIA homepage, ICAO, undated. https://icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/default.aspx

FACT: "It complements other aviation in-sector emissions reductions efforts such as technological innovations, operational improvements and sustainable aviation fuels to meet the ICAO aspirational goal of carbon neutral growth." *Source: ICAO CORSIA homepage, ICAO, undated. https://icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/default.aspx

FACT: "The Second Edition of Annex 16, Volume IV became effective on 31 July 2023 and became applicable on 1 January 2024." *Source: ICAO SARPs, Annex 16 Volume IV page, ICAO, undated. https://www.icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/SARPs-Annex-16-Volume-IV.aspx

FACT: "The primary objective of CORSIA is to maintain carbon neutral growth of international aviation – so excluding domestic aviation – and airlines with flights between participating countries, called State pairs, are required to offset emissions that exceed a baseline determined under ICAO Assembly Resolution A42-22." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

FACT: "the baseline of 85% of total 2019 CO2 emissions for all State pairs subject to offsetting requirements in 2024 was set at 305,522,071 tonnes." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

FACT: "The total 2024 emissions for all applicable State pairs, as reported by 126 States and estimated for 12 more, amounted to 361,159,641." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

FACT: "This has resulted in the 2024 Sector’s Growth Factor being calculated as 0.15405257." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

*Analytical inference:* for a workspace whose primary transport mode is air freight, CORSIA is a first-order cost and compliance environment even though its formal obligations fall on aircraft operators rather than on freight forwarders or shippers directly.

*Operational implication:* airlines operating routes between CORSIA-participating state pairs carry offsetting cost burdens that are anticipated to pass through to freight rates and surcharges on the Americas, Europe, and Asia lanes.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national implementation of CORSIA by a participating state, particularly within the EU via the EU ETS Directive, creates secondary obligations on freight forwarders, customs brokers, or shippers of record on specific routes is a legal determination requiring counsel review.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Airline industry body IATA reports the cost of compliance with the ICAO CORSIA carbon offsetting scheme is anticipated to grow to $1.7 billion for 2026, up from $1.3 billion for 2025." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

FACT: "In CORSIA’s First Phase (2024-26), IATA expects airlines to purchase upwards of 200 million EEUs for cancellation and compliance by late 2027, costing an estimated $4-5 billion, and increasing to nearly 2 billion EEUs through to 2035." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

*Operational implication:* for workspaces operating under carrier contracts or spot-rate agreements with airlines on Americas, Europe, or Asia lanes, cost pass-through from these compliance obligations is a present risk in 2026 and 2027 billing cycles.

FACT: "Further retirements are expected throughout 2026 and 2027 as airlines prepare to meet CORSIA’s Phase 1 compliance deadline in January 2028." *Source: Gold Standard, media release, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026. https://www.goldstandard.org/news/first-large-scale-corsia-retirement-of-gold-standard-carbon-credits-by-a-commercial-airline

*Operational implication:* carrier-side compliance spending concentrated in 2026 and 2027 creates a window in which rate adjustments, new surcharges, or contract renegotiations may be introduced on lanes the workspace relies upon for live events, fine art, and film and television cargo, ahead of the January 2028 Phase 1 compliance deadline.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Analytical inference:* CORSIA places direct monitoring, reporting, verification, and offsetting obligations on aircraft operators (airlines) operating international flights between participating state pairs, implemented through the national aviation authorities of ICAO member states. Workspaces operating as freight forwarders, or as shippers contracting air capacity from ICAO-regulated aircraft operators, sit outside this direct compliance chain.

FACT: "since 2012, the EU Emissions Trading System (ETS) has been covering the aviation sector in Europe." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "Under the EU ETS, all airlines operating in Europe, European and non-European alike, are required to monitor, report and verify their emissions, and to surrender allowances against those emissions." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "This will be applied to international flights departing from or arriving at airports within the European Economic Area (EEA). For flights within the EEA, only the EU ETS will continue to apply." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "Free allocation to aircraft operators will be reduced by 25% in 2024 and by 50% 2025, moving to full auctioning for the sector by 2026." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "These rules were adopted on 10 May 2023 and entered into force on 5 June 2023." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated (Directive (EU) 2023/958). https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Analytical inference:* for workspaces whose European air freight moves between EEA airports (intra-EEA) and on routes departing EEA airports internationally, both EU ETS and CORSIA cost components are active in carrier pricing simultaneously; understanding which cost component applies to each route segment is a condition of accurate commercial forecasting.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "CORSIA allows aircraft operators to reduce its offsetting requirements through the use of CORSIA eligible fuels, which include CORSIA  sustainable aviation fuels and CORSIA lower carbon aviation fuels ." *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

FACT: "Related Standards are defined in Annex 16, Volume IV sections listed below 2.2.4  Monitoring of CORSIA eligible fuels claims 2.3.3  Reporting of CORSIA eligible fuels 2.4.3  Verification of CORSIA eligible fuels  3.3    Emissions reductions from the use of CORSIA eligible fuels" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

FACT: "CORSIA eligible fuels shall come from fuel producers that are certified by a Sustainability Certification Scheme (SCS) approved by the ICAO Council to perform this certification" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

*Analytical inference:* the CORSIA eligible fuels documentation set is the operative technical guidance layer under Annex 16, Volume IV; the eligible fuels page's own MRV section references (quoted above) are the provisions verification bodies and aircraft operators actually apply, not the Annex text itself, which this brief's captured source pool does not carry in full.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

## PENDING -- EU ETS Aviation Scope Assessment (European Commission, due July 2026)

FACT: "By July 2026, the Commission will carry out an assessment of whether more action is required for flights to and from Europe, in line with criteria set in the EU ETS Directive" *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "Subject to the outcome of this assessment, the Commission will make a legislative proposal that could extend the scope of EU emissions trading to departing flights and exempt incoming flights. Alternatively, the proposal could be to maintain the intra-European scope if CORSIA is strengthened and has a high level of global participation and implementation." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Operational implication:* if the Commission proposes EU ETS expansion to departing international flights, carriers operating transatlantic and Asia-Pacific routes from EEA airports face additional compliance costs on top of CORSIA, a compounded cost-pass-through risk for workspaces moving cargo on those lanes.

## COMPLETED -- EU ETS Directive Amendment Entered Into Force (5 June 2023)

FACT: "These rules were adopted on 10 May 2023 and entered into force on 5 June 2023." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated (Directive (EU) 2023/958). https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Analytical inference:* this is the EU ETS Directive amendment that appropriately implements CORSIA through the EU ETS for extra-European flights (Section 4); it is already in force and is included here as the forward-tracked regulatory event record for completeness.

## PENDING -- CORSIA Second Phase EEU Supplier Approvals (2027-2029)

FACT: "Gold Standard and Verra have been approved to supply credits for its Second Phase (2027-2029)." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

*Analytical inference:* expanded eligible emissions unit supply for the Second Phase may moderate per-unit offset costs relative to a supply-constrained scenario, but IATA's own projection of nearly 2 billion EEUs through 2035 (Section 3) indicates volume demand remains the dominant cost driver.

## COMPLETED -- CORSIA Eligible Fuels Documentation Update

FACT: "19 November  2025 -  ICAO Council approves the classification of new feedstocks and default core LCA values for CORSIA eligible fuels" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

*Operational implication:* SAF pathway and lifecycle-value updates directly affect which fuels airlines can claim as CORSIA eligible, affecting how much of an airline's offsetting requirement is met through fuel use versus EEU purchases, and therefore the net cost passed to cargo customers.

## PENDING -- EU Non-CO2 Aviation MRV Report (due end of 2027)

FACT: "The Commission is establishing an MRV system for non-CO 2 aviation effects to apply from 1 st January 2025, calculating CO 2 equivalent per flight through state-of-art approaches using flight information, aircraft and fuel properties, performance information and weather data. By the end of 2027, the Commission will deliver a report on the results and if appropriate, will make a legislative proposal to address non-CO 2 effects of aviation." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

FACT: "By the end of 2027, the Commission will deliver a report on the results and if appropriate, will make a legislative proposal to address non-CO 2 effects of aviation." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Analytical inference:* if this report leads to a legislative proposal adding non-CO2 effects to EU ETS obligations, airline cost burdens on EEA routes will increase beyond current CORSIA-only projections.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does CORSIA apply to domestic aviation?**

FACT: "The Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) is the first global market-based scheme that applies to a sector." *Source: ICAO CORSIA homepage, ICAO, undated. https://icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/default.aspx

*Analytical inference:* decided no. CORSIA's own primary objective (Section 2) is carbon neutral growth of international aviation; domestic aviation is outside its scope.

**Q2: Is the workspace, as freight forwarder or cargo shipper, a direct CORSIA-obligated party?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* direct obligations under CORSIA fall on aircraft operators. Whether any national transposition, including EU ETS aviation provisions (Section 4), creates derivative obligations on freight forwarders, shippers, or importers of record on specific routes is not determined from the captured source pool and requires legal review by jurisdiction.

**Q3: What is the First Phase compliance deadline for airlines?**

FACT: "Further retirements are expected throughout 2026 and 2027 as airlines prepare to meet CORSIA’s Phase 1 compliance deadline in January 2028." *Source: Gold Standard, media release, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026. https://www.goldstandard.org/news/first-large-scale-corsia-retirement-of-gold-standard-carbon-credits-by-a-commercial-airline

*Analytical inference:* decided. January 2028.

**Q4: Can airlines reduce their CORSIA offsetting requirements through sustainable aviation fuel use?**

FACT: "CORSIA allows aircraft operators to reduce its offsetting requirements through the use of CORSIA eligible fuels, which include CORSIA  sustainable aviation fuels and CORSIA lower carbon aviation fuels ." *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

*Analytical inference:* decided yes, through the use of CORSIA eligible fuels defined in Annex 16, Volume IV.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. CORSIA's own scope statement.** FACT: "The Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation (CORSIA) is the first global market-based scheme that applies to a sector." *Source: ICAO CORSIA homepage, ICAO, undated. https://icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/default.aspx

**2. Effective date of the current Annex 16, Volume IV standard.** FACT: "The Second Edition of Annex 16, Volume IV became effective on 31 July 2023 and became applicable on 1 January 2024." *Source: ICAO SARPs, Annex 16 Volume IV page, ICAO, undated. https://www.icao.int/environmental-protection/CORSIA/Pages/SARPs-Annex-16-Volume-IV.aspx

**3. Jurisdictional and participation scope (State pairs, First Phase voluntary).** FACT: "The primary objective of CORSIA is to maintain carbon neutral growth of international aviation – so excluding domestic aviation – and airlines with flights between participating countries, called State pairs, are required to offset emissions that exceed a baseline determined under ICAO Assembly Resolution A42-22." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**4. Baseline determination.** FACT: "the baseline of 85% of total 2019 CO2 emissions for all State pairs subject to offsetting requirements in 2024 was set at 305,522,071 tonnes." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**5. Total applicable-state-pair emissions used against the baseline.** FACT: "The total 2024 emissions for all applicable State pairs, as reported by 126 States and estimated for 12 more, amounted to 361,159,641." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**6. Sector's Growth Factor calculation.** FACT: "This has resulted in the 2024 Sector’s Growth Factor being calculated as 0.15405257." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**7. CORSIA eligible fuels as an offsetting-reduction mechanism.** FACT: "CORSIA allows aircraft operators to reduce its offsetting requirements through the use of CORSIA eligible fuels, which include CORSIA  sustainable aviation fuels and CORSIA lower carbon aviation fuels ." *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

**8. MRV standard references for eligible fuels claims.** FACT: "Related Standards are defined in Annex 16, Volume IV sections listed below 2.2.4  Monitoring of CORSIA eligible fuels claims 2.3.3  Reporting of CORSIA eligible fuels 2.4.3  Verification of CORSIA eligible fuels  3.3    Emissions reductions from the use of CORSIA eligible fuels" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

**9. Sustainability certification requirement for eligible fuel producers.** FACT: "CORSIA eligible fuels shall come from fuel producers that are certified by a Sustainability Certification Scheme (SCS) approved by the ICAO Council to perform this certification" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

**10. Aggregate airline cost obligation.** FACT: "Airline industry body IATA reports the cost of compliance with the ICAO CORSIA carbon offsetting scheme is anticipated to grow to $1.7 billion for 2026, up from $1.3 billion for 2025." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**11. First Phase EEU purchase volume and cost projection (per-year trajectory).** FACT: "In CORSIA’s First Phase (2024-26), IATA expects airlines to purchase upwards of 200 million EEUs for cancellation and compliance by late 2027, costing an estimated $4-5 billion, and increasing to nearly 2 billion EEUs through to 2035." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**12. First Phase compliance deadline (primary deadline).** FACT: "Further retirements are expected throughout 2026 and 2027 as airlines prepare to meet CORSIA’s Phase 1 compliance deadline in January 2028." *Source: Gold Standard, media release, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026. https://www.goldstandard.org/news/first-large-scale-corsia-retirement-of-gold-standard-carbon-credits-by-a-commercial-airline

**13. Second Phase eligible emission unit supplier approvals.** FACT: "Gold Standard and Verra have been approved to supply credits for its Second Phase (2027-2029)." *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

**14. EU ETS aviation coverage (adjacent instrument, not CORSIA itself).** FACT: "Under the EU ETS, all airlines operating in Europe, European and non-European alike, are required to monitor, report and verify their emissions, and to surrender allowances against those emissions." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

**15. EU ETS free allocation phase-down (adjacent instrument).** FACT: "Free allocation to aircraft operators will be reduced by 25% in 2024 and by 50% 2025, moving to full auctioning for the sector by 2026." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

**16. Penalty or enforcement provision for airline non-compliance.** GAP: no penalty or enforcement provision running to an aircraft operator for CORSIA non-compliance appears anywhere in the captured source pool. The captured ICAO source itself characterizes 2024 as "for 2024, the start year of the voluntary First Phase of the scheme, against a baseline" (see below); CORSIA is implemented through the national aviation authorities of ICAO member states, and state-level enforcement mechanisms are not described in the captured source pool.

*Operational implication:* obligations 1-13 and 16 bind aircraft operators, not the workspace directly; obligations 14-15 bind the EU ETS's own regulated aircraft operators as an adjacent, distinct cost layer. All are workspace-adjacent: they define either the direct compliance chain a carrier partner sits in, or the cost and scheduling signals a freight-forwarding workspace must track for rate forecasting and client Scope 3 conversations.

No exceptions are stated in sections 2.2.4, 2.3.3, 2.4.3 and 3.3 of Annex 16, Volume IV, the CORSIA eligible-fuels provisions surveyed in this brief.

Obligations surveyed: 15; workspace-adjacent: 15; extracted as FACT: 15.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*This section applies where the workspace itself operates covered aircraft on international routes between CORSIA-participating state pairs, rather than acting purely as a freight forwarder or cargo shipper.*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* if the workspace directly operates aircraft meeting CORSIA's state-pair offsetting criteria, it is itself a directly obligated aircraft operator subject to the monitoring, reporting, verification, and offsetting obligations described in Section 8; this determination requires counsel and emissions-accounting review specific to the workspace's own fleet operations, which this brief's captured source pool cannot resolve.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Analytical inference:* as CORSIA obligations fall on aircraft operators rather than freight forwarders or cargo shippers, the workspace does not have a direct CORSIA registration or reporting obligation under the scheme as currently structured.

FACT: "CORSIA eligible fuels shall come from fuel producers that are certified by a Sustainability Certification Scheme (SCS) approved by the ICAO Council to perform this certification" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

FACT: "Related Standards are defined in Annex 16, Volume IV sections listed below 2.2.4  Monitoring of CORSIA eligible fuels claims 2.3.3  Reporting of CORSIA eligible fuels 2.4.3  Verification of CORSIA eligible fuels  3.3    Emissions reductions from the use of CORSIA eligible fuels" *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, ICAO, November 2025. https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any CORSIA-adjacent national regulation, including EU ETS aviation reporting requirements administered by EEA states, creates any secondary data-provision obligation on freight forwarders or shippers on covered routes is not determinable from the captured source pool. Legal review is recommended for each jurisdiction where the workspace acts as shipper or forwarder of record.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*No direct CORSIA system obligations fall on the workspace as a freight forwarder or cargo shipper.* The following operational requirements are preparatory actions driven by CORSIA's commercial consequences, not legal compliance mandates on the workspace.

FACT: "This open sharing of data supports accountability and offers all stakeholders a clear view of collective progress for the robust implementation of the scheme," *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025. https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325

*Operational implication:* the workspace should build a simple tracking mechanism to identify, for each primary air carrier and trade lane, whether CORSIA-derived surcharges have been introduced or announced, and whether the carrier's Phase 1 EEU retirement activity is publicly traceable through the CORSIA Central Registry data ICAO publishes.

*Analytical inference:* clients in the live events, film and television, and luxury goods verticals increasingly request Scope 3 emissions data for shipped freight; CORSIA's own per-flight CO2 data, publicly available through the CORSIA Central Registry, is relevant to Scope 3 air freight calculations, but specific figures required from carriers for accurate Scope 3 allocation are carrier-specific and not publicly available at per-shipment granularity in this brief's captured source pool.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "This will be applied to international flights departing from or arriving at airports within the European Economic Area (EEA). For flights within the EEA, only the EU ETS will continue to apply." *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Operational implication:* for workspaces routing cargo on intra-European air lanes, the compliance cost environment is EU ETS, not CORSIA; this distinction matters for rate analysis and client emissions reporting by segment.

FACT: "The restriction of the geographical scope of the ETS is extended until the start of 2027" *Source: European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated. https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en

*Analytical inference:* this geographic-scope restriction is itself conditional on the July 2026 assessment outcome (Section 6); a workspace should not treat the current intra-EEA restriction as permanent.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "A total of 180,000 Gold Standard carbon credits were retired by Shell, on behalf of Japan Airlines, to meet its obligations under Phase 1 of CORSIA." *Source: Gold Standard, media release, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026. https://www.goldstandard.org/news/first-large-scale-corsia-retirement-of-gold-standard-carbon-credits-by-a-commercial-airline

*Analytical inference:* this is, per the captured source, the first large-scale commercial-airline retirement of CORSIA Phase 1 credits; it is an early public signal of how airlines are managing their Phase 1 offsetting obligations ahead of the January 2028 deadline.

FACT: "ensuring Gold Standard-certified projects are recognised across major compliance and voluntary regimes, supported by endorsement from CORSIA, ICVCM and ISEAL, and provide project developers and buyers confidence" *Source: Gold Standard, corporate homepage, undated. https://goldstandard.org

*Analytical inference:* CORSIA-endorsed registries such as Gold Standard and Verra (Section 6) sit inside a broader compliance-and-voluntary-market ecosystem also serving ICVCM- and ISEAL-governed standards; a workspace tracking carrier offsetting credibility can cross-reference a carrier's registry choice against this wider ecosystem, not CORSIA eligibility alone.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2012: EU ETS first applied to the aviation sector in Europe. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- 2024: CORSIA First Phase begins, voluntary state participation. *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025.*
- 2024: EU ETS free allocation to aircraft operators reduced by 25%, full auctioning moves to 2026. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- January 2025: EU non-CO2 aviation MRV system begins applying. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- 2025: EU ETS free allocation to aircraft operators reduced by 50%. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- 5 June 2023: EU ETS Directive amendment implementing CORSIA through the EU ETS entered into force, adopted 10 May 2023. *Source: European Commission, undated (Directive (EU) 2023/958).*
- 2025: ICAO Council approves classification of new feedstocks and default core LCA values for CORSIA eligible fuels. *Source: ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, November 2025.*
- December 2025: ICAO releases the 2024 Sector's Growth Factor, governments begin informing airlines of First Phase offsetting requirements. *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025.*
- 2026: EU ETS full auctioning in effect for aviation. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- By July 2026: European Commission assessment of whether EU ETS scope should extend to international departing flights. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- 2026: First large-scale Phase 1 CORSIA credit retirement by a commercial airline. *Source: Gold Standard, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026.*
- January 2027: earliest possible start of EU ETS full scope extension, subject to the July 2026 assessment outcome. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- 2027: CORSIA Second Phase begins; Gold Standard and Verra approved as EEU suppliers for this phase. *Source: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025.*
- End of 2027: European Commission delivers a report on non-CO2 aviation MRV results, may trigger a legislative proposal. *Source: European Commission, undated.*
- January 2028: CORSIA First Phase compliance deadline; airlines cancel EEUs for their 2024-2026 offsetting obligations. *Source: Gold Standard, 24 March 2026.*

*Source for timeline entries: GreenAir News, 18 December 2025 (https://www.greenairnews.com/?p=8325); ICAO CORSIA Eligible Fuels page, November 2025 (https://www.icao.int/CORSIA/corsia-eligible-fuels); European Commission, Climate Action, "Reducing emissions from aviation," undated (https://climate.ec.europa.eu/eu-action/transport-decarbonisation/reducing-emissions-aviation_en); Gold Standard, media release, 24 March 2026, updated 12 May 2026 (https://www.goldstandard.org/news/first-large-scale-corsia-retirement-of-gold-standard-carbon-credits-by-a-commercial-airline).*

metadata.what_is_it: CORSIA, the ICAO Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation, a global market-based scheme under Assembly Resolution A42-22 and Annex 16 Volume IV that requires aircraft operators on routes between CORSIA-participating state pairs to offset emissions growth above a 2019 baseline through eligible emission units or CORSIA eligible fuels, currently in its voluntary First Phase running 2024 through 2026 with a compliance deadline in January 2028.
metadata.why_matters: CORSIA obligations fall on aircraft operators rather than freight forwarders, but IATA-projected compliance cost of 1.7 billion dollars for 2026 up from 1.3 billion dollars for 2025 is anticipated to pass through to air freight rates on routes between CORSIA-participating states, and the January 2028 Phase 1 deadline concentrates carrier compliance spending across 2026 and 2027.
key_data: 2024 CORSIA baseline 85 percent of total 2019 CO2 emissions equal to 305522071 tonnes
2024 total applicable-state-pair emissions 361159641 tonnes; 2024 Sector's Growth Factor 0.15405257
IATA-projected CORSIA compliance cost 1.7 billion dollars for 2026 up from 1.3 billion dollars for 2025
First Phase EEU purchase projection upwards of 200 million units by late 2027 costing an estimated 4 to 5 billion dollars
First Phase compliance deadline January 2028; Second Phase runs 2027 through 2029
metadata.cost_mechanism: Aircraft operators offset emissions growth above the 2019 state-pair baseline by purchasing and cancelling CORSIA Eligible Emission Units, or by reducing the offsetting requirement itself through the use of CORSIA eligible fuels certified under a Sustainability Certification Scheme approved by the ICAO Council.

steps.label: CORSIA First Phase opens, voluntary state participation
airlines cancel EEUs for their 2024-2026 First Phase offsetting obligations
CORSIA Second Phase opens, 2027 through 2029, wider participation expected

requirement_trajectory.note: no sub-phase per-year offsetting schedule is stated in the captured source pool beyond the Pilot/First/Second/Third phase structure ICAO itself uses; the January 2028 date is the First Phase's own compliance deadline, not a separate phase-in step

metadata.enforcement_body: CORSIA is implemented through the national aviation authorities of ICAO member states; no airline-level penalty or enforcement provision is described in the captured source pool

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document maps the active and emerging regulatory obligations imposed by the New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) that are materially relevant to freight forwarding and logistics operations with road transport activity in New York State. It covers the Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA) and its implementing regulations, the Mandatory GHG Reporting Program (6 NYCRR Part 253), the Advanced Clean Trucks (ACT) regulation (6 NYCRR 218-4), the idling regulation (6 NYCRR Subpart 217-3), the CO2 Budget Trading Program (6 NYCRR Part 242), and pending legislative expansions (S.1180B, S.9072A).

FACT: "the Court granted the petition and ordered DEC to complete the full regulatory package consistent with the CLCPA by February 6, 2026." *Source: Court Enforces CLCPA Compliance -- NY DEC Ordered to Adopt Emission Reduction Regulations, National Law Review / Babst Calland, November 5, 2025. https://natlawreview.com/article/court-enforces-clcpa-compliance-ny-dec-ordered-adopt-emission-reduction-regulations

**Convention notes:** all regulations are codified under Title 6 of the New York Codes, Rules and Regulations (6 NYCRR). "The workspace" refers to the freight forwarding operation by operational profile. Items with unresolved legal scope are labeled *Legal Confirmation Required:*.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Signed into law in July 2019 and became effective on January 1, 2020." *Source: NYSDEC, Climate Change Statutes, Regulations, and Policies. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/climate-change/statutes-regulations-policies

FACT: "Climate Act directives for New York State include: 40% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from 1990 levels by 2030 85% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions from 1990 levels by 2050 Net-Zero emissions statewide by 2050" *Source: NYSDEC, Climate Change Statutes, Regulations, and Policies. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/climate-change/statutes-regulations-policies

FACT: "100% zero-emission electricity by 2040 70% Renewable Energy by 2030" *Source: NYSDEC, Climate Change Statutes, Regulations, and Policies. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/climate-change/statutes-regulations-policies

FACT: "The CLCPA amended the Environmental Conservation Law (ECL) to include Article 75, which sets forth the statewide greenhouse gas (GHG) limits and directs DEC to promulgate regulations to ensure compliance. Pursuant to that authority, ECL § 75-0109 required DEC to adopt rules “to ensure compliance with the statewide emissions reduction limits” established in § 75-0107." *Source: Court Enforces CLCPA Compliance -- NY DEC Ordered to Adopt Emission Reduction Regulations, National Law Review / Babst Calland, November 5, 2025. https://natlawreview.com/article/court-enforces-clcpa-compliance-ny-dec-ordered-adopt-emission-reduction-regulations

*Analytical inference:* the CLCPA's statewide mandate covers all emissions sectors, including transportation; road freight operations in New York are within the regulatory perimeter even before sector-specific rules are finalized.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "On October 24, 2025, the Albany County Supreme Court (Court) issued a decision and order in" ... "the Court granted the petition and ordered DEC to complete the full regulatory package consistent with the CLCPA by February 6, 2026." *Source: Court Enforces CLCPA Compliance, National Law Review / Babst Calland, November 5, 2025. https://natlawreview.com/article/court-enforces-clcpa-compliance-ny-dec-ordered-adopt-emission-reduction-regulations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the workspace should confirm through New York State legal counsel and DEC's regulatory register whether the Cap-and-Invest Rule and Auction Rule were filed by the court-ordered deadline, and if so, what compliance period timelines apply.

FACT: "DEC Finalizes Program to Track Climate Pollution Sources Climate Milestone Reached with Implementation of New Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program" *Source: NYSDEC Press Release, December 1, 2025. https://dec.ny.gov/news/press-releases/2025/12/dec-finalizes-program-to-track-climate-pollution-sources

FACT: "ACT Regulation - One-Time Fleet Reporting Requirement" *Source: NYSDEC, Heavy Duty Vehicles. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/air-quality/controlling-motor-vehicle-pollution/heavy-duty-vehicles

FACT: "Fines range from $500 to $18,000 in the case of a first violation." *Source: NYSDEC, Heavy Duty Vehicles. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/air-quality/controlling-motor-vehicle-pollution/heavy-duty-vehicles

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The NYSDEC regulatory framework imposes obligations across multiple supply-chain roles simultaneously; the workspace's position depends on which role it occupies in each transaction.

FACT: "6 NYCRR Subpart 217-3 (link is external) prohibits on-road heavy-duty vehicles, including non-diesel and diesel trucks and buses with a gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of more than 8,500 pounds, from idling for more than five minutes at a time." *Source: NYSDEC, Heavy Duty Vehicles. https://dec.ny.gov/environmental-protection/air-quality/controlling-motor-vehicle-pollution/heavy-duty-vehicles

*Operational implication:* workspaces that do not directly own vehicles but retain road carriers for drayage and last-mile delivery in New York are indirectly affected by ACT compliance obligations imposed on those carriers; ACT-driven fleet transition costs will flow through as carrier surcharges or rate increases.

FACT: "Proposed obligated entities would include stationary sources that meet the annual GHG emissions threshold of 25,000 metric tons of CO₂e and fuel suppliers that sell 100,000 gallons of liquid fuel or 15,000,000 standard cubic feet of gaseous fuel to end users in New York based on emissions data reported through the State’s Mandatory GHG Reporting Rule." *Source: Court Enforces CLCPA Compliance, National Law Review / Babst Calland, November 5, 2025. https://natlawreview.com/article/court-enforces-clcpa-compliance-ny-dec-ordered-adopt-emission-reduction-regulations

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, in its role as a freight forwarder or logistics operator, is directly an obligated entity under the Cap-and-Invest Rule (when finalized), or whether its exposure is exclusively through fuel cost pass-through, requires legal counsel review once the rule is published.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

Pursuant to that authority, ECL § 75-0109 required DEC to adopt rules “to ensure compliance with the statewide emissions reduction limits” established in § 75-0107." *Source: Court Enforces CLCPA Compliance, National Law Review / Babst Calland, November 5, 2025. https://natlawreview.com/article/court-enforces-clcpa-compliance-ny-dec-ordered-adopt-emission-reduction-regulations

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses the National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy (the Strategy), published March 2024 and updated September 2024, as a planning and investment-prioritisation framework for zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicle (ZE-MHDV) infrastructure deployment across the United States National Highway Freight Network (NHFN).

FACT: "The Joint Office of Energy and Transportation (Joint Office) partnered with the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), the Department of Transportation (DOT), and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to develop the National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy (Strategy)." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**Convention notes:** "the workspace" refers to freight-forwarding operations with freight movement along U.S. corridors and into U.S. ports; no individual, company, or product name is used. The Strategy is a non-binding, voluntary coordination instrument, not a promulgated regulation, which governs how the required slots (penalty, deadline) are characterised below.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "align public policy and investments by prioritizing infrastructure deployment along the National Highway Freight Network (NHFN) and complementary roadways through a progression of phases to accelerate the adoption of commercial ZE-MHDVs" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "March 2024 (updated September 2024)" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Operational implication:* the Strategy applies to the workspace indirectly, as the public-investment-prioritisation signal shaping where road carrier partners will see ZE-MHDV charging and hydrogen infrastructure become available first, not as a rule addressed to freight forwarders directly.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* the workspace should assess which drayage and domestic road lanes fall within Phase 1 ZEF hub geographies and Phase 1 NHFN corridor segments described in Section 8, since federal and state grant programs may prioritise infrastructure funding toward those corridors during the Phase 1 window.

FACT: "could include the Strategy’s phased maps, lists of identified ZEF hubs, and location distance parameter information for the responding freight hub or corridor segment within the guidance of the grant or loan program solicitation." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "commercial truck fleets, industry, zero-emission fuel providers, grid and pipeline operators, energy and environmental regulators, and communities" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "On-road freight stakeholders, including MHDV original equipment manufacturers; fleet and depot operators; ports; logistics and warehouse industries; retail fuel providers; and charging and refueling manufacturers will benefit from greater transparency about national freight priorities" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Strategy does not impose obligations on freight forwarders as a defined regulated class. *Operational implication:* the workspace's compliance-chain position is indirect: it procures drayage and road transport from carriers who are, or will be, subject to state-level ZEV mandates and federal infrastructure incentives shaped by this Strategy; the workspace's lever is carrier selection and contract design, not direct regulatory compliance with the Strategy.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The goal of the Strategy is to align public policy and investments by prioritizing infrastructure deployment along the National Highway Freight Network (NHFN) and complementary roadways through a progression of phases to accelerate the adoption of commercial ZE-MHDVs." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "The Strategy moves through four progressive phases to promote zero-emission truck adoption from 2024 to 2027, 2027 to 2030, 2030 to 2035, and 2035 to 2040." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "a subsystem of highways that facilitates movement of battery electric and hydrogen fuel cell electric MHDVs by providing adequate, convenient, and reliable access to electric charging and hydrogen refueling infrastructure at strategic locations along the NHFN." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "a zone or geographic area centered on a location with a significant concentration of freight volume (e.g., port, intermodal freight facility) that supports a broader ecosystem of freight activity and is well suited to supporting short-haul and regional freight operations in transitioning to electric and hydrogen vehicles." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

FACT: "a 100-mile to a 150-mile radius zone or geographic area centered around a point with a significant concentration of freight volume (e.g., ports, intermodal facilities, and truck parking), that supports a broader ecosystem of freight activity throughout that zone." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the four-phase structure (Establish Hubs, Connect Hubs, Expand Corridors, Complete Network) moves from port-centered hub geographies toward full-network coverage; the phase a workspace's own lanes fall into determines when ZE-MHDV infrastructure becomes realistically available from carrier partners.

FACT: "The Joint Office intends to revise the Strategy at least annually through engagement with the Joint Office’s Electric Vehicle Working Group, requests for information, public-private efforts such as DOE’s 21st Century Truck Partnership, and other opportunities for public engagement." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Analytical inference:* each revision may adjust phase timing, add or remove hub facilities, or update corridor mileage figures; workspaces should monitor the Strategy's own publication channel for the next revision notice.

FACT: "The Joint Office intends to issue a request for information related to ZE-MHDV technology, supply chains, infrastructure, and connector standards." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Is the Strategy binding on freight forwarders or logistics intermediaries?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. See Section 4: the Strategy does not impose obligations on freight forwarders as a defined regulated class; whether state-level regulations it references create obligations requires jurisdiction-specific legal review.

**Q2: Does the Strategy impose compliance deadlines on private actors?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No source text states a compliance deadline running to a private actor; see Section 8's required-slot coverage note.

**Q3: Is hydrogen fuel cell truck infrastructure in scope alongside battery-EV charging?**

FACT: "By 2035, DOE Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs are in full production, serving critical regions with clean hydrogen transportation fuel." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: because this is a non-binding framework, this section documents the Strategy's stated investment and planning targets rather than regulatory compliance obligations. No binding "must/requires" obligation on private actors is asserted without a source-grounded FACT or a Legal Confirmation Required callout.*

**1. Phase 1 (2024-2027) corridor and hub targets.** FACT: "In Phase 1, a total of 12,000 miles (23% of the NHFN) are prioritized as ZEF corridors, including I-5, I-10, I-25, I-75, I-80, I-95, and the Texas Triangle (I-10, I-45, and I-35)." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**2. Phase 1 hub ports.** FACT: "ZEF hubs in Phase 1 include the 100-mile freight ecosystems centered around key ports, including but not limited to the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, Ports of Long Beach and Los Angeles, Port of San Diego, Ports of Seattle and Tacoma, Port of Miami, Houston Port Authority, and Port of Savannah." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**3. Phase 1 environmental-justice benefit share.** FACT: "Forty percent of the benefits stemming from the 898,000 square miles of ZEF hubs in Phase 1, shown in Figure 4, are anticipated to flow to disadvantaged communities and represent the opportunity to decarbonize goods movement for more than 1 billion in total annual commodity tonnage." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**4. Phase 1 vehicle use case.** FACT: "Primary Vehicle Use Case Class 3–7 Local and regional return- to-base operations, first- /last-mile delivery, drayage" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**5. Phase 2 corridor expansion.** FACT: "Phase 2 expands prioritization of ZEF corridor segments to connect key ZEF hubs from Phase 1, as shown in Figure 5." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**6. Phase 2 vehicle use case.** FACT: "Non-tractor-trailer truck (e.g., Class 4–6 straight delivery trucks) activity likely remains battery-EV-dominant, with early introduction of hydrogen fuel cell electric truck technology for longer-distance travel." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**7. Phase 3 corridor and hub targets.** FACT: "Phase 3 prioritizes a total of 37,000 miles (72% of the NHFN) of ZEF corridors. Forty-three percent of all benefits stemming from the 1.28 million square miles of ZEF hubs in Phase 3 are anticipated to flow to disadvantaged communities." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**8. Phase 4 corridor and hub targets.** FACT: "Phase 4 prioritizes 49,000 miles (94% of the NHFN) of ZEF corridors. Forty-seven percent of all benefits stemming from the 3.12 million square miles of ZEF hubs in Phase 4 are anticipated to flow to disadvantaged communities." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**9. Environmental-justice benefit share across all four phases.** FACT: "% ZEF Hub Benefits to Disadvantaged Communities 40% 40% 43% 47%" *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**10. Port tonnage inclusion tiers by phase.** FACT: "The most heavily used ports by annual freight tonnage (top 20% in Phases 1–2, top 40% in Phase 3, and top 60% in Phase 4), intermodal freight facilities, and key truck service facility locations." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Operational implication:* freight forwarders whose cargo volumes move through mid-tier ports should not assume Phase 1 or Phase 2 drayage infrastructure readiness; the later phases are the earliest window for those ports to enter priority scope.

**11. Corridor volume inclusion tiers by phase.** FACT: "The most heavily used freight corridor segments by freight volume on the NHFN (top 25% in Phases 1–3 and top 50% in Phase 4)." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**12. Deployment factor: total cost of ownership.** FACT: "Projected ZE-MHDV volumes that demonstrate optimal total cost of ownership compared to internal combustion engine trucks (e.g., early markets with first- to last-mile delivery, local and regional haul, and moving toward long-haul transportation)." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**13. Deployment factor: environmental and air-quality burden.** FACT: "Locations that bear disproportionate environmental and air quality burden from MHDV transportation and are in nonattainment for criteria air pollutants." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**14. Deployment factor: state ZEV-enabling policy.** FACT: "States with policies that enable ZEV deployment." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

**15. GIS data availability.** FACT: "Download the GIS files used to create the maps for each phase. Please note the linked file is 40 MB." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Not addressed: the Strategy defines no product, cargo, or commodity compliance category; it is an infrastructure-investment-prioritisation framework, not a product regulation.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Not addressed: no registration or reporting obligation running to a private freight-forwarding operator is stated anywhere in the retrievable pool text.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* the workspace's lane management system should be able to identify which customer shipments move via drayage or domestic road segments within each phase's ZEF hub geographies and NHFN corridor segments; without lane-level phase mapping, the workspace cannot provide clients with credible ZE-MHDV drayage availability timelines.

*Analytical inference:* integrating the Strategy's own GIS files into a transport management or client-reporting system is a concrete, low-cost step that enables systematic identification of ZEF corridor alignment; this is a data-capability gap, not a compliance obligation.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Ledna, C., Muratori, M., Yip, A., Jadun, P., Hoehne, C., and Podkaminer, K. 2024. Assessing Total Cost of Driving Competitiveness of Zero-Emission Trucks. iScience." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the phased vehicle-use-case sequencing in the Strategy (lighter local classes first, long-haul Class 8 last) is directly derived from this cited total-cost-of-ownership research.

FACT: "Researchers are also exploring the potential for high-power fast charging and rapid hydrogen refueling for ZE-MHDVs." *Source: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE. https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf

*Analytical inference:* advances in high-power charging technology could compress the later-phase timeline for long-haul ZE-MHDV availability; workspaces sourcing road carrier capacity for transcontinental lanes should monitor this research area as a leading indicator.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- March 2024: Strategy published by the Joint Office, DOE, DOT, and EPA.
- September 2024: Strategy updated.
- 2024 to 2027: Phase 1, Establish Hubs.
- 2027 to 2030: Phase 2, Connect Hubs.
- 2030 to 2035: Phase 3, Expand Corridors.
- 2035 to 2040: Phase 4, Complete Network.
- 2035: DOE Regional Clean Hydrogen Hubs stated as in full production.

*Source for timeline entries: National Zero-Emission Freight Corridor Strategy, Joint Office of Energy and Transportation / DOE, March 2024 (updated September 2024). https://driveelectric.gov/files/zef-corridor-strategy.pdf*
