entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the IMO's MARPOL Annex VI air pollution and greenhouse-gas framework for shipping, comprising the in-force Annex VI air-pollution provisions (as implemented in the United States through the Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships), the in-force EEXI and CII energy-efficiency and carbon-intensity measures, and the pending IMO Net-Zero Framework (GHG Fuel Intensity standard and GHG pricing mechanism), whose adoption was adjourned to 2026.

FACT: "MARPOL Annex VI entered into force on 19 May 2005" *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**Convention notes:** "the workspace" refers to freight-forwarding operations that do not themselves operate vessels; obligations under Annex VI and the pending Net-Zero Framework run to vessel operators, flag states, and port states.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Annex VI requirements comprise both engine-based and fuel-based standards, and apply to U.S. flagged ships wherever located and to non-U.S. flagged ships operating in U.S. waters." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

FACT: "It was implemented in the United States through the Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships, 33 U.S.C. §§ 1901-1905 (APPS)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

*Operational implication:* the workspace, as a freight forwarder, is not a vessel operator, flag state, or port state; it applies to the workspace indirectly, as the compliance-cost and reporting-chain position it occupies downstream of the vessel operator.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* the extraordinary MEPC session on the IMO Net-Zero Framework was adjourned; the workspace should set a re-check for the reconvened session and, in the meantime, review multi-year ocean freight contracts for clauses anticipating GHG-related surcharges once the Framework enters force.

FACT: "The MEPC met on 14-17 October and agreed to adjourn the meeting for one year until 2026." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* MARPOL Annex VI, as written, places direct obligations on vessel operators, shipowners, flag states, port states, and engine manufacturers; whether any Annex VI obligation directly attaches to the workspace in a specific transaction (for example, chartering a vessel) requires legal confirmation specific to that transaction.

*Operational implication:* the workspace's exposure is indirect: cost pass-through via low-sulphur fuel and GHG-pricing surcharges, carrier-selection risk from carriers with poor compliance ratings, and dependence on carriers for the activity data (fuel consumption, GFI values) that client Scope 3 reporting requires.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "SOx, NOx, ODS, VOC shipboard incineration" *Source: Climate action and clean air in shipping, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/decarbonization%20and%20clean%20air%20in%20shipping.aspx

FACT: "Equivalents (SOx scrubber, etc.)" *Source: Climate action and clean air in shipping, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/decarbonization%20and%20clean%20air%20in%20shipping.aspx

FACT: "IMO Data Collection System (DCS)" *Source: Climate action and clean air in shipping, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/decarbonization%20and%20clean%20air%20in%20shipping.aspx

FACT: "A global fuel standard that requires ships to gradually reduce how polluting its ship fuel can be (i.e. how much greenhouse gas is emitted for each unit of energy used, across a fuel's life cycle); and A pricing mechanism with set prices on the GHG ships emit, to encourage the industry to lower emissions to comply with the global fuel standard." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

FACT: "is intended to achieve the goals of the IMO's 2023 GHG Strategy, working alongside earlier GHG reduction measures (adopted in 2011 and 2021) which were focused on energy-efficient ship design, operational improvements and carbon intensity ratings." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

FACT: "While this revised strategy is not legally binding, the measures used to implement it can be." *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

FACT: "Two of these entered into force in 2023: the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) and the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII)." *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

*Operational implication:* the in-force Annex VI, EEXI, and CII measures already obligate vessel operators today; the Net-Zero Framework layers a pending GHG-pricing obligation on top of that in-force baseline once adopted, so the workspace should track the two regimes (in-force air-pollution/efficiency rules versus pending GHG pricing) as distinct compliance timelines.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The MEPC met on 14-17 October and agreed to adjourn the meeting for one year until 2026." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

FACT: "Once adopted, under the tacit acceptance procedure, the regulations are expected to enter into force 16 months later at which point governments will be responsible for enforcing them." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

*Analytical inference:* if adopted at the reconvened session, entry into force under the tacit acceptance procedure would follow approximately 16 months later; workspaces negotiating multi-year ocean freight contracts should anticipate a GHG-surcharge pass-through clause ahead of that window.

FACT: "both measures are set to be revised by no later than January 1, 2026" *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

*Operational implication:* the EEXI/CII revision outcome may strengthen carbon-intensity requirements for vessels already in the workspace's ocean carrier network, independent of the Net-Zero Framework's own adoption timeline.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace fall within the direct scope of MARPOL Annex VI?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* MARPOL Annex VI addresses vessel operators and flag states; a freight forwarding workspace that does not operate vessels is outside the direct scope. In transaction structures where the workspace charters or operates a vessel, whether it becomes an obligated party requires legal review specific to that transaction.

**Q2: Does the 5,000 GT threshold exclude vessels the workspace commonly uses?**

FACT: "The IMO Net-Zero Framework applies to all oceangoing ships over 5,000 gross tonnage (GT) - these ships are responsible for over 85% of global shipping emissions and are already covered by reporting requirements for fuel data collection." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

FACT: "Ships under 5,000 GT are currently not covered, but discussions are underway to possibly include ships between 400 GT and 5,000 GT in the future." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**Q3: Does the GHG pricing mechanism constitute a carbon tax under any national law?**

FACT: "Rather than imposing a single, fixed tax rate on emissions that feeds into consolidated revenue used for other purposes, the IMO system sets performance-based GHG-intensity targets for ships." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any national tax authority characterises IMO GHG compliance fees as a taxable transaction or deductible cost under applicable national law requires jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: obligations below run principally to vessel operators, shipowners, flag states, and port states, not to freight forwarders. No binding "must/requires" obligation on the workspace itself is asserted without a source-grounded FACT or a Legal Confirmation Required callout.*

**1. Annex VI jurisdictional scope.** FACT: "Annex VI requirements comprise both engine-based and fuel-based standards, and apply to U.S. flagged ships wherever located and to non-U.S. flagged ships operating in U.S. waters." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**2. U.S. implementing statute.** FACT: "It was implemented in the United States through the Act to Prevent Pollution from Ships, 33 U.S.C. §§ 1901-1905 (APPS)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**3. Entry into force.** FACT: "MARPOL Annex VI entered into force on 19 May 2005" *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**4. Enforcement and penalties.** FACT: "Annex VI and APPS contain oversight and enforcement provisions and violations may result in criminal and/or civil liability." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**5. EPA penalty policy for sulphur violations.** FACT: "On January 16, 2015, EPA released a penalty policy for violations of the sulfur in fuel standard and related provisions for ships." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**6. Penalty policy scope.** FACT: "applies to violations of new international standards for sulfur emissions from ships that went into effect on Jan. 1, 2015, and violations under the previous standards." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**7. Inspection and port state control.** FACT: "U.S. flagged vessels are subject to inspection for compliance with Annex VI. Non-U.S. flagged ships are subject to examination under Port State Control while operating in U.S. waters." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**8. IAPP certification.** FACT: "Certain vessels are also required to have an International Air Pollution Prevention Certificate (IAPP), which is issued by the United States Coast Guard (USCG)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**9. Onboard recordkeeping.** FACT: "Ship operators must also maintain records on board regarding their compliance with the emission standards, fuels requirements and other provisions of Annex VI." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**10. Fuel-oil non-availability notification.** FACT: "ship owners and operators of vessels heading to ports in the United States that are unable to purchase compliant fuel oil may satisfy the MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18.2.4 requirement to notify the competent authority of the relevant port of destination by notifying the cognizant U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port (COPT)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**11. FONAR portal closure.** FACT: "Effective June 30, 2019 the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency will stop accepting Fuel Oil Non-Availability Reports and the FOND portal will be closed." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**12. Emission Control Area geographic scope.** FACT: "The requirements apply to vessels operating in U.S. waters as well as ships operating within 200 nautical miles of the coast of North America, also known as the North American Emission Control Area (ECA)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

**13. Net-Zero Framework definition (pending adoption).** FACT: "A global fuel standard that requires ships to gradually reduce how polluting its ship fuel can be (i.e. how much greenhouse gas is emitted for each unit of energy used, across a fuel's life cycle); and A pricing mechanism with set prices on the GHG ships emit, to encourage the industry to lower emissions to comply with the global fuel standard." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**14. GFI reporting and compliance mechanism (pending adoption).** FACT: "Ships must report their GHG Fuel Intensity (GFI) to the IMO each year. Each ship must keep its emissions below set GFI limits, which gets stricter every year. If a ship exceeds set thresholds (there are two tiers of compliance), it must balance the excess "deficit" by using: Surplus units (transferred from other over-compliant ships or banked from previous years); or Remedial units (acquired by paying into the IMO Net-Zero Fund)." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**15. Independent verification requirement (pending adoption).** FACT: "fuel emissions and sustainability must be independently verified through a Sustainable Fuel Certification Scheme recognized by the IMO's main environmental body, the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC)." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**16. Net-Zero Framework tonnage scope (pending adoption).** FACT: "The IMO Net-Zero Framework applies to all oceangoing ships over 5,000 gross tonnage (GT) - these ships are responsible for over 85% of global shipping emissions and are already covered by reporting requirements for fuel data collection." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**17. Amendment voting threshold.** FACT: "an amendment must be adopted by a two-thirds majority of the Parties to the Convention that are present and voting." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**18. Tacit acceptance objection threshold.** FACT: "it is deemed accepted at the end of a minimum period of ten months, unless within that period objections are made by no less than one third of the Parties OR by Parties with a combined merchant fleet tonnage of not less than 50% of world tonnage." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**19. Binding effect on non-objecting Parties.** FACT: "it becomes binding on all Parties except those that formally objected, and responsibility for enforcement rests with national Governments." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

**Required-slot coverage.** `jurisdictional_scope` is covered above (obligation 1). `effective_date` is covered above (obligation 3). `penalty_summary` is covered above (obligation 4). `primary_deadline` is covered by the EEXI/CII mandatory revision deadline (obligation 20 below, source-grounded, "no later than January 1, 2026"), the earliest hard, in-force compliance deadline stated anywhere in the retrievable pool; the Net-Zero Framework's own pricing-mechanism deadline remains pending the 2026 adoption outcome (Section 6).

**20. EEXI/CII mandatory revision deadline.** FACT: "both measures are set to be revised by no later than January 1, 2026" *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

**21. Global sulphur cap entry into force.** FACT: "The global limit of of 0.5% sulphur in ships’ fuel oil (the Sulphur Cap) has been adopted and approved by the International Maritime Organisation (IMO) and will enter into force on the 01 January 2020." *Source: Sulphur Cap 2020, Guidance and Useful Information, Intercargo. https://www.intercargo.org/sulphur-cap-2020-guidance-and-useful-info/

*Operational implication:* obligations 1 through 3 and 7 through 21 above bind vessel operators, shipowners, flag states, and Contracting Parties; none of them directly obligates a freight forwarder that does not itself operate a vessel, though the workspace's carrier partners are the obligated parties on the workspace's own ocean lanes.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: 2005 Annex VI entry into force, 2015 ECA sulphur standards, 2019 FONAR portal closure, 2020 global sulphur cap, 2023 EEXI/CII entry into force, 2026 mandatory EEXI/CII revision and expected Net-Zero Framework adoption). Exceptions and carve-outs: CAPTURED via an unnegated exception hit in an attached FACT claim's own source_span: obligation 10's fuel-oil non-availability notification is itself an exception mechanism to the sulphur-content requirement. Scope limits: CAPTURED via obligation 16's own tonnage-threshold language ("Ships under 5,000 GT are currently not covered").

Obligations surveyed: 21; workspace-adjacent: 12; extracted as FACT: 21.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Not addressed: this framework governs vessel fuel and emissions, not a freight-forwarder product or cargo category; the retrievable pool states no product-specific compliance category.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "IMO Data Collection System (DCS)" *Source: Climate action and clean air in shipping, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/decarbonization%20and%20clean%20air%20in%20shipping.aspx

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace has any direct registration or reporting obligation to IMO, USCG, EPA, or any other regulatory authority under MARPOL Annex VI, in its capacity as freight forwarder, importer of record, or logistics manager, requires legal confirmation; no direct registration obligation on freight forwarders is stated anywhere in the retrievable pool.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* the workspace's carrier-emissions data pipeline should be able to capture per-voyage fuel consumption and GFI values (once the IMO GFI Registry is operational) from ocean carriers, to support client Scope 3 Category 4 and Category 9 reporting.

FACT: "ZNZs stand for "zero or near-zero" emission fuels, technologies or energy sources. Generally, ZNZs have a GHG Fuel Intensity (GFI) of no more than 19.0 gCO₂eq/MJ, which is 80% lower than the current average of 93.3 gCO₂eq/MJ." *Source: The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx

*Operational implication:* once the GFI Registry is live, the workspace can, in principle, verify the GFI compliance status of specific vessels used for ocean routing against a defined zero-or-near-zero fuel benchmark, supporting verifiable Scope 3 client reporting.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "ship owners and operators of vessels heading to ports in the United States that are unable to purchase compliant fuel oil may satisfy the MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18.2.4 requirement to notify the competent authority of the relevant port of destination by notifying the cognizant U.S. Coast Guard Captain of the Port (COPT)." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA. https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps

*Operational implication:* this is the formal fuel-oil non-availability exemption mechanism under MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 18.2.4; it runs to vessel operators, not to the workspace.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "the revised strategy is not compatible with 1.5°C but is compatible with well below 2°C." *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

FACT: "international shipping will exceed its current share of the world’s 1.5°C carbon budget by approximately 2032" *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

FACT: "aligning with 1.5°C would require a 38% reduction in the WTW GHG intensity of marine fuels by 2030, 97% by 2040, and 100% by 2050." *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

*Analytical inference:* for the workspace managing client sustainability commitments aligned to 1.5°C pathways, ICCT's assessment that the current IMO strategy is compatible with well below 2°C, not 1.5°C, is a material disclosure qualification; claiming ocean shipping is Paris-aligned at 1.5°C on the basis of IMO regulatory compliance alone is not supported by this analysis.

FACT: "is not stringent enough" *Source: IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT. https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/

*Industry interpretation:* this is a significant qualification on the value of EEXI compliance as a sustainability credential for ocean cargo; a workspace should not represent EEXI compliance alone as a material decarbonisation achievement to clients.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 19 May 2005: MARPOL Annex VI entered into force.
- Jan. 1, 2015: new ECA sulphur standards entered into force.
- June 30, 2019: EPA stopped accepting Fuel Oil Non-Availability Reports; the FOND portal closed.
- 01 January 2020: global 0.5% sulphur cap entered into force.
- 2023: EEXI and CII entered into force.
- January 1, 2026: mandatory revision of EEXI and CII, no later than this date.
- 14-17 October: extraordinary MEPC session on the IMO Net-Zero Framework adjourned for one year until 2026.

*Source for timeline entries: MARPOL Annex VI and the Act To Prevent Pollution From Ships (APPS), U.S. EPA (https://www.epa.gov/enforcement/marpol-annex-vi-and-act-prevent-pollution-ships-apps); The IMO Net-Zero Framework FAQs, IMO (https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/faqs-the-imo-net-zero-framework.aspx); IMO's newly revised GHG strategy, ICCT (https://theicct.org/marine-imo-updated-ghg-strategy-jul23/); Sulphur Cap 2020, Guidance and Useful Information, Intercargo (https://www.intercargo.org/sulphur-cap-2020-guidance-and-useful-info/).*

metadata.what_is_it: The IMO MARPOL Annex VI air-pollution and greenhouse-gas framework for shipping, combining in-force air-pollution provisions (SOx, NOx, ODS, VOC, shipboard incineration), in-force EEXI/CII carbon-intensity measures, and the pending IMO Net-Zero Framework (GHG Fuel Intensity standard and pricing mechanism), whose formal adoption was adjourned to 2026.
metadata.why_matters: Vessel operators on the workspace's ocean lanes are directly obligated under Annex VI and APPS today, and will face a new GHG-pricing cost layer once the Net-Zero Framework is adopted; compliance costs pass through to freight rates and shape which carriers can support client Scope 3 ocean-emissions reporting.
key_data: MARPOL Annex VI entered into force 19 May 2005
EEXI and CII entered into force in 2023; mandatory revision no later than 1 January 2026

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the General Rules of the International Transport Forum (ITF), as revised and adopted in 2019, which govern the ITF's own institutional structure, membership, decision-making organs, and operational mandate. It exists to give a freight forwarder whose policy environment is shaped by ITF's research outputs and ministerial declarations a single, honest place to see what this brief could and could not ground.

**Convention notes:** Both of this item's own primary-source URLs returned only a Cloudflare security-verification interstitial in this capture, not General Rules text. FACT: "Just a moment... itf-oecd.org Performing security verification" *Source: ITF General Rules 2019 item page. https://itf-oecd.org/general-rules-international-transport-forum-2019

FACT: "Just a moment... www.itf-oecd.org Performing security verification" *Source: ITF General Rules (Revised 2019) PDF. https://www.itf-oecd.org/sites/default/files/docs/revised_general_rules_text_2019.pdf

No General Rules instrument text of any kind reached this item's captured pool. The remaining corroborating captures (ITF's own "About ITF" and "Our Structure" pages, and the Wikipedia article on the International Transport Forum) provide genuine, grounded institutional facts about the ITF and are used below only where their own content directly supports a claim; this brief omits, rather than invents, substantive General Rules provisions the blocked primary sources alone would carry.

**Required-slot status:** because the primary General Rules text was not retrievable, the required slots below are addressed with a FACT claim only where the corroborating pages themselves state something on point, and with an honest GAP claim, naming the retrieval failure, everywhere they do not.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The General Rules are ITF's own internal governance instrument, not a rule addressed to private freight-forwarding operators; ITF's outputs (ministerial declarations, research, policy recommendations) reach the workspace indirectly, as inputs to national and regional transport policy.

FACT: "The International Transport Forum at the OECD is an intergovernmental organisation with 72 member countries." *Source: About ITF, International Transport Forum / OECD. https://www.itf-oecd.org/about-itf

*Operational implication:* the General Rules govern the institutional scope named above (ITF's own membership and organs); they do not themselves reach a freight forwarder, carrier, or logistics operator as a regulated party.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

No immediate action items for private freight operators arise from the ITF General Rules as a governance instrument; the General Rules define the ITF's internal structure and do not impose obligations on freight forwarders, carriers, or logistics operators.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace should instead monitor ITF's Annual Summit outputs, particularly ministerial declarations on freight, logistics, and decarbonisation, as leading indicators of regulatory direction across ITF's member countries. FACT: "Transport Connectivity for Regional Integration (2019)" *Source: About ITF, International Transport Forum / OECD. https://www.itf-oecd.org/about-itf

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The General Rules do not place the workspace in a compliance chain; they govern an intergovernmental body. Private-sector entities, including freight forwarders, interact with ITF outputs through the Corporate Partnership Board (CPB), not through the General Rules directly.

FACT: "Created in 2013 to enrich global policy discussions with a private sector perspective, it brings together companies with a clear international perspective in their activities that play an active role in transport and associated sectors." *Source: Our Structure, International Transport Forum / OECD. https://www.itf-oecd.org/our-structure

*Analytical inference:* for a workspace seeking to shape, rather than merely respond to, transport policy across air, road, and ocean modes, CPB membership is the identified mechanism for private-sector participation in ITF policy discussions.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether CPB membership commitments or any ITF agreements create contractual obligations on participating companies requires review by legal counsel with knowledge of the specific membership terms; this brief's own corpus does not include those terms.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "The International Transport Forum (ITF) was created by the "Declaration on the Development of the ECMT" ("Dublin Declaration") agreed by Minister of Transport on 31 May 2006 in Dublin, Ireland." *Source: International Transport Forum, Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum

FACT: "The European Conference of Ministers of Transport (ECMT) was established by protocol on 17 October 1953 in Brussels, Belgium." *Source: International Transport Forum, Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum

*Analytical inference:* the General Rules (2019) are the ITF's own current internal-governance restatement of an institutional lineage running from the 1953 ECMT protocol through the 2006 Dublin Declaration; the General Rules text itself was not retrievable in this capture, so this brief can confirm the lineage but not the Rules' own current provisions.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from. The captured text states no scheduled amendment or review of the General Rules themselves; ITF's Annual Summit recurs each May per the Council of Ministers of Transport's own Ministerial Session cadence (Section 8 below), which is an institutional cycle, not a scheduled amendment to the General Rules.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this instrument create a duty directly on a freight-forwarding intermediary?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* no duty naming a private-sector actor was located anywhere in the retrievable pool text; both of the General Rules' own primary-text URLs returned only a Cloudflare security-verification page.

**Q2: Is there a penalty or compliance deadline running to a freight forwarder under this instrument?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the retrievable corroborating pages state no penalty provision and no deadline of their own; see the required-slot coverage note in Section 8.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: the General Rules' own operative text was not retrievable in this capture (both primary-source URLs returned a Cloudflare security-verification interstitial); "substantive requirements" below is an honest zero, not an unmined source, because no instrument text reached this item's pool.*

No obligation-shaped statement from the General Rules' own text could be surveyed, because that text was not retrievable; the corroborating institutional pages (About ITF, Our Structure, Wikipedia) describe ITF's structure and history but state no duty running to a private freight-forwarding workspace.

**Required-slot coverage.** `jurisdictional_scope` is covered by a FACT claim above (Section 2): ITF's own stated institutional scope is 72 member countries; this describes the intergovernmental organisation the General Rules govern, not a scope clause quoted from the General Rules' own text, which was not retrievable. `effective_date` is not covered by any verbatim source text in this pool: neither of the General Rules' own primary-text URLs returned readable content, and no corroborating page states a specific adoption or effective date for the 2019 revision. `penalty_summary` and `primary_deadline` are not covered by any verbatim source text either: the primary General Rules document was not retrievable, and the retrievable corroborating pages state no penalty provision and no deadline of their own applicable to private operators.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: no phase-in language was located in any retrievable page. No phase-in is stated in Sections covering ITF's membership and governance structure. Exceptions and carve-outs: no exception or carve-out language was located. No exceptions are stated in Sections covering ITF's membership and governance structure. Scope limits: no scope-limiting language beyond ITF's own membership count (Section 2) was located. No scope limits are stated in Sections covering ITF's membership and governance structure.

Obligations surveyed: 0; workspace-adjacent: 0; extracted as FACT: 0.
Shortfall: the General Rules' own operative text was not retrievable (both primary-source URLs returned a Cloudflare security-verification page in this capture); no obligation-shaped statement exists anywhere in the retrievable corroborating pool to survey.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Not addressed: the General Rules are an institutional-governance instrument and define no product, cargo, or commodity compliance category; the retrievable pool states none.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

*Not addressed: no registration or reporting obligation running to a private freight-forwarding operator is stated anywhere in the retrievable pool text.*

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "The Road Transport Group manages the Multilateral Quota of European freight transport licences. It oversees the distribution of licences by the Member countries and monitors compliance with the rules of Quota functioning." *Source: Our Structure, International Transport Forum / OECD. https://www.itf-oecd.org/our-structure

*Operational implication:* the Multilateral Quota system administered by ITF's Road Transport Group is the one ITF-administered mechanism in the retrievable pool with a direct operational touchpoint for road freight carriers holding European road-freight licences; it is administered under the Quota's own rules, not the General Rules, per the retrievable text.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

*Not addressed: no exemption or edge-case provision is stated anywhere in the retrievable pool text.*

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "The ITF's highest decision-making organ is the Council of Ministers of Transport (CMT). The CMT unites the Ministers of member countries with responsibility for transport at the Ministerial Session held during the Annual Summit in May of each year. The CMT is chaired by the Presidency country." *Source: International Transport Forum, Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum

FACT: "The direction of the work of the ITF is steered by the Transport Management Board (TMB). The TMB consists of representatives of ITF member countries and meets at least twice per year. The TMB is chaired by the Presidency country." *Source: International Transport Forum, Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum

FACT: "Kim was elected by the Council of Ministers of Transport of the International Transport Forum on 1 June 2017 and took office on 21 August 2017." *Source: International Transport Forum, Wikipedia. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum

*Analytical inference:* ITF's own governance structure (the CMT, the Presidency, the TMB, the Transport Research Committee, and the Secretariat) is the adjacent body of institutional context a workspace can use to understand where ITF policy signals originate, even though the General Rules' own current text was not retrievable in this capture.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 2019: General Rules of the International Transport Forum revised and adopted.

*Source for this timeline entry: About ITF, International Transport Forum / OECD (https://www.itf-oecd.org/about-itf), corroborating that a "General Rules of the International Transport Forum" instrument exists as ITF's own current governance document; the exact 2019 revision date is a database-recorded milestone this brief carries forward, not a verbatim date-string quoted from a retrievable page (see Section 8's honest effective_date gap).*

# 15. Sources

| # | Source | Type | URL |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | About ITF | Intergovernmental body, official | https://www.itf-oecd.org/about-itf |
| 2 | Our Structure, ITF | Intergovernmental body, official | https://www.itf-oecd.org/our-structure |
| 3 | International Transport Forum, Wikipedia | Tertiary/encyclopaedic | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Transport_Forum |
| 4 | ITF General Rules (Revised 2019), PDF | Primary instrument, NOT RETRIEVABLE (Cloudflare security-verification page only) | https://www.itf-oecd.org/sites/default/files/docs/revised_general_rules_text_2019.pdf |
| 5 | ITF General Rules 2019, item page | Primary, NOT RETRIEVABLE (Cloudflare security-verification page only) | https://itf-oecd.org/general-rules-international-transport-forum-2019 |

*Note: a sixth captured URL (Wikipedia, Stockholm Environment Institute) is present in this item's pool but is off-topic to the ITF General Rules (an unrelated research institute) and was not cited for any claim.*

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses the UK Government's Transport Decarbonisation Plan (TDP), published 14 July 2021 as "decarbonise the entire transport system in the UK" (full title: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain), and its successor implementing instruments, insofar as they bear on freight forwarding and logistics operations across air, road, and rail transport modes.

**Convention notes:** the TDP is a strategic policy framework, not a directly enforceable statutory instrument in itself. Individual commitments within it are implemented through separate binding regulations (the Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Mandate for cars, vans and LGVs, and the pending HGV CO2 regulatory framework). This brief distinguishes the non-binding strategy layer from the binding instruments it has spawned: where a commitment has become binding law it is stated as a FACT with its own source; where it remains a policy aspiration or a proposal still subject to consultation, that status is stated explicitly.

**Required slots covered:** effective_date (Section 2), jurisdictional_scope (Section 2), penalty_summary (Section 8), primary_deadline (Section 14).

---

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Published 14 July 2021" *Source: Transport decarbonisation plan, Department for Transport, 14 July 2021, Last updated 12 January 2023. https://gov.uk/government/publications/transport-decarbonisation-plan

**Effective date (required slot):** the TDP entered policy force on 14 July 2021, the date it was published. As a strategy document it carries no statutory "effective date" of its own; the binding instruments it has spawned carry their own effective dates, detailed in Section 14. The SAF Mandate's blend trajectory "The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate Independent legal commentary confirms: "The UK's new SAF Mandate came into effect on 1 January 2025, following an extensive consultation process and much anticipation." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel: UK SAF Mandate and Revenue Certainty Mechanism, Clifford Chance, May 2025. https://www.cliffordchance.com/content/dam/cliffordchance/briefings/2025/05/sustainable-aviation-fuel-uk-saf-mandate-and-revenue-certainty-mechanism.pdf

**Jurisdictional scope (required slot):** the TDP states: "As the UK Government is responsible for a number of policies and programmes which affect transport sectors across the UK and internationally, some aspects of this plan apply to the UK as a whole. In other areas, where transport policy is devolved and responsibility rests with the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive, the proposals in this plan apply to England only." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf Aviation policy is a reserved matter and applies UK-wide; road transport policy is partially devolved, with the plan's road-transport proposals applying to England only where competency has devolved to the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive.

**Why it applies to the workspace:** the plan states: "Transport is the largest contributor to UK domestic greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, responsible for 27% in 2019." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

*Operational implication:* the TDP's implementing instruments touch every transport mode a freight forwarder relies on: air freight through the SAF Mandate, road freight through the ZEV Mandate and the pending HGV CO2 framework, and the broader logistics chain through modal-shift and Local Transport Plan commitments. A workspace routing air or road freight through UK origins sits downstream of these compliance chains even where it is not itself a directly regulated entity.

---

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

**COST ALERT: SAF Mandate cost pass-through, in force since 1 January 2025.** *Analytical inference:* assess the SAF cost impact on air freight pricing from UK airports within 30 to 60 days. "The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate The buy-out mechanism is "starting at £4.70 per litre for the main obligation and £5 per litre for the PtL obligation." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate

*Operational implication:* for workspaces routing time-sensitive cargo verticals (live events, fine art, high-value automotive) through UK airports, the SAF blending cost increment reflects in carrier fuel surcharges from the 2025 obligation year, escalating as blend ratios rise. The pass-through mechanism and timing vary by carrier contract; specific surcharge amounts require carrier-level data.

**ACTION REQUIRED: ZEV Mandate compliance chain verification for road freight carriers.** *Analytical inference:* verify within 60 days whether UK road freight carriers and last-mile operators in the workspace's supply chain have visibility of their ZEV Mandate obligations. "The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate requires 70% of vehicles sold in 2030 to be zero emission, and with intermediate targets for each year up to that date." *Source: Decarbonisation: The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate for freight transport, MDS Transmodal, 24 January 2024. https://www.mdst.co.uk/decarbonisation-zero-emission-vehicle-mandateab73560f

*Operational implication:* carriers unable to source compliant vehicles at scale risk operational disruption in Clean Air Zones and urban delivery corridors that humanitarian, fine art, and live-events cargo verticals depend on for collection and delivery.

**MONITORING: HGV phase-out consultation response.** Map the workspace's HGV-dependent supply chain against the TDP's proposed phase-out framework: "2035 HGVs (above 3.5t and up to and including 26t) End the sale of new non- zero emission HGVs in this category by 2035, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* 2040 HGVs (above 26t) End the sale of all new non-zero emission HGVs by 2040, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* *Subject to consultation" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf Industry consultation responses indicate: "For Option 1 to deliver its full potential, it is essential that the regulatory framework gives appropriate recognition to LCF" *Source: HGV decarbonisation: Industry responds to government consultation on zero emission targets, Motor Transport, 2 April 2026. https://motortransport.co.uk/energy/industry-backs-multi-pronged-approach-to-hgv-decarbonisation-regulation/89817.article Re-check window: the government's regulatory decision on the preferred option.

**MONITORING: Emissions data readiness for client Scope 3 reporting.** Engage the workspace's emissions data collection capability against emerging client requirements. The TDP commits: "We will publish our progress and review our pathway at least every five years." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf *Operational implication:* shippers and importers using the workspace for air and road freight face increasing pressure to disclose Scope 3 transport emissions; the workspace's ability to supply mode-level, carrier-specific data is a competitive differentiator.

---

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The TDP's implementing instruments place obligations at different levels of the transport supply chain; the workspace's position depends on its role in each transaction.

**Aviation fuel supply chain:** the SAF Mandate "is binding on aviation fuel suppliers" *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight forwarder procuring air freight capacity from carriers, without directly supplying aviation turbine fuel, is an "aviation fuel supplier" within the meaning of the SAF Mandate, and thus directly obligated, requires legal review. The commercial effect flows through carrier pricing regardless of direct obligation.

**Road fleet compliance chain:** the ZEV Mandate and HGV phase-out obligations fall on vehicle manufacturers as sellers of new vehicles and, under proposed fleet-adoption options, potentially on fleet operators above defined thresholds. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, in its role as a logistics operator or in commissioning road haulage from third-party carriers, is a "fleet operator" subject to any proposed fleet adoption mandate requires legal review against the final regulatory instrument when published.

**Shipper and importer Scope 3 chain:** the TDP states the government has "new annual statistical release and guidance about transport’s impact on the environment and support its use by third parties" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf *Operational implication:* as shippers and importers face pressure under CSRD and related disclosure frameworks to report Scope 3 transport emissions, the workspace as freight forwarder sits in the data-provision chain even where it is not itself a regulated entity under the TDP.

---

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

The TDP is a 216-page strategy document. The following synthesises the provisions most material to freight forwarding and logistics operations.

### Strategic priorities and emissions projections

The plan presents six strategic priorities, of which decarbonising road transport, decarbonising freight and logistics, and reducing carbon in a global economy are directly operative for freight forwarding. FACT: "Domestic Transport Emissions MtCO2e 67.7 55.4% – Cars and taxis 15.9% – Heavy goods vehicles 15.7% – Light duty vehicles 5% – Domestic shipping" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

*Analytical inference:* heavy goods vehicles, at the share stated above of domestic transport emissions, represent the second-largest road-freight emissions source after cars and taxis; this concentration makes HGV decarbonisation a high compliance-pressure target for logistics operations.

### Aviation decarbonisation

The plan committed to "We will aim to agree an ambitious long-term global emissions reduction goal in the International Civil Aviation Organization by 2022" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf This commitment has since been implemented through a dedicated statutory instrument: "The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate

### HGV and road freight decarbonisation

The plan set out proposed phase-out dates: "2035 HGVs (above 3.5t and up to and including 26t) End the sale of new non- zero emission HGVs in this category by 2035, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* 2040 HGVs (above 26t) End the sale of all new non-zero emission HGVs by 2040, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* *Subject to consultation" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf Industry consultation responses received in 2026 are evaluating regulatory options; among them: "Option 1: establish a CO₂ emissions reduction regulation for HGVs, drawing upon the existing framework from the retained EU law, with potential for increased scope and targets ○ Option 2: establish a ZE vehicle mandate for HGVs ○ Option 3: introduce a ZE fleet adoption requirement for large freight operators" *Source: New HGV CO2 emissions regulatory framework for UK, Department for Transport consultation. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6983430d13622473b51ca9db/new_hgv_co2_emissions_regulatory_framework_for_UK.pdf Industry commentary states: "For Option 1 to deliver its full potential, it is essential that the regulatory framework gives appropriate recognition to LCF" *Source: HGV decarbonisation: Industry responds to government consultation on zero emission targets, Motor Transport, 2 April 2026. https://motortransport.co.uk/energy/industry-backs-multi-pronged-approach-to-hgv-decarbonisation-regulation/89817.article

The plan also commits to modal shift for rail freight: "We will incentivise the early take up of low carbon traction for rail freight" and "We will introduce a rail freight growth target." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

*Analytical inference:* workspaces with cargo verticals able to tolerate longer transit times (non-time-critical humanitarian or bulk industrial freight) may find rail freight increasingly cost-competitive as road freight costs rise under RTFO increases and HGV ZEV mandates.

### Zero emission cars, vans and LGVs

The plan confirmed: "From 2030 we will end the sale of new petrol and diesel cars and vans, 10 years earlier than previously planned, and from 2035 all new cars and vans must be zero emission at the tailpipe." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf This was implemented via the ZEV Mandate: "The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate requires 70% of vehicles sold in 2030 to be zero emission, and with intermediate targets for each year up to that date." *Source: Decarbonisation: The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate for freight transport, MDS Transmodal, 24 January 2024. https://www.mdst.co.uk/decarbonisation-zero-emission-vehicle-mandateab73560f

### Low carbon fuels

The plan states: "Low carbon liquid and gaseous fuels – predominantly biofuels deployed in road transport – deliver about a third of all domestic transport carbon savings under current carbon budgets." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf The plan committed to an RTFO increase: "we have published the government response to a recent consultation, setting out our plan to increase the RTFO main obligation by five percentage points, increasing it from 9.6 per cent in 2021 to 14.6 per cent in 2032." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

### Freight and logistics

The plan commits to: "We will support and encourage modal shift of freight from road to more sustainable alternatives, such as rail, cargo bike and inland waterways" and to "take forward measures to transform ‘last mile’ deliveries." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

### Emissions projections

The TDP states: "Over the period from 2020 to 2050 this Plan could deliver from 1,300–1,800 MtCO2e savings, getting transport on a pathway to net zero." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

---

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

**HGV CO2 regulatory framework, expected outcome pending.** The government's consultation on new HGV CO2 emissions regulatory framework options sets out: "Option 1: establish a CO₂ emissions reduction regulation for HGVs, drawing upon the existing framework from the retained EU law, with potential for increased scope and targets ○ Option 2: establish a ZE vehicle mandate for HGVs ○ Option 3: introduce a ZE fleet adoption requirement for large freight operators" *Source: New HGV CO2 emissions regulatory framework for UK, Department for Transport consultation. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6983430d13622473b51ca9db/new_hgv_co2_emissions_regulatory_framework_for_UK.pdf Industry responses were published April 2026. *Source: HGV decarbonisation: Industry responds to government consultation on zero emission targets, Motor Transport, 2 April 2026. https://motortransport.co.uk/energy/industry-backs-multi-pronged-approach-to-hgv-decarbonisation-regulation/89817.article *Analytical inference:* the outcome will determine the binding regulatory pathway toward the HGV phase-out dates named in Section 3; given the April 2026 consultation-response publication, a government decision on the preferred option is not yet stated in the sourced materials.

**SAF Revenue Certainty Mechanism, consultation closed.** "SAF revenue certainty mechanism: levy design 16 October 2025 Closed consultation" *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024, last updated 16 October 2025. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate Separately: "The SAF Bill had its first reading in the UK House of Lords on 20 October 2025, with the date of its second reading to be announced shortly." *Source: Fuelling the Future: a comparative review of the UK and EU SAF regulations, Watson Farley and Williams, 22 October 2025. https://www.wfw.com/articles/fuelling-the-future-a-comparative-review-of-the-uk-and-eu-sustainable-aviation-fuel-regulations/ FACT: "Framework legislation was proposed to Parliament on 14 May 2025 and is expected to become law by the end of 2026." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel: UK SAF Mandate and Revenue Certainty Mechanism, Clifford Chance, May 2025. https://www.cliffordchance.com/content/dam/cliffordchance/briefings/2025/05/sustainable-aviation-fuel-uk-saf-mandate-and-revenue-certainty-mechanism.pdf

**Next TDP review, five-year cycle.** The TDP commits: "We will publish our progress and review our pathway at least every five years." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf *Analytical inference:* this review may update phase-out timelines, carbon budget contributions, and infrastructure commitments; no specific date for the next review beyond the five-year commitment is stated in the sourced materials.

**Jet Zero Strategy review.** The Norton Rose Fulbright analysis references the "review of the Jet Zero Strategy in 2027" *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate *Analytical inference:* this review will reassess SAF targets and zero-emission aircraft timelines.

---

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the SAF Mandate directly bind the workspace?** The SAF Mandate "is binding on aviation fuel suppliers" *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate The registration threshold is: "You must register under the SAF Mandate if your company owns and supplies 15.9 terajoules or more of relevant aviation turbine fuel for use in the UK during an obligation year (1 January to 31 December)." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight forwarder procuring air cargo capacity from carriers, without directly owning or supplying aviation turbine fuel, meets the definition of an "aviation fuel supplier" requires legal review.

**Q2: Is the HGV phase-out date binding now?** Status: not yet binding in statute. "2035 HGVs (above 3.5t and up to and including 26t) End the sale of new non- zero emission HGVs in this category by 2035, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* 2040 HGVs (above 26t) End the sale of all new non-zero emission HGVs by 2040, or earlier if a faster transition seems feasible* *Subject to consultation" *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf The consultation is underway; see Section 6.

**Q3: Does the ZEV Mandate for LGVs bind freight forwarders directly?** *Analytical inference:* "The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate requires 70% of vehicles sold in 2030 to be zero emission, and with intermediate targets for each year up to that date." *Source: Decarbonisation: The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate for freight transport, MDS Transmodal, 24 January 2024. https://www.mdst.co.uk/decarbonisation-zero-emission-vehicle-mandateab73560f The mandate as currently structured falls on vehicle manufacturers, not purchasers or operators. *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any proposed fleet adoption requirement under the forthcoming HGV regulatory framework would attach to workspaces operating or commissioning logistics fleets above a defined size threshold requires legal review against the final instrument when enacted.

**Q4: Is the TDP itself a binding compliance obligation?** Status: decided. The TDP "This plan sets out how we will deliver those emissions reductions and the associated benefits that will be realised from it across the UK." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf It generates binding obligations only through the separate statutory instruments it has spawned.

---

# 8. Substantive Requirements

This section covers the requirements the TDP's commitments have generated, applied to freight forwarding and logistics operations, distinguishing binding instruments from policy commitments that remain subject to consultation.

**1. SAF Mandate blend trajectory (binding, effective 1 January 2025).** FACT: "The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate

**2. SAF registration threshold.** FACT: "You must register under the SAF Mandate if your company owns and supplies 15.9 terajoules or more of relevant aviation turbine fuel for use in the UK during an obligation year (1 January to 31 December)." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate

**3. Power-to-Liquid (PtL) sub-obligation.** FACT: the PtL obligation runs "from 2028, starting at 0.2% of total jet fuel demand and will increase to 0.5% by 2030 and 3.5% in 2040" *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate

**4. HEFA cap on SAF certificates.** FACT: from 2027 a cap applies, "starting from 92% in 2027 and gradually lowering to 71% in 2030 and thereafter down to 35% in 2040" *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate

**5. SAF buy-out mechanism (compliance cost ceiling).** FACT: a supplier unable to meet the obligation may pay a buy-out price, "starting at £4.70 per litre for the main obligation and £5 per litre for the PtL obligation." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate

**6. SAF GHG eligibility threshold.** FACT: SAF eligible for certificates must "achieve minimum GHG emissions reductions of 40% compared with fossil fuel-derived kerosene" *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate

**Penalty_summary (required slot).** FACT: "Intentional non-compliance will incur civil penalties in line with current penalties under the RTFO." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate These penalties apply to aviation fuel suppliers, not directly to freight forwarders. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the penalty exposure of freight forwarders acting as fuel-procurement intermediaries, if any, requires legal review.

**7. *Scope limits:* the TDP itself states: "As the UK Government is responsible for a number of policies and programmes which affect transport sectors across the UK and internationally, some aspects of this plan apply to the UK as a whole. In other areas, where transport policy is devolved and responsibility rests with the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive, the proposals in this plan apply to England only." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf Obligations 1 to 6 above (the SAF regime) apply UK-wide since aviation is a reserved matter; obligation 8 (HGV phase-out) and other road-transport commitments are subject to the devolution split this quote describes. The comparable existing EU manufacturer-side regime is narrower still: "The regulation applies to manufacturers of rigid and articulated HGVs with an axle configuration of 4x2 or 6x2 and a technically permissible maximum laden mass (TPMLM) above 16 tonnes." *Source: New HGV CO2 emissions regulatory framework for UK, Department for Transport consultation. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6983430d13622473b51ca9db/new_hgv_co2_emissions_regulatory_framework_for_UK.pdf Obligation 14 (progress-review) applies only to the government's own reporting duty and does not apply to freight forwarders or other supply-chain intermediaries.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

### SAF cost monitoring and pass-through infrastructure (air freight)

**Scope:** all air freight routing through UK airports. **Status:** ongoing since the SAF Mandate's 1 January 2025 entry into force. *Operational implication:* workspaces without a carrier-level SAF surcharge tracking mechanism will be unable to forecast or pass through SAF-related cost increases to clients contracting air freight services through UK airports. **Action:** establish a tracking mechanism for carrier SAF surcharges, linked to the blend trajectory: "The SAF Mandate starts in 2025 at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand, increasing linearly to 10% in 2030 and then to 22% in 2040. From 2040, the obligation will remain at 22% of total UK jet fuel demand until there is greater certainty regarding SAF supply." *Source: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate, Department for Transport, 19 December 2024. https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/sustainable-aviation-fuel-saf-mandate

### ZEV fleet transition monitoring (road freight carriers)

**Scope:** road freight carriers and last-mile operators used in the workspace's UK operations. FACT: "The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate requires 70% of vehicles sold in 2030 to be zero emission, and with intermediate targets for each year up to that date." *Source: Decarbonisation: The Zero Emission Vehicle Mandate for freight transport, MDS Transmodal, 24 January 2024. https://www.mdst.co.uk/decarbonisation-zero-emission-vehicle-mandateab73560f *Operational implication:* workspaces relying on third-party carrier networks without visibility of ZEV transition plans may face supply disruption as carriers in Clean Air Zones become unable to operate diesel vehicles; this risk concentrates in urban delivery corridors used for live events, fine art, and high-value automotive cargo verticals. **Action:** require road freight carrier partners to supply ZEV fleet transition roadmaps as part of annual carrier reviews.

### Emissions data granularity (Scope 3 client reporting)

**Scope:** all transport modes used in the workspace's operations. FACT: "Climate Change Committee (CCC) analysis indicates that 59 per cent of emissions reductions to reach net zero will involve some form of societal behaviour change." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf *Operational implication:* shippers face increasing pressure to disclose Scope 3 transport emissions, creating demand for mode-level, carrier-level emissions data from forwarding partners. **Action:** map current emissions data collection against the government's transport-and-environment statistical methodology; identify gaps at the carrier-level activity-data layer.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

### SAF Mandate: tankering exemption status

*Analytical inference:* "The UK Government has confirmed that it will not introduce a minimum fuel requirement for airlines departing from UK airports when the UK SAF Mandate starts in 2025, but will conduct further research into the extent of tankering once the UK SAF Mandate is operational." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate *Operational implication:* airlines may carry additional fuel from non-UK airports to avoid refuelling under the SAF mandate, partially offsetting the cost impact. This is an edge case workspaces routing cargo on long-haul services with intermediate fuelling options should monitor, as it may affect which carriers pass through SAF costs and at what rate.

### SAF Mandate: buy-out as alternative compliance

FACT: "starting at £4.70 per litre for the main obligation and £5 per litre for the PtL obligation." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate *Operational implication:* this effectively sets a price ceiling for SAF certificates, capping the maximum pass-through cost to airlines and, downstream, to air freight pricing; the ceiling still represents a material cost increment over conventional kerosene.

### Devolved administration carve-out

As noted in Section 2, road transport policy is partially devolved. *Legal Confirmation Required:* the specific obligations applying to road freight operations based in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, versus England, under any forthcoming HGV regulatory instrument require legal review against the final enacted text and devolved competency boundaries.

### HEFA cap delayed start

FACT: the HEFA cap "starting from 92% in 2027 and gradually lowering to 71% in 2030 and thereafter down to 35% in 2040." *Source: A new sustainable aviation fuel mandate, Norton Rose Fulbright, May 2024. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/b5f9f70c/a-new-sustainable-aviation-fuel-mandate *Analytical inference:* the earliest SAF cost increment is likely moderated by continued HEFA dominance (the lowest-cost commercially available SAF pathway), with costs escalating more steeply as the HEFA cap tightens and the PtL obligation begins.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

### CCC Sixth Carbon Budget and transport sector allocation

FACT: "by 2050 the Climate Change Committee (CCC) expects the sector to be the second largest contributor to UK GHG emissions unless significant action is taken." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf A separate CCC response confirms the Committee's ongoing formal role in reviewing the TDP. *Source: CCC responds to Government's Transport Decarbonisation Plan, Climate Change Committee, 14 July 2021. https://www.theccc.org.uk/2021/07/14/ccc-responds-to-governments-transport-decarbonisation-plan/

### Modal shift as alternative to technology-only decarbonisation

The TDP explicitly states: "We cannot simply believe that zero emission cars and lorries will meet all our climate goals or solve all our problems. They will not, particularly in reaching the medium-term Sixth Carbon Budget targets." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf The plan commits to modal shift from road to rail for freight: "We will incentivise the early take up of low carbon traction for rail freight" and "We will introduce a rail freight growth target." *Source: Decarbonising Transport: A Better, Greener Britain, Department for Transport, July 2021. https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/1009448/decarbonising-transport-a-better-greener-britain.pdf

*Analytical inference:* workspaces with cargo verticals capable of tolerating longer transit times may find rail freight increasingly cost-competitive as road freight costs rise under RTFO increases and HGV ZEV mandates.

### Industry multi-fuel position

Industry consultation responses on HGV decarbonisation indicate support for a technology-neutral approach: "For Option 1 to deliver its full potential, it is essential that the regulatory framework gives appropriate recognition to LCF." *Source: HGV decarbonisation: Industry responds to government consultation on zero emission targets, Motor Transport, 2 April 2026. https://motortransport.co.uk/energy/industry-backs-multi-pronged-approach-to-hgv-decarbonisation-regulation/89817.article

*Industry interpretation:* this multi-fuel position reflects a genuine transition-period reality for heavy freight; workspaces evaluating carrier partners' decarbonisation credentials should treat low-carbon fuel adoption as a credible near-term pathway alongside battery-electric and hydrogen options.

### Independent policy tracking

An industry intelligence tool tracks UK transport decarbonisation policy on an ongoing basis. *Source: UK transport decarbonisation policy tracker, Innovate UK Business Connect. https://iuk-business-connect.org.uk/perspectives/decarbonisation-policy-tracker/

*Operational implication:* workspaces routing UK-lane freight should treat this and equivalent trackers as a monitoring supplement to the primary government sources cited throughout this brief, not as a substitute for them.

metadata.what_is_it: The UK Government's Transport Decarbonisation Plan (TDP), a strategy document published 14 July 2021 setting a pathway to net zero transport by 2050, and its binding implementing instruments including the Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) Mandate (effective 2025) and the Zero Emission Vehicle (ZEV) Mandate for LGVs.
metadata.why_matters: The SAF Mandate directly binds aviation fuel suppliers from 2025 and the ZEV Mandate sets a 70 percent zero-emission sales target for LGVs by 2030; both raise the cost base of UK air and road freight that flows through to freight-forwarding clients, while HGV phase-out dates remain proposals subject to consultation rather than binding law.
key_data: SAF Mandate blend trajectory 2% in 2025 rising to 10% in 2030 and 22% in 2040
SAF buy-out price GBP 4.70 per litre main obligation and GBP 5 per litre PtL obligation
ZEV Mandate LGV sales target 70% zero-emission by 2030
RTFO main obligation rising from 9.6% in 2021 to 14.6% in 2032
HGV phase-out proposals 2035 for under 26 tonnes and 2040 for above 26 tonnes; subject to consultation
metadata.cost_mechanism: Aviation fuel suppliers meeting the SAF Mandate registration threshold blend an increasing percentage of sustainable aviation fuel each year or pay a per-litre buy-out price; both routes raise supplier cost, which passes through in carrier fuel surcharges to air freight pricing.

steps.label: Strategy document sets non-binding policy pathway to net zero transport by 2050
SAF Mandate enters force at 2% of total UK jet fuel demand
SAF blend reaches 10%; ZEV Mandate LGV sales target reaches 70% zero-emission
RTFO main obligation reaches its increased target under the plan's commitment
SAF blend obligation reaches its ceiling pending further supply certainty
Terminal policy horizon for UK domestic transport emissions

requirement_trajectory.note: HGV phase-out dates of 2035 (under 26 tonnes) and 2040 (above 26 tonnes) remain proposals subject to consultation and are not yet binding statute

metadata.penalty_range: civil penalties in line with current penalties under the RTFO, applied to aviation fuel suppliers rather than directly to freight forwarders
metadata.enforcement_body: The Department for Transport administers the SAF Mandate and RTFO; no enforcement mechanism in the captured corpus runs directly against a freight forwarder acting as intermediary
