entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Council Decision 84/358/EEC, by which the European Economic Community approved and became a Contracting Party to the Bonn Agreement, the 1983 multilateral treaty for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances. It exists to give a freight forwarder with North Sea shipping or aviation exposure a single place to see which duties the Agreement places directly on ship masters and aircraft pilots, which duties run only between the Contracting Party governments, and when the Agreement's own provisions take effect.

FACT: "84/358/EEC: Council Decision of 28 June 1984 concerning the conclusion of the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "The Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances is hereby approved on behalf of the European Economic Community." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Decision Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "Done at Luxembourg, 28 June 1984." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances, was signed on 13 September 1983" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Decision recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

**What the workspace should expect to decide:** whether the workspace itself, or a vessel or aircraft it charters or operates, flies the flag of or is registered in a Contracting Party to the Bonn Agreement (Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, or the United Kingdom), since that determines whether the master or pilot reporting duty in Section 8 applies directly.

*Analytical inference:* this Decision and the Agreement it approves are both from the 1980s and remain the governing North Sea pollution-cooperation instrument for those Contracting Parties; there is no indication in the captured text of a later withdrawal or replacement.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

The Bonn Agreement is a mutual-assistance and information-exchange treaty among coastal states of the North Sea (plus the European Economic Community as a Contracting Party in its own right), not a directly enforceable EU regulation on private undertakings.

FACT: "This Agreement shall apply whenever the presence or the prospective presence of oil or other harmful substances polluting or threatening to pollute the sea within the North Sea area, as defined in Article 2 of this Agreement, presents a grave and imminent danger to the coast or related interests of one or more Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* the Agreement applies to the workspace directly only through the specific master-and-pilot reporting duty described in Section 8; the rest of the Agreement's cooperation, cost-sharing, and governance provisions run between the Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community, not between those governments and a private freight forwarder.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Analytical inference:* this Agreement has no forward-looking action item running to a private party as of the export date beyond the standing reporting duty described in Section 8; the captured text states no recurring compliance deadline of its own for a freight forwarder.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

*Legal Confirmation Required:* the Agreement's cooperation, notification, cost-reimbursement, and governance duties described in Section 8 run between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community; only the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2) names a private-sector actor directly, and whether a specific workspace vessel or aircraft is captured by it is a fact-specific, flag-and-registration question outside this brief's scope.

*Analytical inference:* a workspace operating vessels flagged in, or aircraft registered in, one of the eight named Contracting Parties sits inside this Agreement's reporting chain for North Sea incidents; a workspace with no such flagged or registered assets sits outside it entirely.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Upon the entry into force of this Agreement the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil, done at Bonn on 9 June 1969, shall cease to be in force." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Per the workspace's reading:* this 1983 Bonn Agreement is the controlling instrument, superseding the original 1969 Bonn Agreement referenced in this Decision's own recitals; a workspace should not rely on the 1969 text as current.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

*Analytical inference:* no forward events are recorded for this item in the export this brief was authored from, and the captured text states no scheduled future event beyond the standing meeting and review cycle described in Section 8 (obligation 9), which runs between Contracting Parties rather than being a scheduled event a workspace itself must track.

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does this Agreement create a duty directly on a freight-forwarding intermediary?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Only one duty in the captured text names a private-sector actor: the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2). Every other duty described in Section 8 runs between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community.

**Q2: What must a ship master or aircraft pilot do if North Sea pollution is detected?**

*Operational implication:* Section 8 (obligation 2) describes the duty to report without delay through the most practicable channel; Section 8 (obligation 3) describes the standard reporting form the Contracting Parties must establish for this purpose.

**Q3: Is there any penalty or compliance deadline running to a freight forwarder under this Agreement?**

*Legal Confirmation Required:* No. See Section 8's required-slot coverage note below; this Agreement's own text states no penalty provision and no fixed compliance deadline running to any private party.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

*Note: this is a multilateral cooperation Agreement, not a directly enforceable regulation. "Substantive requirements" here means the Agreement's own stated duties, most of which run between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community rather than to a private party; only obligation 2 below names ship masters and aircraft pilots directly.*

**1. Geographic and triggering scope.** FACT: "This Agreement shall apply whenever the presence or the prospective presence of oil or other harmful substances polluting or threatening to pollute the sea within the North Sea area, as defined in Article 2 of this Agreement, presents a grave and imminent danger to the coast or related interests of one or more Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 1. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* a workspace's own North Sea shipping or aviation activity sits inside this scope whenever a grave and imminent pollution danger is present, regardless of which Contracting Party's zone it occurs in.

**2. Master-and-pilot reporting duty.** FACT: "The Contracting Parties undertake to request the masters of all ships flying their flags and pilots of aircraft registered in their countries to report without delay through the channels which may be most practicable and adequate in the circumstances" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 5(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this is the one duty in the captured text that names a private-sector actor (a ship's master, an aircraft's pilot) directly; whether it applies to a specific workspace vessel or aircraft depends on its flag state or country of registration being one of the eight named Contracting Parties.

**3. Standard reporting form.** FACT: "The Contracting Parties shall establish a standard form for the reporting of pollution as required under paragraph 1 of this Article." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 5(3). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* this is a duty on the Contracting Parties to create the form masters and pilots would use under obligation 2 above; it does not itself bind a private operator, but it shapes the mechanics of the reporting duty that does.

**4. National-organization notification duty.** FACT: "Contracting Parties undertake to inform the other Contracting Parties about" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 4. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this obligation runs between Contracting Party governments; it does not itself bind a freight forwarder, though the competent authority it identifies is the body a workspace vessel would report to under obligation 2.

**5. Cost-reimbursement mechanic for mutual assistance.** FACT: "if the action was taken by one Contracting Party at the express request of another Contracting Party, the Contracting Party requesting such assistance shall reimburse to the assisting Contracting Party the costs of its action" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 9(1)(a). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this cost-allocation duty runs between Contracting Party governments; the captured text states no mechanism by which a private vessel operator or freight forwarder would be charged directly under this Article.

**6. Annual expenditure contribution and cap.** FACT: "Each Contracting Party shall contribute 2,5 % towards the annual expenditure of the Agreement. The ballance of the Agreement's expenditure shall be divided among Contracting Parties other than the European Economic Community in proportion to their gross national product in accordance with the scale of assessment adopted regularly by the United Nations General Assembly. In no case shall the contribution of a Contracting Party to this balance exceed 20 % of the balance." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 15(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this funding formula runs between Contracting Party governments and the European Economic Community; it does not itself impose a levy on a private freight forwarder.

**7. Non-prejudice safeguard.** FACT: "The provisions of this Agreement shall not be interpreted as in any way prejudicing the rights and obligations of the Contracting Parties under international law, especially in the field of the prevention and combating of marine pollution." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 8(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this preserves each Contracting Party's own existing international-law rights and obligations; it does not itself alter a private party's rights under other marine-pollution instruments.

**8. Agreement entry-into-force condition.** FACT: "This Agreement shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the Governments of all the States mentioned in Article 18 of this Agreement and the European Economic Community have signed the Agreement without reservation as to ratification, acceptance or approval." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* the Agreement's own entry into force is conditional on unanimous, unreserved signature by all nine named parties (the eight States plus the European Economic Community) rather than tied to a single fixed calendar date; a workspace should treat this Decision's own 28 June 1984 approval as the European Economic Community's own side of that condition, not proof that the whole Agreement was already in force on that date.

**9. Amendment entry-into-force mechanic.** FACT: "Such an amendment shall enter into force on the first day of the second month following the date on which the Depositary Government has received notifications of approval from all Contracting Parties." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 16(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this governs future amendments to the Agreement or its Annex; it does not itself impose a duty on a private party, but it is the mechanism by which the geographic zones and duties described elsewhere in Section 8 could change.

**10. Denunciation term and delay.** FACT: "1. After this Agreement has been in force for five years it may be denounced by any Contracting Party. 2. Denunciation shall be effected by a notification in writing addressed to the Depositary Government which shall notify all the other Contracting Parties of any denunciation received and of the date of its receipt. 3. A denunciation shall take effect one year after its receipt by the Depositary Government." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 22. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this five-year minimum term plus one-year denunciation delay runs between Contracting Party governments; a workspace has no denunciation right of its own under this Article.

**Required-slot coverage: penalty and primary deadline.** No penalty, fine, or sanction provision naming any party is stated anywhere in this Agreement's operative text (Articles 1 to 24) or its Annex; the cost provisions above (obligations 5 and 6) address reimbursement and expenditure-sharing between Contracting Party governments, not a penalty running to any party. No compliance deadline running to a private party is stated in Articles 1 to 24 either: the one duty naming a private-sector actor (obligation 2, Article 5(2)) requires reporting "without delay" rather than by a fixed date, and every dated mechanic in the Agreement (obligation 8's entry into force, obligation 9's amendment entry into force, obligation 10's denunciation) runs between Contracting Party governments and the Depositary Government, never to a private party.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED (see metadata.requirement_trajectory: signature at Bonn on 13 September 1983, EEC approval by this Decision on 28 June 1984, conditional entry into force under obligation 8, a five-year minimum term before denunciation under obligation 10, and a further one-year delay before a denunciation takes effect; no phase-in of the reporting duty itself is stated). Exceptions and carve-outs: no exception or carve-out language is stated in the captured text; No exceptions are stated in Articles 1 to 24 of this Agreement. Scope limits: no scope-limiting language beyond the geographic and triggering scope captured in obligation 1 is stated; No scope limits are stated in Articles 1 to 24 of this Agreement, and the geographic trigger in obligation 1 does not exclude or limit any Contracting Party's own obligations.

Obligations surveyed: 10; workspace-adjacent: 4; extracted as FACT: 10.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Not addressed: this Agreement is a government-to-government cooperation treaty and defines no product-specific compliance category a freight forwarder's cargo could fall into; the captured text (Articles 1 to 24 and the Annex) states no product, cargo, or commodity classification of any kind.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "the competent authority responsible for receiving and dispatching reports of such pollution and for dealing with questions concerning measures of mutual assistance between Contracting Parties" *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 4(b). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Operational implication:* a workspace vessel or aircraft covered by the master-and-pilot reporting duty (Section 8, obligation 2) reports to this competent authority, using the standard form each Contracting Party is required to establish under Article 5(3) (Section 8, obligation 3).

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Note: this Agreement creates no technical system of its own beyond the reporting channel and standard form already described in Section 8 and Section 10; "operational system requirements" here means the monitoring a workspace should maintain if it operates flagged or registered assets in a Contracting Party.*

**1. Flag and registration check.** *Operational implication:* a workspace should confirm whether any vessel it operates flies the flag of, or any aircraft it operates is registered in, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, or the United Kingdom, since only those flags and registrations bring the master-and-pilot reporting duty into play.

**2. Incident-reporting channel.** *Operational implication:* a workspace with in-scope assets should have a process for its masters and pilots to report North Sea oil or harmful-substance incidents without delay, per Section 8 (obligation 2).

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "The Contracting Parties may unanimously invite any other coastal State of the north-east Atlantic area to accede to this Agreement." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 20(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

FACT: "Two or more Contracting Parties may modify the common boundaries of their zones described in the Annex to this Agreement." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 17(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* both mechanisms can change which states and which zones the Agreement covers; a workspace should not treat the eight named Contracting Parties or the Annex's own zone boundaries as permanently fixed.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Upon the entry into force of this Agreement the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil, done at Bonn on 9 June 1969, shall cease to be in force." *Source: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358, Agreement Article 19(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358

*Analytical inference:* the original 1969 Bonn Agreement is the direct predecessor this 1983 Agreement replaces; a workspace researching the history of North Sea pollution cooperation should treat the 1983 text, not the 1969 text, as the operative instrument the European Economic Community itself joined.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 9 June 1969: the original Bonn Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil was signed, later superseded by this 1983 Agreement.
- 13 September 1983: the Agreement for cooperation in dealing with pollution of the North Sea by oil and other harmful substances was signed at Bonn.
- 28 June 1984: the Council of the European Communities adopted Decision 84/358/EEC, approving the Agreement on behalf of the European Economic Community.

*Source for timeline entries: EUR-Lex, CELEX 31984D0358 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:31984D0358).*

# 15. Sources

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Canada's Clean Fuel Regulations (SOR/2022-140), which require liquid fossil fuel suppliers to gradually reduce the carbon intensity of the gasoline and diesel they produce and sell for use in Canada. It covers the obligations that fall on primary suppliers, registered creators, foreign suppliers and carbon-intensity contributors, and the workspace-facing consequences for freight forwarders and carriers who purchase or rely on those fuels in Canada. Monetary figures below are Canadian dollars (CA$) unless otherwise noted.

FACT: "The goal of the Clean Fuel Regulations is to significantly reduce pollution by making the fuels we use every day cleaner over time." *Source: What are the Clean Fuel Regulations?, Environment and Climate Change Canada. https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/managing-pollution/energy-production/fuel-regulations/clean-fuel-regulations/about.html

FACT: "The Clean Fuel Regulations will deliver up to 26 million tonnes (Mt) of GHG emissions reductions in 2030." *Source: What are the Clean Fuel Regulations?, Environment and Climate Change Canada. https://www.canada.ca/en/environment-climate-change/services/managing-pollution/energy-production/fuel-regulations/clean-fuel-regulations/about.html

*Operational implication:* the Regulations do not regulate freight forwarders directly. They regulate the fuel supply chain that feeds a workspace's Canada-lane operations, so the practical exposure runs through fuel cost, fuel availability, and carrier-level carbon-intensity data rather than through a direct compliance obligation on the workspace itself.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "primary supplier primary supplier means a person who (a) owns, leases, operates, controls or manages a fuel production facility in Canada at which gasoline or diesel is produced; or (b) imports gasoline or diesel into Canada." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "foreign supplier foreign supplier means the owner of a facility outside Canada at which a low-carbon-intensity fuel is produced or the person who leases, operates, controls or manages such a facility." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "registered creator registered creator means a person registered with the Minister in accordance with subsection 25(1)." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "carbon-intensity contributor carbon-intensity contributor means a person who applies for the approval of a carbon intensity under subsection 80(1) for a set of activities carried out over the life cycle of a fuel in the liquid class or a low-carbon-intensity fuel with the intention to transfer the approved carbon intensity to a registered creator or foreign supplier or to another carbon-intensity contributor." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "compliance period compliance period means (a) the period that begins on the day on which these Regulations are registered and ends on December 31, 2022; (b) the period that begins on January 1, 2023 and ends on June 30, 2023; (c) the period that begins on July 1, 2023 and ends on December 31, 2023; or (d) after December 31, 2023, each calendar year." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: "makes the annexed Clean Fuel Regulations under sections 140 Footnote c and 326 and subsection 330(2) of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 Footnote b and subsection 5(1) of the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act Footnote d ." *Source: Order Fixing the Coming into Force of the Clean Fuel Regulations, Canada Gazette Part II, Vol. 156, No. 14. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

*Operational implication:* a workspace is not itself a primary supplier, registered creator, foreign supplier or carbon-intensity contributor unless it directly produces or imports gasoline or diesel into Canada in the covered volumes, or directly creates compliance credits. The obligations above bind fuel producers, importers and credit creators in the supply chain that a freight-forwarding workspace purchases from.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any role the workspace occupies (fuel importer, bunkering intermediary, bulk fuel purchaser) meets the "imports gasoline or diesel into Canada" branch of the primary supplier definition requires counsel review on the workspace's own fuel-handling activity.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a fuel that is produced in Canada or imported into Canada before July 1, 2023." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 5(4), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* the carbon-intensity reduction obligation on primary suppliers' pools of gasoline and diesel has been in effect since July 1, 2023; this is a live, ongoing compliance regime, not a future obligation.

FACT: "A carbon intensity determined in accordance with any of sections 76 to 79 that was approved by the Minister before July 1, 2024 ceases to be valid on December 31, 2025. The registered creator, carbon-intensity contributor or foreign supplier may, on or after July 1, 2024, submit a new application to the Minister for the approval of the carbon intensity under subsection 80(1)." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 86(9), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

*Operational implication:* registered creators, carbon-intensity contributors and foreign suppliers whose carbon-intensity approvals were granted before July 1, 2024 faced an approval-expiry event on December 31, 2025. A workspace relying on such a party's fuel-supply carbon-intensity data for its own Scope 3 reporting should confirm whether the underlying approval was renewed.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The Clean Fuel Regulations are a company-level, supply-chain compliance regime; the covered entities are primary suppliers, registered creators, foreign suppliers and carbon-intensity contributors, not freight forwarders acting as intermediaries.

FACT: "The regulations will also establish a credit market whereby the annual CI reduction requirement could be met via three main categories of credit-creating actions: (1) actions that reduce the CI of the fossil fuel throughout its lifecycle, (2) supplying low-carbon fuels, and (3) supplying fuel and energy in advanced vehicle technologies." *Source: Order Fixing the Coming into Force of the Clean Fuel Regulations, Canada Gazette Part II, Vol. 156, No. 14. https://gazette.gc.ca/rp-pr/p2/2022/2022-07-06/html/sor-dors140-eng.html

*Operational implication:* compliance costs incurred by fuel suppliers and credit creators under this credit market are likely to be reflected in the price of gasoline and diesel purchased by carriers and, in turn, in freight pricing on Canada lanes; workspace clients operating under disclosure frameworks that request Scope 3 fuel-related emissions data may separately request carbon-intensity information from Canadian fuel suppliers or carrier partners.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Fuel LCA Model Fuel LCA Model means the fuel life-cycle assessment model that is developed by the Minister in accordance with ISO Standard 14040 and that consists of the procedures that must be followed to determine the carbon intensity of a fuel, energy source or material input using life-cycle inventories for various pathways." *Source: Clean Fuel Regulations SOR/2022-140, s. 1(1), Department of Justice Canada. https://laws-lois.justice.gc.ca/eng/regulations/SOR-2022-140/FullText.html

FACT: the Fuel LCA Model saw "the Jan 2025 release of Version 4.0 Fuel LCA Model" *Source: IETA Business Brief, Canada Clean Fuel Regulation (CFR), IETA/cKinetics, September 2025. https://www.ieta.org/uploads/wp-content/2025/09/IETA_Business_Brief-Canada-Clean-Fuel-Regilation-CFR-September_2025finalone.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the Fuel LCA Model is the technical calculation methodology underlying every carbon-intensity figure in this brief; periodic model updates (such as the Version 4.0 release) can change how a given pathway's carbon intensity is calculated without changing the Regulations' own text, so a workspace tracking carbon-intensity claims from a Canadian fuel or credit supplier should confirm which model version was used.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

metadata.what_is_it: Canada's Clean Fuel Regulations (SOR/2022-140), a federal fuel-supply carbon-intensity reduction regime requiring gasoline and diesel primary suppliers to reduce the carbon intensity of the fuel they produce or import into Canada by approximately 15 percent below 2016 levels by 2030, administered through a compliance credit market.
metadata.why_matters: The Regulations govern the fuel-supply chain feeding a workspace's Canada-lane operations rather than the workspace itself; compliance costs and carbon-intensity data generated by primary suppliers and registered creators are likely to be reflected in fuel pricing and in Scope 3 emissions data requests from clients operating under disclosure frameworks.
key_data: carbon intensity reduction of approximately 15 percent below 2016 levels by 2030
up to 26 million tonnes of GHG emissions reductions delivered in 2030
400 cubic metre per compliance period de minimis threshold for primary supplier obligations
2024 average compliance credit price CA $157
credit clearance ceiling price formula CPI-indexed from a $300 base
metadata.cost_mechanism: Primary suppliers who cannot meet their annual reduction requirement through fuel-supply carbon intensity alone acquire or create compliance credits in a market whose 2024 average price was CA $157 per credit, or contribute to a registered emission-reduction funding program at a formula-based rate; these costs flow into gasoline and diesel pricing for fuel purchasers, including carriers on Canada lanes.

steps.label: Clean Fuel Regulations (SOR/2022-140) registered and made
carbon-intensity reduction and volumetric requirements become effective for primary suppliers
carbon-intensity approvals granted before July 1, 2024 cease to be valid
default carbon-intensity schedule reaches its lowest scheduled level; Regulations' own reduction target is measured against this year

requirement_trajectory.note: the default carbon intensity for unapproved pathways is set on a stated per-year schedule from 2022 through 2030 and following years under Section 8; no source in this brief's corpus states a schedule change beyond 2030

metadata.penalty_range: administrative monetary penalties (AMPs) issued under the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Regulations for certain violations; no maximum or per-violation dollar figure for this instrument was located in the captured source text
metadata.enforcement_body: Environment and Climate Change Canada administers and enforces the Clean Fuel Regulations under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 and the Environmental Violations Administrative Monetary Penalties Act; no enforcement mechanism in the captured corpus runs directly against a freight forwarder acting as an intermediary

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the International Maritime Organization's (IMO) Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) and Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) mandatory carbon intensity requirements, adopted as amendments to MARPOL Annex VI. Regulations in force from 1 November 2022; certification and reporting requirements effective from 1 January 2023; CII reduction factors through 2030 set by resolution MEPC.400(83); SEEMP Part III revision deadline December 31, 2025; IMO Phase 2 review running Spring 2026 to Spring 2028.

**Transport mode scope:** This document applies exclusively to ocean transport. EEXI and CII are ship level regulations under IMO and MARPOL authority. They do not apply to air, road, or rail freight.

**Who should read this document:** operations leads assessing ocean freight carrier selection and procurement; commercial leadership negotiating ocean freight contracts; legal counsel reviewing compliance obligations and contract exposure.

**Convention note:** binding obligation language in this document is either (a) a direct FACT quoted from source content, (b) labeled *Analytical inference:*, *Industry interpretation:*, or *Operational implication:*, or (c) routed to a *Legal Confirmation Required:* callout. No unlabeled binding assertion appears.

FACT: "Amendments to the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL) Annex VI enter into force on 1 November 2022." *Source: Rules on ship carbon intensity and rating system enter into force, IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "The Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) is a technical measure that assesses the energy efficiency of existing ships over 400 gross tonnage (GT). It requires vessels to meet a specific energy efficiency baseline, calculated based on their design." *Source: EEXI and CII, 2025 Guide to Shipping's Sustainability Regulations, Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

FACT: "The Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) measures the operational carbon intensity of ships over 5,000 GT. It quantifies annual CO₂ emissions per tonne-mile, rating vessels from A (best) to E (worst). Ships must achieve at least a C rating; those rated D for three consecutive years or E in any year must submit a corrective action plan." *Source: EEXI and CII, 2025 Guide to Shipping's Sustainability Regulations, Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

FACT: "From 1 January 2023 it will be mandatory for all ships to calculate their attained Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) to measure their energy efficiency and to initiate the collection of data for the reporting of their annual operational carbon intensity indicator (CII) and CII rating." *Source: Rules on ship carbon intensity and rating system enter into force, IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

FACT: "As a stimulus to reduce carbon intensity of all ships by 40% by 2030 compared to 2008 baseline, ships will be required to calculate two ratings: their attained Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) to determine their energy efficiency, and their annual operational Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and associated CII rating." *Source: Rules on ship carbon intensity and rating system enter into force, IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

*Operational implication:* the workspace does not own or operate ships. EEXI and CII obligations bind vessel owners and operators directly under MARPOL Annex VI. CII ratings are, however, increasingly embedded in ocean carrier selection, charter party terms, and client sustainability reporting, which makes this regulation operationally and commercially material for a freight forwarder even without a direct statutory obligation.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace, acting as freight forwarder or importer of record rather than vessel owner or operator, bears any direct MARPOL Annex VI compliance obligation under the EEXI or CII frameworks requires counsel review.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

## COST ALERT: CII reduction factor tightens annually through 2030

FACT: "A 2% reduction factor will be applied every year from 5% in 2023 reaching 11% by 2026, with further reduction figures for 2027 to 2030 under development." *Source: CII ratings announced, Infineum Insight, 4 March 2025. https://www.infineuminsight.com/en-gb/articles/cii-ratings-announced/

FACT, reduction factor table from resolution MEPC.400(83) (adopted 11 April 2025): "Table 1: Reduction factor (Z%) for the CII relative to the 2019 reference line Year Reduction factor relative to 2019 2023 5% 2024 7% 2025 9% 2026 11% 2027 13.625% 2028 16.250% 2029 18.875% 2030 21.500%" *Source: Resolution MEPC.400(83), Amendments to the 2021 Guidelines on the operational carbon intensity reduction factors relative to reference lines (CII reduction factors guidelines, G3), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.400(83).pdf

*Operational implication:* carriers facing D or E ratings under the tightening reduction factor may pass compliance costs into freight rates as carbon surcharges or fuel adjustment factors. The workspace should request CII rating transparency from ocean carriers before booking, particularly on long-haul routes where older tonnage is more likely to be represented.

## WINDOW: SEEMP Part III revision deadline, December 31, 2025

FACT: "All ships must update their SEEMP Part III by December 31, 2025, to comply with new IMO CII reduction targets." *Source: Class News 13/2025, New IMO CII Guidelines require SEEMP Part III revisions, Lloyd's Register, 18 July 2025. https://www.lr.org/en/knowledge/class-news/13-25/

*Operational implication:* this deadline binds vessel owners and operators, not freight forwarders. A carrier that failed to revise its SEEMP Part III by December 31, 2025 faces a compliance gap from 1 January 2026 forward; the workspace should confirm current SEEMP Part III status with its primary ocean carriers as a booking-risk check.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Under the EEXI framework , all existing ships of 400 GT and above are required to calculate their attained Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI)" *Source: Improving the Energy Efficiency of Ships, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/improving%20the%20energy%20efficiency%20of%20ships.aspx

FACT: "CII is mandatory for ships of 5,000 gross tonnage and above." *Source: Improving the Energy Efficiency of Ships, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/ourwork/environment/pages/improving%20the%20energy%20efficiency%20of%20ships.aspx

The direct compliance chain runs flag Administration to vessel owner or operator to classification society or Recognized Organization (RO). The workspace, acting as freight forwarder, sits outside this statutory chain.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's role as importer or shipper of record on a given ocean shipment creates any derivative MARPOL Annex VI obligation, for example through charter party terms or national implementing legislation in flag or port states, requires counsel review.

*Analytical inference:* the workspace's primary exposure is commercial and reputational, not statutory: client contracts requiring low carbon logistics, Scope 3 emissions reporting where the CII rating of the carrier affects the workspace's reported transport emissions, and carrier selection liability where a D or E rated carrier creates an audit finding.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "MEPC 83 adopted resolution MEPC.400(83) on Amendments to the 2021 Guidelines on the operational carbon intensity reduction factors relative to reference lines (CII reduction factors guidelines, G3) (resolution MEPC.338(76) )." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

FACT: "Table 1: Reduction factor (Z%) for the CII relative to the 2019 reference line Year Reduction factor relative to 2019 2023 5% 2024 7% 2025 9% 2026 11% 2027 13.625% 2028 16.250% 2029 18.875% 2030 21.500%" *Source: Resolution MEPC.400(83), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.400(83).pdf

FACT: "Further amendments to MARPOL Annex VI (IMO Resolution MEPC.328(76)) were adopted at 76th session of the IMO’s Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC 76) in 2021, and the CII rating is introduced from 1 January 2023 based on the annual fuel consumption of each ship." *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html

FACT: "MEPC 76 (June 2021) adopted, by resolution MEPC. 328(76), amendments to MARPOL Annex VI introducing the short-term GHG reduction measure containing a technical Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI), an operational Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and an enhanced Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)" *Source: Resolution MEPC.377(80), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.377(80).pdf

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

## MONITORING: MEPC 84, draft amendments to MARPOL Annex VI regulation 27

FACT: "MEPC 83 also approved draft amendments to regulation 27 of MARPOL Annex VI. These amendments are expected to be adopted at MEPC 84 in May 2026." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Analytical inference:* amendments to regulation 27 may alter the reference lines or correction factors used in CII calculations, affecting the ratings earned by carriers the workspace books. The source states these amendments were, as of its capture, expected to be adopted at MEPC 84 in May 2026; whether MEPC 84 in fact adopted them should be reconfirmed against a current IMO record before this item is relied upon for a live decision.

## MONITORING: IMO Phase 2 review, Spring 2026 to Spring 2028

FACT: "Phase 1 of the review was finalized in 2025, which gathered and analyzed data from Member States about their experience in implementing the short-term measures, identifying a list of challenges and gaps. Phase 2 will run from Spring 2026 to Spring 2028, to further develop the SEEMP framework and metrics." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Analytical inference:* Phase 2 outputs are the primary source of forward regulatory risk for the SEEMP framework and CII metrics through 2028. Potential outcomes include revised reduction factors, enhanced enforcement mechanisms, or new corrective action triggers.

## MONITORING: IMO Net-Zero Framework and GHG Fuel Intensity mechanism

FACT: "The IMO’s Marine Environment Protection Committee met from April 27 to May 1, 2026, with further discussion expected at its Second Extraordinary Session on December 4, 2026, subject to confirmation by MEPC 85." *Source: The New IMO Carbon Rules in 2026, Across the Ocean Shipping, 11 May 2026. https://atoshipping.com/the-new-imo-carbon-rules-in-2026-how-sea-freight-compliance-is-affecting-global-shipping-costs/

FACT: "Proposed remedial unit prices include $380 and $100 per tonne for 2028 to 2030, with future pricing subject to review." *Source: The New IMO Carbon Rules in 2026, Across the Ocean Shipping, 11 May 2026. https://atoshipping.com/the-new-imo-carbon-rules-in-2026-how-sea-freight-compliance-is-affecting-global-shipping-costs/

*Analytical inference:* the GHG Fuel Intensity (GFI) based IMO Net-Zero Framework, if adopted, would layer a fuel pricing mechanism on top of CII and EEXI. The remedial unit prices stated are proposed figures, subject to review, and the framework had not been formally adopted as of the date of this source.

**Forward event on record:** As a stimulus to reduce carbon intensity of all ships by 40% by 2030 compared to 2008 baseline, ships will be required to calculate two ratings: their attained Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) to determine their energy efficiency, and their annual operational Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and associated CII rating. This 2030 target date is the long-term horizon against which the annual CII reduction factors above are set.

# 7. Threshold Questions

## Decided Questions

**Q1: Does EEXI apply to the workspace's ocean carriers?**
FACT: "It must be calculated for ships of 400 gt and above, in accordance with the different values set for ship types and size categories." *Source: Rules on ship carbon intensity and rating system enter into force, IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx All ocean carriers booking cargo for the workspace operate vessels well above 400 GT. **Decided: yes, EEXI applies to the carriers the workspace books.**

**Q2: Does CII apply to the workspace's ocean carriers?**
FACT: "The CII applies to ships above 5,000 GT of the following ships types: bulk carriers, gas carriers, tankers, container ships, general cargo ships, refrigerated cargo carriers, combination carriers, LNG carriers, vehicle carriers, Ro-Ro cargo vessels, Ro-Ro passenger vessels and cruise ships." *Source: CII, Carbon Intensity Indicator, Sustainable Ships. https://www.sustainable-ships.org/rules-regulations/cii Standard container vessels, Ro-Ro carriers, and general cargo vessels used on the workspace's trade lanes fall within these named ship types. **Decided: yes, CII applies to the carriers the workspace books.**

**Q3: Does EEXI or CII apply directly to the workspace as a freight forwarder?**
EEXI and CII impose obligations on shipowners and operators under MARPOL Annex VI, not on cargo interests or freight forwarders. **Decided: no direct statutory obligation identified in the captured sources.** *Legal Confirmation Required:* whether charter party terms or specific national port state legislation on the workspace's trade lanes could create a derivative obligation on the workspace as shipper or importer of record.

## Questions Requiring Legal Confirmation

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether EU ETS obligations, which extend to maritime transport on EU connected voyages, interact with CII obligations to create dual reporting or cost pass through requirements on freight forwarders booking cargo on EU connected routes.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether BIMCO CII clauses or equivalent charter party terms between the workspace's ocean carriers and their charterers create indirect cost pass through liability to the workspace as a beneficial cargo owner or sub-charterer.

# 8. Substantive Requirements

## EEXI Requirements: Ship Design Efficiency

**1. Applicability threshold.** FACT: "It must be calculated for ships of 400 gt and above, in accordance with the different values set for ship types and size categories." *Source: IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

**2. Definition and scope.** FACT: "The Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) is a technical measure that assesses the energy efficiency of existing ships over 400 gross tonnage (GT). It requires vessels to meet a specific energy efficiency baseline, calculated based on their design." *Source: Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

**3. Compliance mechanism.** FACT: "Compliance is verified through a one-time certification process, and ships must have an approved EEXI technical file and a compliant EEXI value to receive an International Energy Efficiency Certificate (IEEC)." *Source: Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

**4. Ongoing stability.** FACT: "EEXI requirements are stable, with no major changes expected." *Source: Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

## CII Requirements: Operational Carbon Intensity

**5. Applicability threshold and scope limit.** FACT: "The CII applies to ships above 5,000 GT of the following ships types: bulk carriers, gas carriers, tankers, container ships, general cargo ships, refrigerated cargo carriers, combination carriers, LNG carriers, vehicle carriers, Ro-Ro cargo vessels, Ro-Ro passenger vessels and cruise ships." *Source: Sustainable Ships. https://www.sustainable-ships.org/rules-regulations/cii

**6. Rating scale and minimum standard.** FACT: "Based on a ship's CII, its carbon intensity will be rated A, B, C, D or E (where A is the best). The rating indicates a major superior, minor superior, moderate, minor inferior, or inferior performance level." *Source: IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

**7. Corrective action trigger and penalty consequence.** FACT: "A ship rated D for three consecutive years, or E for one year, has to submit a corrective action plan to show how the required index of C or above will be achieved." *Source: IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

**8. Annual reporting deadline.** FACT: "Deadline for DCS and CII submission remains unchanged - no later than 31 March each year." *Source: DNV CII Overview. https://www.dnv.com/maritime/insights/topics/CII-carbon-intensity-indicator/

**9. Statement of Compliance retention.** FACT: "The attained annual operational CII and the environmental rating (A to E) will be noted on the DCS Statement of Compliance (SoC), which will be required to be kept on board for five years." *Source: DNV CII Overview. https://www.dnv.com/maritime/insights/topics/CII-carbon-intensity-indicator/

**10. Correction factors and voyage adjustments.** FACT: "Starting in 2024, the CII must be calculated and reported to the Data Collection System (DCS) verifier together with the aggregated DCS data for the previous year, including any correction factors and voyage adjustments." *Source: DNV CII Overview. https://www.dnv.com/maritime/insights/topics/CII-carbon-intensity-indicator/

**11. CII reduction factor trajectory, 2023 to 2030.** FACT, table from resolution MEPC.400(83): "Table 1: Reduction factor (Z%) for the CII relative to the 2019 reference line Year Reduction factor relative to 2019 2023 5% 2024 7% 2025 9% 2026 11% 2027 13.625% 2028 16.250% 2029 18.875% 2030 21.500%" *Source: Resolution MEPC.400(83), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.400(83).pdf

**12. CII reduction factor narrative confirmation.** FACT: "A 2% reduction factor will be applied every year from 5% in 2023 reaching 11% by 2026, with further reduction figures for 2027 to 2030 under development." *Source: Infineum Insight, 4 March 2025. https://www.infineuminsight.com/en-gb/articles/cii-ratings-announced/

**13. First-year CII rating outcomes (2023 reporting data).** FACT: "IMO reports that the first set of data has been submitted by 28,620 ships, with a combined 1,301 million GT. Of those ships, for the 2023 reporting period, 24,653 ships reported operational CII ratings. 78% of the CIIs reported met the ‘C’ or better target. However, 1,541 vessels reported an ‘E’ rating, which means they must now adopt a plan of approved corrective action." *Source: Infineum Insight, 4 March 2025. https://www.infineuminsight.com/en-gb/articles/cii-ratings-announced/

**14. Penalty and enforcement provisions.** FACT: "Penalties for non-compliance could be introduced as part of these measures." *Source: Infineum Insight, 4 March 2025. https://www.infineuminsight.com/en-gb/articles/cii-ratings-announced/

**15. Regulatory review deadline.** FACT: "requires the IMO to review the effectiveness of the implementation of the CII and EEXI requirements, by 1 January 2026 at the latest, and, if necessary, develop and adopt further amendments." *Source: MEPC 76 meeting summary, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/MeetingSummaries/Pages/MEPC76meetingsummary.aspx

**16. Application scope of MARPOL Annex VI (exceptions clause).** FACT: "The provisions of this Annex shall apply to all ships, except where expressly provided otherwise ." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 1, Application, as quoted in EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

**17. SEEMP Part I exemption for non-propelled units and platforms.** FACT: "It is not applied to ships not propelled by mechanical means, and platforms including FPSOs, FSUs and drilling rigs, regardless of their propulsion." *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html

*Analytical inference:* obligations 1 to 4 and 16 to 17 bind EEXI-covered vessels and their statutory exemptions; obligations 5 to 15 bind CII-covered vessels, their annual reporting cycle, and the penalty and enforcement provisions attached to a persistent D or E rating. None of these seventeen obligations state a duty running directly to a freight forwarder, importer, or logistics coordinator; every obligation above runs to the vessel owner, operator, flag Administration, or Recognized Organization.

*Per-year trajectory:* the reduction factor progresses from 5% in 2023 to 21.500% in 2030, phased in annually as set out in obligation 11's table (2027: 13.625%, 2028: 16.250%, 2029: 18.875%, 2030: 21.500%), relative to the 2019 reference line.

*Exceptions and carve-outs:* obligation 16 (MARPOL Annex VI applies to all ships "except where expressly provided otherwise") and obligation 17 (SEEMP Part I is not applied to non-mechanically propelled ships and platforms including FPSOs, FSUs and drilling rigs) are both stated exceptions in the captured source text.

*Scope limit:* obligation 5 states the CII scope limit directly: the CII applies to ships above 5,000 GT of the named ship types listed there; no source in this pool states a scope limit for freight forwarders or cargo intermediaries as such.

Obligations surveyed: 17; workspace-adjacent: 17; extracted as FACT: 17.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*This section applies where the workspace itself operates covered vessels rather than acting purely as an intermediary.*

*Legal Confirmation Required:* if the workspace directly operates a vessel of 400 GT or above (EEXI) or 5,000 GT or above (CII), it is itself a directly covered entity subject to the certification, rating, and reporting obligations in Section 8; this determination requires counsel and vessel-operations review specific to the workspace's own fleet, if any.

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

These obligations bind vessel operators, not freight forwarders. They are documented here because the workspace's carrier selection and contract governance depends on understanding what its carriers must produce.

FACT: "Aggregation of the collected data, calculation of the CII and the CII rating, and reporting to the Administration or an RO - Within three months after the end of each calendar year" *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html

FACT: "In the case of a rating result of E in any year or a rating of D for 3 consecutive years, it is necessary to fill out a corrective action plan in the SEEMP III and submit it to the Administration or an RO. - Within four months after the end of each calendar year" *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html

FACT: "Verification of the reporting data including the CII rating result, verification of the revised SEEMP Part III including a corrective action plan, and issuance of Statement of Compliance by the Administration or an RO - Not later than five months after the end of each calendar year" *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html

FACT: "For 2023, you will need to collect data related to CII, to report fuel consumption data and Attained Operational CII no later than 31 March 2024." *Source: CII requirements explained, timeline, procedures and calculations, qtagg.com, 6 March 2023. https://qtagg.com/2023/03/06/cii-requirements-explained-timeline-procedures-and-calculations/

FACT: "A Statement of Compliance (SoC) is to be issued no later than 31 May 2024," *Source: CII requirements explained, timeline, procedures and calculations, qtagg.com, 6 March 2023. https://qtagg.com/2023/03/06/cii-requirements-explained-timeline-procedures-and-calculations/

*Operational implication:* for workspace carrier partners, the annual reporting cycle runs from calendar-year data collection through a three, four, and five month post-year-end sequence (aggregation and reporting, corrective action plan where triggered, and third-party verification and Statement of Compliance issuance). Carrier-level rating data may not reach the freight forwarder until well into the following calendar year.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* the workspace should build capacity to request and receive CII rating and Statement of Compliance data from ocean carrier partners, since no IMO mechanism in the captured sources mandates that carriers share this data with cargo owners, and this data underpins Scope 3 emissions reporting to clients.

FACT: "The attained annual operational CII and the environmental rating (A to E) will be noted on the DCS Statement of Compliance (SoC), which will be required to be kept on board for five years." *Source: DNV CII Overview. https://www.dnv.com/maritime/insights/topics/CII-carbon-intensity-indicator/

*Operational implication:* the five year on-board retention period for the Statement of Compliance means historical carrier CII performance is, in principle, verifiable on request or via Port State Control inspection records, even where a carrier does not proactively disclose it.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

**EEXI tonnage threshold, smaller vessels.** FACT: "It must be calculated for ships of 400 gt and above, in accordance with the different values set for ship types and size categories." *Source: IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx Vessels below 400 GT are outside EEXI scope.

**CII tonnage threshold, smaller vessels.** FACT: "CII applies to ships 5,000 gross tonnage and above." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx Short-sea, coastal, or feeder vessels below 5,000 GT used for port delivery or island connections may not be subject to CII ratings.

*Operational implication:* for a humanitarian cargo vertical where delivery may involve smaller feeder vessels to remote or island destinations, the CII reporting chain may not cover the final-leg vessel. This is a Scope 3 reporting gap, not a compliance exemption.

**SEEMP Part I exemption for non-propelled units and platforms.** FACT: "It is not applied to ships not propelled by mechanical means, and platforms including FPSOs, FSUs and drilling rigs, regardless of their propulsion." *Source: SEEMP, IMO DCS and CII, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/en/activities/statutory/seemp/index.html Not relevant to the workspace's own cargo operations, but relevant when a workspace transaction involves an offshore-adjacent asset move.

**MARPOL Annex VI general exceptions clause.** FACT: "The provisions of this Annex shall apply to all ships, except where expressly provided otherwise ." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 1, Application, as quoted in EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "To resolve the current situation, best practices may include BIMCO’s CII clauses in charter parties’ contracts. They feature performance-based CII incentives (e.g., bonuses for A/B ratings), driven by regulation, market demand, and ESG accountability." *Source: EEXI and CII, 2025 Guide to Shipping's Sustainability Regulations, Searoutes, 21 October 2025. https://searoutes.com/2025/10/21/eexi-cii-shipping-sustainability-regulations-2026-2028/

*Industry interpretation:* charter party disputes over speed versus rating performance are an early signal that CII compliance cost is already contested commercial ground between owners and charterers; a workspace booking on a charter-linked lane should expect CII performance language to appear in carrier contract terms going forward.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether standard BIMCO CII clauses, or an equivalent, are appropriate for the workspace's specific freight booking arrangements as a forwarder rather than as a charterer requires counsel review.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- June 2021: MEPC 76 adopted, by resolution MEPC.328(76), amendments to MARPOL Annex VI introducing the EEXI and CII short-term GHG reduction measure and an enhanced SEEMP.
- 2018: the measures trace to IMO's commitment under its 2018 Initial Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships, targeting a 40% carbon intensity reduction by 2030 compared to 2008.
- 1 November 2022: MARPOL Annex VI amendments enter into force.
- 1 January 2023: EEXI and CII certification requirements come into effect; data collection for the annual operational CII begins.
- 31 March 2024: first CII and DCS submission deadline, for 2023 reporting year data.
- 31 May 2024: first Statement of Compliance issuance deadline.
- 2024: first CII ratings issued, covering 2023 operating data; 78% of reporting ships met a C rating or better.
- December 31, 2025: SEEMP Part III revision deadline for the 2026 to 2030 reduction factor implementation plan under resolution MEPC.400(83).
- May 2026: MEPC 84, expected adoption of draft MARPOL Annex VI regulation 27 amendments.
- Spring 2026 to Spring 2028: IMO Phase 2 review of the short-term GHG reduction measure, developing the SEEMP framework and metrics further.
- December 4, 2026: IMO Second Extraordinary Session, further discussion of the IMO Net-Zero Framework, subject to confirmation by MEPC 85.
- 2027: 13.625% CII reduction factor relative to the 2019 reference line takes effect.
- 2028: 16.250% CII reduction factor takes effect.
- 2029: 18.875% CII reduction factor takes effect.
- 2030: 21.500% CII reduction factor takes effect; long-term target of a 40% carbon intensity reduction relative to 2008.

FACT: "MEPC 76 (June 2021) adopted, by resolution MEPC. 328(76), amendments to MARPOL Annex VI introducing the short-term GHG reduction measure containing a technical Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI), an operational Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) and an enhanced Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP)" *Source: Resolution MEPC.377(80), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.377(80).pdf

FACT: "The measures are part of IMO's commitment under its 2018 Initial Strategy on Reduction of GHG Emissions from Ships to reduce carbon intensity from all ships by 40% by 2030 compared to 2008." *Source: Rules on ship carbon intensity and rating system enter into force, IMO Press Briefing, 1 November 2022. https://www.imo.org/en/MediaCentre/PressBriefings/pages/CII-and-EEXI-entry-into-force.aspx

FACT: "As the requirements for EEXI and CII certification come into effect on 1 January 2023, the first annual reporting will be completed in 2023, with initial CII ratings given in 2024." *Source: MARPOL Annex VI amendments enter into force, SAFETY4SEA, 1 November 2022. https://safety4sea.com/marpol-annex-vi-amendments-enter-into-force/

metadata.what_is_it: IMO mandatory Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) and Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) carbon intensity requirements under MARPOL Annex VI, applying to existing ships of 400 GT and above (EEXI) and 5000 GT and above (CII), with certification and annual reporting effective from 1 January 2023 and CII reduction factors tightening annually through 2030.
metadata.why_matters: CII ratings are increasingly embedded in ocean carrier selection, charter party terms, and client Scope 3 sustainability reporting; a D or E rated carrier creates carrier selection and disclosure risk for a freight forwarder even though EEXI and CII bind vessel owners and operators, not cargo intermediaries, directly.
key_data: EEXI threshold 400 gross tonnage and above
CII threshold 5000 gross tonnage and above
CII reduction factor 11 percent in 2026 rising to 21.5 percent in 2030 relative to the 2019 reference line
78 percent of 24653 reporting ships met a C rating or better in the first 2023 reporting year
SEEMP Part III revision deadline 31 December 2025
metadata.cost_mechanism: No formal global financial penalty mechanism for CII non-compliance is stated in the captured sources; the consequence for a D rating in three consecutive years or an E rating in any year is a mandatory corrective action plan, with carriers able to pass compliance costs into freight rates as carbon surcharges or fuel adjustment factors ahead of any formal penalty regime.
