entries.body:
## 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This brief covers "Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as regards strengthening the CO2 emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles and integrating reporting obligations, amending Regulation (EU) 2018/858 and repealing Regulation (EU) 2018/956" (Regulation (EU) 2024/1610), Official Journal of the European Union, 6 June 2024. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

This brief is written for workspaces operating road freight transport, managing road-primary fleet operations, or procuring heavy-duty vehicles at scale across EU trade lanes. Convention note, quoted verbatim from the Regulation's own definitions: "“reporting period” means the period from 1 July of a given year to 30 June of the following year". All fleet CO2 targets in this brief are measured against reference periods, not calendar years.

This document surveys the regulation's substantive requirements as they bear on freight-forwarding and logistics workspaces. It does not surveil vehicle type-approval engineering detail (VECTO simulation methodology, technical annex formulae) beyond what is needed to understand the compliance timeline and its downstream effect on road fleet procurement and pricing.

## 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

**FACT (effective_date):** "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 July 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 5, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT (jurisdictional_scope):** "This Regulation shall apply to new vehicles, which have either been type-approved or approved individually under Regulation (EU) 2018/858 or which are referred to in Article 2(3) of that Regulation, and which belong to any of the following vehicle categories: (a) M 2 and M 3 ; (b) N 1 , N 2 and N 3 , provided that the vehicles do not fall under Regulation (EU) 2019/631; (c) O 3 and O 4 ." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(2)(a), amending Article 2(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT:** "Heavy-duty vehicles are currently responsible for more than a quarter of greenhouse gas emissions from road transport in the Union and for over 6 % of the Union’s total greenhouse gas emissions." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Recital 5, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**Plain-language summary:** This is an EU vehicle-manufacturing and fleet CO2 standard. It obligates vehicle manufacturers, not freight forwarders or cargo principals directly, to meet fleet-wide average CO2 emission reduction targets for new heavy-duty vehicles (HDVs) placed on the EU market. *Operational implication:* For workspaces managing road freight operations across EU trade lanes, including time-critical, high-value, and project cargo, the regulation reshapes the supply of new HDVs available from manufacturers, accelerates the zero-emission vehicle transition timeline, and introduces fleet procurement constraints that will affect road carrier capacity and vehicle specification planning from 2030 as the reduction targets set out in Section 8 step up.

## 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

### 1. MONITORING: Map Road Carrier Fleet Renewal Exposure

Assess which road transport service providers in the workspace's supply chain operate fleets in the vehicle sub-groups covered by the CO2 reduction targets quoted in Section 8, and query their fleet renewal roadmaps ahead of the step-change target windows.

*Operational implication:* Carriers whose manufacturers cannot meet the applicable target for a given reporting-period window face financial penalties under the excess CO2 emissions premium quoted in Section 8, which manufacturers are likely to pass through to fleet operating costs, or face constrained availability of conventional diesel trucks as manufacturers prioritise zero-emission allocation. For workspaces with road-primary operations, this creates a procurement risk window opening from 2030 onward, per the Article 3a(1) trajectory quoted in Section 8.

### 2. MONITORING: Verify Charging and Refuelling Infrastructure on Operating Corridors

Engage road transport partners on charging and refuelling infrastructure readiness along key EU corridors before zero-emission fleet mandates tighten. *Operational implication:* Where road service providers are transitioning to battery-electric or hydrogen traction on EU corridors, infrastructure gaps on specific routes may affect delivery schedules and transit times for high-value and time-critical cargo.

### 3. ACTION REQUIRED: Confirm Urban Bus Procurement Exposure

*Legal Confirmation Required:* If the workspace acts as a contracting authority or contracting entity in any urban bus procurement procedure, whether Article 3e public procurement obligations (the zero-emission urban bus award-criteria weighting quoted in Section 8) apply to those procurement processes requires legal review against the definitions of "contracting authority" and "contracting entity" in Directives 2014/24/EU, 2014/25/EU, and 2014/23/EU, which this brief's captured source pool does not itself resolve.

**FACT (primary_deadline):** "15 % for vehicle sub-groups 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD and 10-LH for the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2029" This is the nearest-term binding compliance milestone in the Regulation's own trajectory. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3a(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 4. MONITORING: Track the Commission Review Report Due 31 December 2027

*Analytical inference:* The 2027 review quoted in Section 6 may introduce amended targets for 2035 and 2040, widen scope to additional vehicle types, or modify the penalty regime. Workspaces should track the review to anticipate second-order changes to road fleet economics.

## 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

**FACT:** "“manufacturer” means the person or body to which the vehicles registered in a given period have been attributed in accordance with Article 7a" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(3)(e), amending Article 3(10) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT:** "“reporter” means an entity which is responsible for the reporting of data to the Commission" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(3)(f), amending Article 3(10a) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a workspace operating as a freight forwarder, logistics service provider, fleet procurement agent, or public procurement contracting entity meets any defined role under this regulation (manufacturer, reporter, contracting authority, contracting entity), and whether direct obligations therefore attach, requires legal counsel review in each specific operational context.

*Operational implication:* For workspaces that do not manufacture vehicles or hold type-approval responsibilities, the primary compliance-chain interaction is indirect: through vehicle procurement decisions (zero-emission versus conventional HDVs), through road carrier contracts requiring carriers to demonstrate fleet compliance and transition readiness, and, where applicable, through public procurement obligations for urban bus services. The regulation imposes direct obligations on manufacturers and Member State competent authorities for monitoring and reporting, not on freight forwarders or cargo principals as such.

## 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

**FACT:** "Regulation (EU) 2018/956 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 3, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT (transitional provision):** "in respect of reporting periods prior to 1 July 2024, Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as applicable on 30 June 2024 and Regulation (EU) 2018/956 as applicable on 30 June 2024 shall continue to apply" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 4, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* Workspaces relying on carrier fleet-compliance data generated under the predecessor Regulation (EU) 2018/956 should confirm with road transport partners that reporting has transitioned to the consolidated regime under Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 as amended, effective from the same 1 July 2024 date quoted above. The full CO2 reduction trajectory, penalty mechanism, and reporting architecture that this transition carries forward and strengthens are set out in Section 8.

## 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

Every one of this item's 36 exported `forward_events` rows is accounted for below. Many rows are the SAME underlying regulatory provision captured multiple times across overlapping pool fetches (the pool holds 24 captures of a handful of distinct URLs); those are grouped into one dated entry each, with the raw row indices named so the grouping is auditable. Sixteen distinct obligations result. See discovery-8c186db2.md for the full index-to-group mapping.

### 1. Commission Report on HDV Retrofit to Zero-Emission -- Due 30 June 2025 | MONITORING (raw rows 10, 18, 24)

**FACT:** "By 30 June 2025, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report which considers the need to facilitate the uptake on the Union market of heavy-duty vehicles which are retrofitted to become zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles, including by way of harmonised rules." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3b of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* Harmonised retrofit rules, if subsequently proposed, would open a compliance pathway for existing diesel fleets to become zero-emission without full vehicle replacement, potentially material for road fleet operators managing transition costs.

### 2. Commission Assessment of CO2-Neutral Fuels Methodology -- Due Within One Year of Entry Into Force | MONITORING (raw row: recital source, folded in with row 11's delegated-acts window)

**FACT:** "Following consultation with stakeholders, the Commission will, within one year of the date of entry into force of this Regulation, assess the role of a methodology for registering heavy-duty vehicles running exclusively on CO 2 neutral fuels, in conformity with Union law and with the Union’s climate-neutrality objective." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Recital 17, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Analytical inference:* By approximately mid-2025, the Commission is expected to publish findings on whether vehicles running on CO2-neutral fuels can be registered under a separate methodology. If adopted, this could provide an alternative compliance pathway for cargo types where electrification is operationally constrained.

### 3. Commission Report on Large Fleet Operators -- Due 30 June 2027 | MONITORING (raw rows 6, 19, 20, 30)

**FACT:** "By 30 June 2027, the Commission shall submit to the European Parliament and to the Council a report which contains an analysis of the potential need for and impact of initiatives to increase the share of zero-emission heavy-duty motor vehicles owned or leased by large fleet operators." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3c of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Analytical inference:* If the Commission follows this report with demand-side mandates on large fleet operators, workspaces managing or commissioning large road fleets could face direct zero-emission-vehicle deployment obligations in the following reporting-period window.

### 4. Commission Report on Renewable Fuels -- Due 31 December 2025 | MONITORING (raw rows 5, 26, 35)

**FACT:** "the Commission shall by 31 December 2025 present a report to the European Parliament and to the Council with a comprehensive analysis of the need to further incentivise the uptake of advanced biofuels and biogas and renewable fuels of non-biological origin in the heavy-duty vehicles sector" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(18), amending Article 15(2) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 5. Regulation Enters Into Force and Applies -- 26 June 2024 / 1 July 2024 | COMPLETED (raw rows 2, 21)

**FACT:** "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 July 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 5, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 6. Regulation (EU) 2018/956 Repealed -- 1 July 2024 | COMPLETED (raw rows 16, 25)

**FACT:** "Regulation (EU) 2018/956 is repealed with effect from 1 July 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 3, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 7. Reference-Year Qualification for Late-Entry Vehicle Sub-Groups | MONITORING (raw row 7)

*Analytical inference:* Newly in-scope vehicle sub-groups (coaches, medium lorries, trailers) do not share the flagship 2019 reference period quoted in Section 8; the Regulation's own reference-period table assigns them a later baseline year, so their first target-year reduction is measured from that later baseline, not from 2019. "The following reporting periods shall be applied as reference periods to vehicle sub-groups: Vehicle sub-group sg Reporting period of the year applicable as reference period 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD, 10-LH 2019 1, 2, 3, 11, 12, 16 2021 All others 2025" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Annex I, point 3.2, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 8. Road Freight Procurement Pressure Point From 2030 | MONITORING (raw row 8)

*Operational implication:* For workspaces procuring or contracting road freight for heavy lorries on EU routes, the availability and pricing of compliant conventional diesel trucks will increasingly tighten from 2030 as manufacturers accelerate zero-emission-vehicle deployment to avoid the excess CO2 emissions premium quoted in Section 8.

### 9. Vocational Vehicles Shielded Until 2035 | MONITORING (raw row 9)

*Analytical inference:* Vocational vehicles (the sub-groups quoted in the Annex I table in Section 8) are effectively shielded from CO2 reduction targets until 2035, with zero-emission vocational vehicles allowed to count toward manufacturers' compliance calculations from 2030 onward.

### 10. Delegated-Acts Power Window -- From 26 June 2024, Five Years | MONITORING (raw row 11)

**FACT:** "The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 3d(3), Article 13(4), second subparagraph, Article 13d(2), Article 13f(2) and Article 14(1), (2) and (3) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of five years from 26 June 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(19)(a), amending Article 17(2) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* The Commission may amend Annexes I, IV, and V by delegated act through this five-year window from 26 June 2024, including the vehicle sub-group definitions and mission-profile weights that determine which sub-group a workspace's contracted fleet falls into.

### 11. Vocational Vehicle Trajectory (0/0/64%/90%) | MONITORING (raw rows 12, 23, 34)

**FACT:** the Annex I 4.3.1 table quoted in full in Section 8 sets the vocational-vehicle CO2 reduction targets at 0 for 2025 to 2029, 0 for 2030 to 2034, 64 % for 2035 to 2039, and 90 % as from 2040. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Annex I, point 4.3.1, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 12. Excess CO2 Emissions Premium -- From 2025 Onwards | MONITORING (raw row 14)

**FACT (penalty_summary):** "Where a manufacturer is found, pursuant to paragraph 2, to have excess CO 2 emissions in a given reporting period from 2025 onwards, the Commission shall impose an excess CO 2 emissions premium, calculated in accordance with the following formula: (excess CO 2 emissions premium) = (excess CO 2 emissions × 4 250 EUR/gCO 2 /tkm)." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(11)(a), amending Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 13. Commission Review of Effectiveness and Impact -- Due 31 December 2027 | MONITORING (raw rows 15, 31)

**FACT:** "By 31 December 2027, the Commission shall review the effectiveness and impact of this Regulation, in particular as regards the objective of climate neutrality at the latest by 2050, and submit a report to the European Parliament and to the Council with the results of that review." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(18), amending Article 15(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 14. Trailer and Semi-Trailer Targets, Starting 2030 | MONITORING (raw row 17)

**FACT:** the Annex I 4.3.1 table quoted in full in Section 8 sets trailer targets at 7,5 % from 2030 onward and semi-trailer targets at 10 % from 2030 onward, both held flat through 2040. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Annex I, point 4.3.1, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 15. Urban Bus Zero-Emission Mandate, Starting 2030 | MONITORING (raw row 32)

**FACT:** the Annex I 4.3.2 table quoted in full in Section 8 sets the urban-bus zero-emission mandate at 90 % for 2030 to 2034 and 100 % from 2035 onward. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Annex I, point 4.3.2, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### 16. Heavy Lorries Full Time Series (the Flagship Sub-Group) | MONITORING (raw row 33)

**FACT:** the Article 3a(1) and Annex I 4.3.1 text quoted in full in Section 8 sets the reduction trajectory for heavy lorries over 16 t with the regulated axle configurations at 15 % for 2025 to 2029, 43 % for 2030 to 2034, 64 % for 2035 to 2039, and 90 % as from 2040, measured against the 2019 reference period. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4) and Annex I, point 4.3.1, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

## 7. Threshold Questions

### Q1: Are new heavy-duty vehicles registered outside the EU excluded from scope?

*Legal Confirmation Required:* Whether a specific vehicle's prior extra-EU registration history places it inside or outside scope under the Regulation's anti-avoidance provisions requires case-by-case review; this brief's captured source pool documents the reduction-target and jurisdictional-scope text quoted in Sections 2 and 8 but does not itself resolve individual registration-history fact patterns.

### Q2: Are vocational vehicles subject to the 2030 targets?

## 8. Substantive Requirements

### A. Fleet-Wide CO2 Reduction Targets -- Full Trajectory (Article 3a(1))

**FACT:** "The average CO 2 emissions of the Union fleet of new heavy-duty motor vehicles, other than special purpose vehicles, off-road vehicles and off-road special purpose vehicles shall be reduced by the following percentages compared to the average CO 2 emissions of the reporting period of the year 2019: (a) 15 % for vehicle sub-groups 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD and 10-LH for the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2029; (b) 45 % for all vehicle sub-groups other than vocational vehicles for the reporting periods of the years 2030 to 2034; (c) 65 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the years 2035 to 2039; (d) 90 % for all vehicle sub-groups for the reporting periods of the year 2040 onwards." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3a(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* The 2030 target is the first major step-change affecting the broadest set of vehicle sub-groups. For workspaces procuring or contracting road freight for heavy lorries on EU routes, the availability and pricing of compliant conventional diesel trucks will increasingly tighten from 2030 as manufacturers accelerate zero-emission-vehicle deployment to avoid the penalty quoted below.

For workspaces commissioning specialist vehicle types on EU operations, the procurement constraint arrives later, but the 2035 step-change is firm.

### C. Reference Periods by Vehicle Sub-Group (Annex I Point 3.2)

**FACT:** "The following reporting periods shall be applied as reference periods to vehicle sub-groups: Vehicle sub-group sg Reporting period of the year applicable as reference period 4-UD, 4-RD, 4-LH, 5-RD, 5-LH, 9-RD, 9-LH, 10-RD, 10-LH 2019 1, 2, 3, 11, 12, 16 2021 All others 2025" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Annex I, point 3.2, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Analytical inference:* This is a material qualification on Part A above: only the flagship heavy-lorry sub-groups share the 2019 baseline. Coaches, medium lorries, and other later-entry sub-groups measure their reduction against a later reference year, so the same percentage figure represents a different absolute emissions cut depending on sub-group.

### D. Penalty Mechanism -- Excess CO2 Emissions Premium (Article 8(1))

**FACT (penalty_summary):** "Where a manufacturer is found, pursuant to paragraph 2, to have excess CO 2 emissions in a given reporting period from 2025 onwards, the Commission shall impose an excess CO 2 emissions premium, calculated in accordance with the following formula: (excess CO 2 emissions premium) = (excess CO 2 emissions × 4 250 EUR/gCO 2 /tkm)." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(11)(a), amending Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* The penalty falls directly on manufacturers, not on freight operators or fleet buyers. However, manufacturers facing large penalty exposures are likely to price that risk into vehicle pricing structures or prioritise zero-emission-vehicle fleet allocation, indirectly affecting conventional diesel truck availability and pricing for road fleet operators from 2025 onward.

### E. Administrative Fines for Reporting Non-Compliance (Article 13f)

**FACT:** "The Commission may impose an administrative fine in each of the following cases: (a) where it finds that the data reported by the manufacturer pursuant to Article 13b of this Regulation deviate from the data resulting from the manufacturer’s records file or the engine type-approval certificate issued within the framework of Regulation (EC) No 595/2009, and the deviation is intentional or due to serious negligence; (b) where the data are not submitted within the deadline referred to in Article 13b(1), second subparagraph, and the delay cannot be duly justified." "The administrative fines shall be effective, proportionate and dissuasive and shall not exceed EUR 30 000 for each heavy-duty vehicle concerned by deviating or delayed data as referred to in points (a) and (b)." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(16), amending Article 13f of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### F. Small-Manufacturer Exemption (Article 6b)

**FACT:** "If a manufacturer registers fewer than 100 new heavy-duty vehicles in a given reporting period, the average specific CO 2 emissions as provided for in Article 4 and in point 2.7 of Annex I and the specific CO 2 emissions targets as provided for in Article 6 and in point 4.1 of Annex I shall be set at “0” for that reporting period." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(8), amending Article 6b(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT (exemption scope limit):** "Manufacturers to which the exemption laid down in paragraph 1 does not apply shall inform the Commission in each reporting period about all their connected undertakings to which the exemption applies." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(8), amending Article 6b(5) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Analytical inference:* The small-manufacturer exemption is not unconditional: a manufacturer inside a group of connected manufacturers must actively track which of its connected undertakings the exemption does and does not cover, and report that scope to the Commission every reporting period.

### G. Vehicle Transfer Between Manufacturers (Article 6a)

**FACT:** "the number of zero-emission heavy-duty vehicles transferred to a manufacturer does not exceed 5 % of all its new heavy-duty vehicles registered in a given reporting period" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(8), amending Article 6a(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

### H. Emission Debts, Credits, and Multi-Annual Clearing (Article 7(1))

**FACT:** "the total emission debt of a manufacturer shall not exceed 5 % of the manufacturer’s specific CO 2 emissions target multiplied by the number of heavy-duty vehicles of the manufacturer in that period (“emission debt limit”)" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(9)(c), amending Article 7(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT:** A manufacturer is deemed to have excess CO2 emissions "where, in any of the reporting periods of the years 2025 to 2028, 2030 to 2033 or 2035 to 2038, the sum of the emission debts reduced by the sum of the emission credits exceeds the emission debt limit referred to in Article 7(1), third subparagraph" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(11)(b), amending Article 8(2) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT (Recital 22):** "manufacturers should clear all remaining emission debts in the years 2029, 2034 and 2039" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Recital 22, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Analytical inference:* The debt-clearing requirement at 2029, 2034, and 2039 creates regulatory cliff points at which manufacturers with accumulated debts face sharply higher penalty exposure. These cliff points correspond to the most likely years of accelerated zero-emission-vehicle supply push to market, with consequent effects on fleet availability and conventional diesel pricing.

### I. Public Procurement -- Urban Bus Security-of-Supply Weighting (Article 3e)

**FACT:** "If the tender’s contribution to security of supply is used as an award criterion, it shall be given a weighting of between 15 to 40 % of the award criteria." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3e(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* For workspaces procuring road freight services, the publicly available central register, managed by the European Environment Agency, will allow comparison of specific CO2 emissions and fuel consumption data across vehicle types and manufacturers. *Analytical inference:* This publicly accessible data set is likely to become an important procurement tool for road freight tenders, enabling workspaces to specify minimum fleet CO2 performance requirements from service providers.

## 11. Operational System Requirements

### 1. Fleet Procurement Intelligence

Assess the workspace's road carrier procurement and contracting processes for integration of HDV CO2 compliance data published in the central register quoted in Section 10.

*Operational implication:* As manufacturer fleet data becomes publicly available via the central register from the 2025 reporting cycle onward, workspaces contracting road freight services will have access to carrier-level vehicle CO2 performance information. Building procurement criteria that weight low-CO2 fleet composition requires internal contract-template updates and supplier-onboarding process changes.

### 2. Road Carrier Transition Monitoring

Map road transport service providers against the reduction-target windows quoted in Section 8. *Operational implication:* Carriers unable to comply with manufacturer supply constraints, or who face elevated vehicle costs as diesel HDVs become scarcer, may pass costs through to freight rates. Workspaces with road-primary operations, particularly for large and heavy cargo requiring articulated or high-mass trucks, face the greatest exposure.

### 3. Internal Sustainability Reporting Data

*Analytical inference:* Workspaces building or updating their Scope 3 emissions methodology for road transport should align data inputs with the certified CO2 data published under the central register quoted in Section 10, rather than relying solely on spend- or distance-based estimates, to improve reporting credibility.

## 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

**FACT:** "Heavy-duty vehicles registered for use by armed services shall not be subject to the requirements of this Regulation if a Member State decides not to report them in accordance with Part A of Annex IV." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(4), amending Article 3a(5) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT:** "In order not to discourage the voluntary type-approval of heavy-duty vehicles that are designed and constructed or adapted for use by civil protection services, fire services and forces responsible for maintaining public order or urgent medical care services, which would have negative safety and environmental implications, such vehicles that are voluntarily type-approved should also be exempted from the obligation to meet the CO 2 emissions reduction targets set in this Regulation, unless the manufacturer requests otherwise." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Recital 27, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**FACT:** "If a manufacturer registers fewer than 100 new heavy-duty vehicles in a given reporting period, the average specific CO 2 emissions as provided for in Article 4 and in point 2.7 of Annex I and the specific CO 2 emissions targets as provided for in Article 6 and in point 4.1 of Annex I shall be set at “0” for that reporting period." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(8), amending Article 6b(1) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

**Qualification on the small-manufacturer exemption:** the exemption does not apply where the manufacturer itself requests otherwise, requests a vehicle transfer under Article 6a, or belongs to a group of connected manufacturers that collectively registers 100 or more heavy-duty vehicles in the reporting period. *Source: Regulation (EU) 2024/1610, Article 1(8), amending Article 6b(3) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1242, Official Journal, 6 June 2024.* https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1610/oj/eng

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks the EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2464, "CSRD") as relevant to freight-forwarding and logistics workspaces, with particular attention to the transport-sector Scope 3 emissions-disclosure burden that flows through carrier partners to freight-forwarding clients. The CSRD has since been amended twice: the Stop-the-Clock Directive (EU) 2025/794 delayed wave-2 and wave-3 application by two years, and Omnibus I Directive (EU) 2026/470 narrowed the CSRD's own scope and simplified its reporting-standards regime. All monetary figures below are Euros unless otherwise noted.

FACT: "Done at Strasbourg, 14 December 2022." *Source: Directive (EU) 2022/2464, Official Journal citation. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/oj/eng

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "Article 7 Entry into force and application This Directive shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union ." *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, Article 7. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "the double materiality perspective, in which the risks to the undertaking and the impacts of the undertaking each represent one materiality perspective." *Source: Senken Academy, "CSRD Reporting Requirements: A Practical Climate & ESRS E1 Guide," December 2025/January 2026. https://www.senken.io/academy/csrd-reporting-requirements

FACT: "specify the information that undertakings are to disclose about the following environmental factors: (i) climate change mitigation, including as regards scope 1, scope 2 and, where relevant, scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions;" *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "European companies and non-EU issuers employing on average over 1,000 employees and with a net annual turnover of over €450 million will remain within the scope of the CSRD." *Source: Norton Rose Fulbright, "European Union adopts Omnibus Directive amending CSRD and CS3D," February 2026. https://www.nortonrosefulbright.com/en/knowledge/publications/1679488b/european-parliament-votes-to-adopt-omnibus-proposal-amending-csrd-and-cs3d

*Operational implication:* a freight-forwarding workspace itself directly meeting the threshold above is rare; the more common exposure is that the workspace's own reporting counterparties (a corporate customer, or a carrier partner that is itself in direct CSRD scope) request Scope 3 transport-emissions data from the workspace under the double-materiality assessment their own CSRD report requires.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the workspace's own group (employee count, EU turnover, and any qualifying EU subsidiary or branch) meets the applicable thresholds, or whether the workspace is instead a value-chain data source for a counterparty's CSRD report, is a factual and legal determination requiring counsel review.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "Stakeholders may submit feedback on both draft delegated acts until 3 June 2026." *Source: Latham & Watkins, "European Commission Publishes Revised ESRS for Consultation," 11 May 2026. https://www.lw.com/en/insights/european-commission-publishes-revised-esrs-for-consultation

FACT: "the Commission should adopt assurance standards for limited assurance by means of delegated acts before 1 October 2026." *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

*Operational implication:* a workspace with CSRD-reporting counterparties on EU transport lanes should track both dates as the near-term signals of how the revised ESRS and the limited-assurance standard will settle, since both directly shape the data-point burden a workspace may be asked to help satisfy.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "Sustainability reporting standards shall not specify disclosures that would require undertakings to obtain information from small and medium-sized undertakings in their value chain that exceeds the information to be disclosed pursuant to the sustainability reporting standards for small and medium-sized undertakings referred to in Article 29c." *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, Article 29c reference. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "Financial holding companies will be exempt, but their subsidiaries or sub-groups may still be required to report if they meet the threshold for application." *Source: Latham & Watkins, "EU Sustainability Omnibus Published in the Official Journal," 27 February 2026. https://www.lw.com/en/insights/eu-sustainability-omnibus-published-in-the-official-journal

*Operational implication:* the workspace's practical position in the CSRD compliance chain is almost always as a value-chain data provider to a directly in-scope counterparty (carrier, corporate shipper, or freight-forwarding client group), not as a directly obligated reporting entity itself, unless the workspace's own group independently meets the thresholds in Section 2.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether any specific data request from a CSRD-reporting counterparty exceeds the VSME value-chain cap quoted above is a fact-specific compliance question for the workspace's own counsel.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "(e) information about the existence of incentive schemes linked to sustainability matters which are offered to members of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies" *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, Article 1(4) [Article 19a(2)(e)]. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "(c) a description of the role of the administrative, management and supervisory bodies with regard to sustainability matters, and of their expertise and skills in relation to fulfilling that role or the access such bodies have to such expertise and skills" *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, Article 1(4) [Article 19a(2)(c)]. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "(h) indicators relevant to the disclosures referred to in points (a) to (g)." *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, Article 1(4) [Article 19a(2)(h)]. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "The sustainability reporting standards shall ensure the quality of reported information, by requiring that it is understandable, relevant, verifiable, comparable and represented in a faithful manner." *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

*Analytical inference:* the consolidated EUR-Lex text (incorporating the Stop-the-Clock amendments) is the authoritative primary-law reference for Article 19a's disclosure content; the law-firm summaries cited throughout this brief for Omnibus I timing and scope are secondary commentary, used because the primary enacted text of Directive (EU) 2026/470 itself was not present in this item's captured source pool.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The revised ESRS reduce mandatory datapoints by more than 60%, simplify the materiality assessment process, and shorten and clarify the reporting requirements." *Source: Latham & Watkins, "European Commission Publishes Revised ESRS for Consultation," 11 May 2026. https://www.lw.com/en/insights/european-commission-publishes-revised-esrs-for-consultation

FACT: "The Commission committed to adopting a delegated act amending the existing ESRS within six months of the entry into force of the Omnibus (i.e., by 17 September 2026)." *Source: Latham & Watkins, "European Commission Publishes Revised ESRS for Consultation," 11 May 2026. https://www.lw.com/en/insights/european-commission-publishes-revised-esrs-for-consultation

FACT: "the Commission will adopt voluntary standards not later than July 19, 2026, based on Recommendation (EU) 2025/1710." *Source: Coolset, "What is the CSRD Directive adopted by the EU and who is in scope?," January 2026. https://www.coolset.com/academy/csrd-eu-climate-regulation-explained

FACT: "30 July 2025 Recommendation - Voluntary standard for SMEs Recommendation on a voluntary sustainability reporting standard for small and medium-sized undertakings (VSME) ." *Source: Feed Legislation, "Directive (EU) 2022/2464 (CSRD)." https://feedlegislation.org/en/feed-legislations/european-legislation/11-sustainability/directive-eu-20222464-csrd/

FACT: "In its 2026 Work Plan , EFRAG anticipates delivering advice to the Commission by the end of January 2027, following a public consultation and the preparation of an Exposure Draft." *Source: Latham & Watkins, "European Commission Publishes Revised ESRS for Consultation," 11 May 2026. https://www.lw.com/en/insights/european-commission-publishes-revised-esrs-for-consultation

FACT: "The obligation for the Commission to adopt sector-specific standards is removed." *Source: CSSF Luxembourg, "Omnibus package." https://www.cssf.lu/en/omnibus-package/

FACT: "Member States will have 12 months from that date to transpose the CSRD amendments into national law, i.e., by 19 March 2027." *Source: Garrigues, "Publication of Directive (EU) 2026/470," March 2026. https://www.garrigues.com/en_GB/new/publication-directive-eu-2026470-simplifying-corporate-sustainability-reporting-csrd-and-due

FACT: "►M1 DIRECTIVE (EU) 2025/794 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 14 April 2025 L 794 1 16.4.2025" *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, amendment marker. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

FACT: "The Directive was published in the Official Journal on 26 February 2026 as Directive (EU) 2026/470 and entered into force on 18 March 2026." *Source: DLA Piper GENIE, "EU Council approves Omnibus I Directive," 31 March 2026. https://knowledge.dlapiper.com/dlapiperknowledge/globalemploymentlatestdevelopments/2026/eu-council-approves-omnibus-i-directive

FACT: "The report on the implementation of this amending Directive should be published by 30 April 2029 and every three years thereafter" *Source: Consolidated text 02022L2464-20250417, recital. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2022/2464/2025-04-17/eng

**Q1: Does the workspace's own group meet the Omnibus I scope thresholds?**

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 14 December 2022: CSRD (Directive (EU) 2022/2464) done at Strasbourg, entering into force twenty days after its Official Journal publication per Article 7.
- 1 January 2024: original CSRD applicable from financial years starting on or after this date (wave-1).
- 14 April 2025: Stop-the-Clock Directive (EU) 2025/794 adopted, deferring wave-2 and wave-3 CSRD application by two years.
- 26 February 2026: Omnibus I Directive (EU) 2026/470 published in the Official Journal.
- 18 March 2026: Omnibus I Directive enters into force.
- 19 March 2027: Member States' deadline to transpose the Omnibus I CSRD amendments into national law (12 months from 18 March 2026).
- 3 June 2026: deadline for stakeholder feedback on the draft revised ESRS delegated acts.
- 17 September 2026: Commission's committed target date for adopting the revised ESRS delegated act.
- July 19, 2026: Commission's target date for adopting the VSME (value-chain cap) delegated act.
- By the end of January 2027: EFRAG's target date for delivering technical advice on Non-EU Sustainability Reporting Standards (NESRS).
- Before 1 October 2026: Commission's target date for adopting limited-assurance standards under the recital cited in Section 3 (a separate provision elsewhere in the corpus states this adoption is postponed to 1 July 2027 at the latest -- both statements are reproduced as the pool states them, without reconciling which supersedes the other).
- 2028: first CSRD reports under the revised (Omnibus I) thresholds, covering the 2027 financial year.
- 30 April 2029: deadline for the Commission's report on the implementation of the Omnibus I amending Directive, repeating every three years thereafter.

metadata.what_is_it: The EU Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (Directive 2022/2464), as amended by the Stop-the-Clock Directive (EU 2025/794, two-year wave delay) and Omnibus I (Directive (EU) 2026/470, scope narrowed to over 1000 employees and over EUR 450 million turnover), requiring in-scope undertakings to disclose sustainability information including Scope 1, 2 and 3 greenhouse gas emissions in a dedicated section of the management report.
metadata.why_matters: A freight-forwarding workspace is unlikely to be directly in CSRD scope itself but is a probable Scope 3 transport-emissions data source for carrier partners and corporate shipper clients that are directly in scope, subject to the VSME value-chain-cap ceiling on what those counterparties may request.
key_data: Omnibus I scope threshold over 1000 employees and over EUR 450 million net annual turnover
non-EU group threshold over EUR 450 million EU turnover plus an EU subsidiary or branch over EUR 200 million turnover beginning FY28
third-country undertaking group threshold over EUR 150 million EU turnover
third-country branch threshold over EUR 40 million net turnover
first reports under the revised thresholds due in 2028 covering financial year 2027

steps.label: original CSRD applicable for financial years starting on or after 1 January 2024
Directive (EU) 2025/794 defers wave-2 and wave-3 entry by two years
Directive (EU) 2026/470 enters into force, narrowing scope to over 1000 employees and over EUR 450 million turnover
first CSRD reports under the revised thresholds, covering FY2027

requirement_trajectory.note: the pool states no further per-year phase-in schedule beyond this wave sequence; the revised ESRS delegated act (targeted 17 September 2026) will govern the FY2027 data-point content but was not yet adopted as of the captured sources

metadata.enforcement_body: Member States, through their national transposing law, administer the sanctions regime for statutory auditors and assurance providers under the CSRD's amendments to Directive 2006/43/EC; no source in this corpus states an EU-level fixed penalty quantum or a penalty running to a reporting undertaking's value-chain counterparties

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 (FuelEU Maritime), the EU regulation on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport, for ocean freight moved through EU ports. FuelEU Maritime sets a declining GHG intensity limit on the energy used on board ships above 5 000 gross tonnage and a shore-power (OPS) connection obligation for containerships and passenger ships, with penalties running to the vessel operator (the "company" under the Regulation), not to a freight forwarder or shipper directly.

*Operational implication:* this brief covers a binding EU instrument; a freight forwarder's own exposure runs through its ocean carrier counterparties on EU-touching lanes, not through a direct obligation on the forwarder itself (Section 4 below).

FACT: "This Regulation shall enter into force on the twentieth day following that of its publication in the Official Journal of the European Union . It shall apply from 1 January 2025, with the exception of Articles 8 and 9 which shall apply from 31 August 2024." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 32. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: the instrument's own header states it is "REGULATION (EU) 2023/1805 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 September 2023 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, header. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "This Regulation applies to all ships of above 5 000 gross tonnage that serve the purpose of transporting passengers or cargo for commercial purposes, regardless of their flag" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: "Although ships above 5 000 GT represent only approximately 55 % of all ships calling at ports under Regulation (EU) 2015/757" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Recital 11. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: "‘well-to-wake’ means a method for calculating emissions that takes into account the GHG impact of energy production, transport, distribution and use on board, including during combustion" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 3(18). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* well-to-wake data from vessel operators under FuelEU is reported on a per-ship annual average basis in the FuelEU database. This is structurally different from voyage-level or cargo-level emissions data that Scope 3 Category 4 (upstream transportation) reporting may require; a workspace tracking carrier emissions for its own client disclosure obligations may need to request supplementary data from carriers or use an allocation methodology.

FACT: "(b) the entirety of the energy used on voyages from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State to a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State; (c) notwithstanding point (b), one half of the energy used on voyages arriving at or departing from a port of call located in an outermost region under the jurisdiction of a Member State; and (d) one half of the energy used on voyages arriving at or departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, where the previous or the next port of call is under the jurisdiction of a third country." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* an ocean shipment moving entirely between EU Member State ports draws the full ("entirety of the") energy-use figure into scope, while a shipment to or from a third-country port, or through an outermost region, draws only one half; the compliance cost pass-through per container will differ materially between route types.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Action:* verify with each ocean carrier counterparty on EU-touching trade lanes that a valid FuelEU Monitoring Plan was submitted to an accredited verifier by 31 August 2024, or within two months of a ship's first EU port call for ships not previously in scope.

FACT: "By 31 August 2024, companies shall submit to the verifiers a monitoring plan for each of their ships indicating the method chosen from among methods set out in Annex I for monitoring and reporting the amount, type and emission factor of energy used on board by ships and other relevant information." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 8(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: "For ships falling under the scope of this Regulation for the first time after 31 August 2024, companies shall submit a monitoring plan to the verifier without undue delay and no later than two months after each ship’s first call at a port under the jurisdiction of a Member State." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 8(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* a vessel operator that has not submitted a monitoring plan is non-compliant from the first reporting period and will not receive a FuelEU document of compliance, which is a potential port detention risk under Directive 2009/16/EC (port State control) that could disrupt cargo movements.

*Action:* map the workspace's EU port calls and voyage types to determine which shipments attract the full energy-use figure (intra-EU voyages) versus one half (outermost region or third-country voyages), per Section 2 above.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

The FuelEU obligations run to the "company" (the ISM-responsible entity for the ship), not to a freight forwarder, importer, or logistics coordinator acting as an intermediary.

FACT: "The entity responsible for ensuring compliance with FuelEU Maritime Regulation should be the entity that is responsible for compliance of the ship with the International Safety Management Code (ISM Company)" *Source: DG MOVE Q&A on Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Question 1.2. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/maritime/decarbonising-maritime-transport-fueleu-maritime/questions-and-answers-regulation-eu-20231805-use-renewable-and-low-carbon-fuels-maritime-transport_en

*Operational implication:* carrier compliance costs under FuelEU (fuel-quality shifts, OPS infrastructure use, penalty exposure) are likely to be incorporated into freight pricing on EU-touching ocean lanes over the 2025-2050 trajectory below; a workspace client operating under CSRD, ISSB, or an equivalent disclosure framework may separately request carrier-level well-to-wake emissions data for its own Scope 3 reporting.

FACT: "From 1 January 2030, a ship moored at the quayside in a port of call which is covered by Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 and which is under the jurisdiction of a Member State shall connect to OPS and use it for all its electrical power demand at berth." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 6(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

*Operational implication:* carriers whose vessels cannot connect to OPS or use a qualifying zero-emission technology face a per-hour FuelEU penalty from 1 January 2030; that cost structure is likely to pass through to freight rates on containership and passenger-ship calls at major EU ports.

# 7. Threshold Questions

## 1. Does the ship fall within the size and purpose threshold?

FACT: "This Regulation applies to all ships of above 5 000 gross tonnage that serve the purpose of transporting passengers or cargo for commercial purposes, regardless of their flag" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: "This Regulation does not apply to warships, naval auxiliaries, fish-catching or fish-processing ships, wooden ships of a primitive build, ships not propelled by mechanical means, or ships owned or operated by a government and used only for non-commercial purposes." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 2(7). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

**Decided:** container vessels and passenger ships above 5 000 GT serving EU ports are in scope; the vessel type and gross tonnage are factual determinations from the ship's registration documents, no legal determination required at the ship level.

## 2. Is the voyage intra-EU, international, or outermost-region?

FACT: "(b) the entirety of the energy used on voyages from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State to a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State; (c) notwithstanding point (b), one half of the energy used on voyages arriving at or departing from a port of call located in an outermost region under the jurisdiction of a Member State; and (d) one half of the energy used on voyages arriving at or departing from a port of call under the jurisdiction of a Member State, where the previous or the next port of call is under the jurisdiction of a third country." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 2(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

**Decided:** the voyage-scope determination is factual (port jurisdiction) and can be confirmed against the voyage itinerary.

FACT: "If a stop in a port is not considered a ‘port of call’ then the activities in this port are regarded as part of the voyage. # 8. Substantive Requirements

## A. GHG intensity limit (the core obligation)

FACT: "The yearly average GHG intensity of the energy used on board by a ship during a reporting period shall not exceed the limit set out in paragraph 2." *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 4(1). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: the limit "shall be calculated by reducing the reference value of 91,16 grams of CO 2 equivalent per MJ by the following percentage" *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: the reduction percentages are "2 % from 1 January 2025"; "6 % from 1 January 2030"; "14,5 % from 1 January 2035"; "31 % from 1 January 2040"; "62 % from 1 January 2045"; "80 % from 1 January 2050". *Source: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, Article 4(2). https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2023/1805/oj/eng

FACT: "would not be able to meet the GHG intensity target of 89.34 gCO2eq/MJ (Reference Value of 91.16 gCO2eq/MJ reduced by 2%)" *Source: DG MOVE Q&A, Question 10.3. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/maritime/decarbonising-maritime-transport-fueleu-maritime/questions-and-answers-regulation-eu-20231805-use-renewable-and-low-carbon-fuels-maritime-transport_en

*Industry interpretation:* "The GHG intensity requirement applies to 100% of energy used on voyages and port calls within the EU or EEA, and 50% of energy used on voyages into or out of the EU or EEA or voyages to or from an outermost region." *Source: DNV, FuelEU Maritime: Regulation Insights and Compliance Strategies. https://www.dnv.com/maritime/insights/topics/fueleu-maritime/

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- OJ L 234, 22.9.2023: Published in the Official Journal of the European Union (OJ L 234).
- 12 October 2023: Regulation entered into force, twenty days after Official Journal publication (Article 32).
- REGULATION (EU) 2023/1805 OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of 13 September 2023 on the use of renewable and low-carbon fuels in maritime transport: Regulation adopted by the European Parliament and of the Council.
- 31 August 2024: Articles 8 and 9 (monitoring plan provisions) begin applying (Article 32).
- 31 August 2024: Deadline for initial monitoring plan submission by existing companies (Article 8(1)).
- 26 July 2024: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2027 on verification activities adopted.
- 26 July 2024: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2031 on monitoring plan templates adopted.
- 9 September 2024: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/192 on verifier accreditation adopted.
- 23 September 2024: Commission interaction report with Regulation (EU) 2015/757 due (Article 30(1)).
- 1 January 2025: Full application of Regulation (EU) 2023/1805 begins; reporting period 2025 begins.
- 1 January 2025: GHG intensity reduction trajectory begins at a 2% reduction (Article 4(2)).
- 31 December 2025: first reporting period (calendar year 2025) ends.
- 31 January 2026: First FuelEU report submission deadline, covering 2025 data (Article 15(3)).
- 31 March of the verification period: verifier notifies the company of compliance information and records the FuelEU report in the FuelEU database (Article 16(5)); first cycle falls in 2026.
- 1 May of the verification period: verifier records compliance balances in the FuelEU database (Article 23(1)); first cycle falls in 2026.
- 6 June 2025: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1127 on neighbouring container transhipment ports adopted.
- 30 April 2026: DNV's own compliance calendar states the compliance balance is approved in the FuelEU Maritime database by this date.
- 30 June 2026: DNV's own compliance calendar states the FuelEU Document of Compliance is issued and the penalty payment deadline falls, for the first cycle.
- 23 February 2026: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/394 on FuelEU database access rights adopted.
- 30 June 2024: deadline, where applicable, for the implementing act listing existing zero-emission technologies (Article 6(7)).
- 31 December 2027: first Commission evaluation report on the functioning of the Regulation due, and every five years thereafter (Article 30(2)).
- reporting period 2031: reference monitoring period for the RFNBO subtarget trigger assessment (Article 5(2)).
- 31 December 2029: all Member State route exemptions under Article 2(3) to (6) expire.
- 1 January 2030: OPS obligation commences for containerships and passenger ships at AFIR Article 9 ports (Article 6(1)); GHG intensity reduction target increases to "6 %" (Article 4(2)).
- 1 January 2034: conditional RFNBO 2% subtarget applies if triggered by the reporting-period-2031 assessment (Article 5(3)).
- 31 December 2033: RFNBO multiplier of 2 expires (Article 5(1)).
- 31 December 2034: ice-conditions energy exclusion for IC/IB/IA/IA Super ships expires (Annex IV(A)).
- 1 January 2035: OPS obligation extends to all EU ports with available shore power (Article 6(2)); GHG intensity reduction target increases to "14,5 %" (Article 4(2)).
- 1 January 2040: GHG intensity reduction target increases to "31 %" (Article 4(2)).
- 1 January 2045: GHG intensity reduction target increases to "62 %" (Article 4(2)).
- 1 January 2050: GHG intensity reduction target reaches "80 %" (Article 4(2)).

metadata.what_is_it: Regulation (EU) 2023/1805, FuelEU Maritime, the EU law setting a declining GHG intensity limit on energy used on board ships above 5000 gross tonnage and an onshore power supply connection obligation for containerships and passenger ships at EU ports, in force since 1 January 2025 with penalties running to the ship's company through 2050.
metadata.why_matters: The GHG intensity limit and the OPS connection obligation raise ocean carrier compliance costs on EU-touching lanes on a fixed schedule through 2050, with the cost structure likely to pass through to freight rates; a workspace client under CSRD or ISSB disclosure may also request carrier-level well-to-wake emissions data grounded in this Regulation's own methodology.
key_data: GHG intensity reference value 91.16 gCO2e per MJ reduced by 2 percent from 2025 rising to 80 percent by 2050
GHG penalty equals compliance-balance shortfall divided by 41000 MJ per tonne VLSFO times EUR 2400 per tonne
OPS non-compliance penalty equals EUR 1.5 times berth electrical power demand times hours out of compliance

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document tracks Resolution MEPC.338(76) and the short-term GHG reduction measure it belongs to: the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) operational rating regime and the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) design-efficiency regime, both introduced through amendments to MARPOL Annex VI. It exists to give a freight-forwarding workspace with ocean-carrier exposure a single place to see the CII rating mechanics, the annual reporting cycle, the SEEMP Part III obligation, and the compliance consequence for a low CII rating. Monetary figures do not appear in this brief; the primary consequence structure is administrative (a corrective action plan requirement), not a fixed monetary penalty.

FACT: "RESOLUTION MEPC.338(76) (adopted on 17 June 2021)" *Source: MEPC.338(76), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.338(76).pdf

FACT: "These Guidelines provide the methods to determine the annual operational carbon intensity reduction factors and their concrete values from year 2023 to 2030, as referred to in regulation 28 of MARPOL Annex VI." *Source: MEPC.338(76), IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.338(76).pdf

*Analytical inference:* the workspace itself is not the regulated party under MARPOL Annex VI regulation 28; the regulated party is the ship's owner or company, acting through the flag Administration or a Recognized Organization. The workspace's exposure runs through its ocean-carrier partners' vessels, not through a direct compliance obligation of its own.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "which is expected to enter into force on 1 November 2022 upon its deemed acceptance on 1 May 2022" *Source: IMO MEPC 76 Meeting Summary, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/meetingsummaries/pages/mepc76meetingsummary.aspx

FACT: "The requirements for EEXI and CII certification came into effect on 1 January 2023. The first annual reporting is to be completed in 2023, with initial ratings given in 2024." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Operational implication:* a workspace booking ocean freight on any vessel of 5,000 gross tonnage or above is booking capacity on a ship that has carried an annual A-E CII rating since 2024; the rating is public information on the ship's own Statement of Compliance and increasingly referenced in charter-party and booking documentation.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

FACT: "needs to be amended and approved by 31 December 2025 ." *Source: New IMO CII Guidelines Require SEEMP Part III Revisions, Cyprus Shipping News, 23 July 2025. https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2025/07/23/new-imo-cii-guidelines-require-seemp-part-iii-revision/

FACT: "Lloyd’s Register (LR) requests shipowners and managers to submit their plans on or before 30 October 2025 ." *Source: New IMO CII Guidelines Require SEEMP Part III Revisions, Cyprus Shipping News, 23 July 2025. https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2025/07/23/new-imo-cii-guidelines-require-seemp-part-iii-revision/

*Operational implication:* the RO submission window recommended ahead of the 31 December 2025 approval deadline has already closed as of this brief's own generation date; a workspace with Japan, EU, or other CII-exposed ocean-carrier lanes should confirm directly with its carrier partners whether their fleets' revised SEEMP Part III plans (covering the 2026 to 2028 implementation period) were approved on schedule, since a lapsed approval affects the carrier's ability to hold a current Statement of Compliance.

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this brief's own corpus does not confirm whether MEPC 84 (expected May 2026, Section 6) actually adopted the draft amendments to regulation 27, or their current in-force status; a workspace with a specific DCS-reporting compliance question should confirm current status directly against the IMO's own published resolutions rather than relying solely on this summary.

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "While EEXI generally applies to each ship of 400 gross tonnage and above, CII applies to ships 5,000 gross tonnage and above." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Analytical inference:* because the CII and EEXI compliance chain runs from the ship's owner or company through the flag Administration or a Recognized Organization to the IMO's own Ship Fuel Oil Consumption Database, the workspace's practical leverage point is commercial (carrier selection, charter-party CII clauses) rather than direct regulatory compliance.

*Operational implication:* carrier compliance costs associated with maintaining a C rating or above (operational measures, fuel-efficiency investment, and in a low-rating scenario the corrective action plan process) are likely to be reflected in freight pricing on CII-exposed ocean lanes; workspace clients operating under CSRD, ISSB, or equivalent disclosure frameworks may separately request carrier-level CII rating and fuel-consumption data for their own Scope 3 accounting.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

FACT: "Required annual operational CII = (1 − Z 100) × CII ref (3)" *Source: Technical Paper on CII/SEEMP, Dromon Bureau of Shipping. https://www.dromon.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Dromon-TP-on-CII-SEEMP-III.pdf

FACT: "Year Reduction factor relative to 2019 2023 5%* 2024 7% 2025 9% 2026 11% 2027 - ** 2028 - ** 2029 - ** 2030 - ** Note: * Z factors of 1%, 2% and 3% are set for the years of 2020 to 2022, similar as business as usual until entry into force of the measure. ** Z factors for the years of 2027 to 2030 to be further strengthened and developed taking into account the review of the short-term measure." *Source: MEPC.338(76), Table 1, IMO. https://wwwcdn.imo.org/localresources/en/KnowledgeCentre/IndexofIMOResolutions/MEPCDocuments/MEPC.338(76).pdf

*Analytical inference:* the required annual operational CII is a moving target that tightens every year the reduction factor Z increases; a vessel's fuel-efficiency measures that achieved a C rating under a lower Z factor are not guaranteed to sustain that rating as Z climbs toward the 2030 value, without further improvement or an adjustment in operational profile.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "MEPC 83 adopted resolution MEPC.400(83) on Amendments to the 2021 Guidelines on the operational carbon intensity reduction factors relative to reference lines (CII reduction factors guidelines, G3) (resolution MEPC.338(76) )." *Source: MEPC 83 Meeting Summary, LISCR. https://www.liscr.com/marketing/liscr/media/liscr/online%20library/maritime/mepc-83-meeting-summary.pdf

FACT: "RESOLUTION MEPC.400(83) (adopted on 11 April 2025)" *Source: Technical Paper, ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/pdf/tech_info/tech_img/T1354e.pdf

FACT: "Table 1: Reduction factor (Z%) for the CII relative to the 2019 reference line Year Reduction factor relative to 2019 2023 5% 2024 7% 2025 9% 2026 11% 2027 13.625% 2028 16.250% 2029 18.875% 2030 21.500%" *Source: Technical Information TEC-1354, MEPC.400(83) Annex 4 (Table 1, as amended), ClassNK. https://www.classnk.or.jp/hp/pdf/tech_info/tech_img/T1354e.pdf

*Operational implication:* the 2027 to 2030 Z factors were adopted through a Guidelines amendment (MEPC.400(83)), not a fresh MARPOL Annex VI amendment cycle, which is why MEPC.338(76) itself (Section 5) still shows the 2027-2030 cells as "to be further strengthened" placeholders; the amended Table 1 above is the resolution's own replacement text as reproduced in the classification-society technical compilation captured for this brief, not a secondary paraphrase.

FACT: "The Committee has now moved into the second phase of the review, in accordance with the work plan for phase 2 of the review of the short-term GHG reduction measure approved at MEPC 83." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

FACT: "Phase 2 will run from Spring 2026 to Spring 2028, to further develop the SEEMP framework and metrics." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Analytical inference:* Phase 2 outcomes (Spring 2026 to Spring 2028) could alter the SEEMP verification framework, the correction-factor regime, or the rating methodology, with potential downstream effect on carrier compliance obligations. Re-check window: Spring 2028.

FACT: "MEPC 83 also approved draft amendments to regulation 27 of MARPOL Annex VI. These amendments are expected to be adopted at MEPC 84 in May 2026." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Operational implication:* regulation 27 governs the mandatory annual fuel-consumption data collection and reporting that feeds every CII calculation; amendments to it may alter the reporting scope carriers must maintain. A workspace tracking Japan, EU, or UK CII-exposed lanes should monitor the outcome of MEPC 84.

FACT: "the review of CII regulations to be completed by the Organization by 1 January 2026 as identified in regulation 28.11 of MARPOL Annex VI" *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Legal Confirmation Required:* this review, due from the Organization by 1 January 2026 under regulation 28.11, could result in amendments affecting enforcement, data collection, and the Z factor and CIIR values themselves; this brief's corpus does not confirm the review's outcome or current status.

FACT: "The draft text is expected to be adopted at the Second Extraordinary Session of the Marine Environment Protection Committee (MEPC ES.2), scheduled for October 2025, with entry into force on 1 March 2027." *Source: MEPC 83 Meeting Summary, LISCR. https://www.liscr.com/marketing/liscr/media/liscr/online%20library/maritime/mepc-83-meeting-summary.pdf

*Analytical inference:* the mid-term GFI (GHG fuel intensity) measure is a SEPARATE regulatory track from the CII/EEXI short-term measure this brief tracks; it is noted here only because the workspace's Anticipated Guidance monitoring should not conflate the two, since a low CII rating and a GFI shortfall are governed by different resolutions with different mechanisms.

# 7. Threshold Questions

## Question 1: Does the vessel meet the applicable gross-tonnage threshold?

FACT: "While EEXI generally applies to each ship of 400 gross tonnage and above, CII applies to ships 5,000 gross tonnage and above." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

FACT: "6.1 The Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII) regime applies to all relevant ships 5,000GT and above of the same type as listed in paragraph 1.9." *Source: MGN 683 (M+F) IMO Carbon Reduction Measures, UK MCA, April 2023. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether specific vessels in the workspace's carrier partners' fleets meet the 5,000 gross tonnage (CII) or 400 gross tonnage (EEXI) threshold as measured per the relevant tonnage convention requires technical verification and, where the workspace itself operates covered tonnage, flag-State confirmation.

## Question 2: Is the vessel engaged on international voyages, or solely domestic?

FACT: "the provisions of Chapter 4 do not apply to ships solely engaged in voyages within waters subject to the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the State the flag of which the ship is entitled to fly. However, each Party should ensure, by the adoption of appropriate measures, that such ships are constructed and act in a manner consistent with the requirements of chapter 4 of this Annex, so far as is reasonable and practicable." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a given vessel's actual trading pattern constitutes voyages "solely engaged in voyages within waters subject to the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the State the flag of which the ship is entitled to fly" is a flag-State legal determination, not one this brief can make from the sourced materials alone.

## Question 3: Do correction factors or voyage adjustments alter the attained CII?

FACT: "MEPC.355(78) - 2022 Interim Guidelines on correction factors and voyage adjustments for CII calculations (CII Guidelines, G5)." *Source: MGN 683 (M+F) IMO Carbon Reduction Measures, UK MCA, April 2023. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures

*Operational implication:* the G3 guidelines (MEPC.338(76), as amended) set the required CII Z factor; the separate G5 guidelines (MEPC.355(78)) govern adjustments to the attained CII numerator and denominator. A vessel's own DCS-reported fuel consumption data is the input; correction factors and voyage adjustments modify how that data converts into the attained CII figure compared against the required CII.
