# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "The owner or relevant certified organisation of a relevant ship must use the data collected under the existing annual fuel oil consumption data collection requirements (MARPOL Annex VI Regulation 27) to calculate the attained annual operational CII of the ship for each 12-month reporting period beginning on 1 January and ending on 31 December." *Source: MGN 683 (M+F) IMO Carbon Reduction Measures, UK MCA, April 2023. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures

FACT: "The attained annual operational CII must be reported to a Certifying Authority by 31 March of the following year to which the data relates." *Source: MGN 683 (M+F) IMO Carbon Reduction Measures, UK MCA, April 2023. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures

*Operational implication:* the annual reporting cycle (1 January to 31 December activity year, 31 March following-year submission deadline) creates a structured data-availability window; carrier-level attained CII and rating data may not reach a freight-forwarding workspace until the second quarter of the calendar year following the activity year.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

FACT: "MEPC.355(78) - 2022 Interim Guidelines on correction factors and voyage adjustments for CII calculations (CII Guidelines, G5)." *Source: MGN 683 (M+F) IMO Carbon Reduction Measures, UK MCA, April 2023. https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures/mgn-683-mf-imo-carbon-reduction-measures

*Operational implication:* a workspace advising on or booking CII-exposed ocean capacity should build capacity to request and receive verified CII rating and DCS fuel-consumption data from carrier partners, since this data underpins both charter-party CII clause administration and any Scope 3 emissions reporting the workspace's own clients require.

FACT: "Engine Power Limitation (EPL), are no longer sufficient on their own to maintain a viable CII rating." *Source: 2026 Maritime Regulations: EEXI and CII Compliance Guide, Esenyel Partners. https://www.esenyelpartners.com/2026-eexi-and-cii-compliance-guide/

*Analytical inference:* Engine Power Limitation is a passive, EEXI-side design measure; it does not itself improve operational CII performance, which is the metric that actually determines the annual A-E rating. A carrier that relied on EPL alone to achieve EEXI compliance is not thereby protected from CII rating risk as the Z factor steepens.

FACT: "BIMCO CII Operations Clause regulates the sharing of responsibility between parties, factors such as port waiting times or unforeseen weather conditions in 2026 can lead to serious legal disputes regarding their impact on CII grades." *Source: 2026 Maritime Regulations: EEXI and CII Compliance Guide, Esenyel Partners. https://www.esenyelpartners.com/2026-eexi-and-cii-compliance-guide/

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a specific charter-party CII operations clause allocates rating-related performance obligations and disputes between owner and charterer in a manner that modifies the regulatory picture above is a legal determination requiring counsel review of the specific contract.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "the provisions of Chapter 4 do not apply to ships solely engaged in voyages within waters subject to the sovereignty or jurisdiction of the State the flag of which the ship is entitled to fly. However, each Party should ensure, by the adoption of appropriate measures, that such ships are constructed and act in a manner consistent with the requirements of chapter 4 of this Annex, so far as is reasonable and practicable." *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

FACT: "ice-classed ship sails in ice conditions to and from a port within the same sea area within the same ice edge: the period of time the ship is in that port (port period) may be included in either the voyage period to that port or the voyage period from that port; and all fuel consumption for that port period may be included in the voyage adjustment" *Source: Rules and Regulations, CII, Sustainable Ships. https://www.sustainable-ships.org/rules-regulations/cii

*Analytical inference:* the ice-classed voyage-adjustment provision is a narrow, vessel-class-specific edge case; it is unlikely to affect a general freight-forwarding workspace's ocean-carrier selection decisions outside of ice-class-relevant trade lanes.

FACT: "New ships which are now entering into service, and existing ships for which a new SEEMP Part III is being developed resulting from change in Management Company or Flag, or both, can include the implementation plan extended to 2028 to avoid reapproval again before 31 December 2025 ." *Source: New IMO CII Guidelines Require SEEMP Part III Revisions, Cyprus Shipping News, 23 July 2025. https://cyprusshippingnews.com/2025/07/23/new-imo-cii-guidelines-require-seemp-part-iii-revision/

*Operational implication:* a new entrant vessel, or a vessel changing management company or flag, is not held to the same 31 December 2025 SEEMP Part III re-approval deadline as an already-approved fleet; its implementation plan can extend straight to 2028.

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "A ship run on a low-carbon fuel can clearly get a higher rating than one running on fossil fuel" *Source: EEXI and CII FAQ, IMO. https://www.imo.org/en/mediacentre/hottopics/pages/eexi-cii-faq.aspx

*Analytical inference:* the corpus does not further quantify the rating benefit of any specific alternative fuel (methanol, ammonia, LNG, biofuels); it states only that a low-carbon fuel can produce a higher rating than fossil fuel, with the actual emission-factor calculation embedded in the G1 CII calculation guidelines outside this corpus.

FACT: "Engine Power Limitation (EPL), are no longer sufficient on their own to maintain a viable CII rating." *Source: 2026 Maritime Regulations: EEXI and CII Compliance Guide, Esenyel Partners. https://www.esenyelpartners.com/2026-eexi-and-cii-compliance-guide/

FACT: "BIMCO CII Operations Clause regulates the sharing of responsibility between parties, factors such as port waiting times or unforeseen weather conditions in 2026 can lead to serious legal disputes regarding their impact on CII grades." *Source: 2026 Maritime Regulations: EEXI and CII Compliance Guide, Esenyel Partners. https://www.esenyelpartners.com/2026-eexi-and-cii-compliance-guide/

*Analytical inference:* the increasing prevalence of charter-party CII clauses is adjacent commercial practice responding to the same rating regime this brief tracks; a workspace negotiating or advising on time-charter arrangements involving CII-exposed vessels should expect rating-allocation language to be increasingly standard rather than exceptional.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 17 June 2021: MEPC.338(76) (the G3 reduction-factor guidelines) adopted by MEPC 76, setting the 2023 to 2026 Z factors and leaving 2027 to 2030 unspecified.
- 1 May 2022: deemed acceptance of the MARPOL Annex VI CII and EEXI amendments.
- 1 November 2022: MARPOL Annex VI CII and EEXI amendments entered into force.
- 2023: Z factor 5% (2023 reporting year, first ratings issued in 2024); CII certification requirements and the SEEMP Part III obligation became mandatory.
- 2024: Z factor 7%.
- 2025: Z factor 9%.
- 11 April 2025: MEPC.400(83) adopted, inserting the 2027 to 2030 Z factors into the G3 guidelines.
- October 2025: MEPC ES.2 scheduled, with expected adoption of the separate mid-term GFI measures.
- 30 October 2025: Lloyd's Register-recommended submission deadline for revised SEEMP Part III plans, to secure approval before 31 December 2025.
- 31 December 2025: deadline for the revised SEEMP Part III (covering the 2026 to 2028 implementation plan) to be approved for currently-approved fleets.
- 1 January 2026: Z factor 11% took effect; the revised SEEMP Part III was needed to be in place; the same date is the Organization's own regulation 28.11 deadline for completing the review of CII regulations (Section 6).
- 2027: Z factor 13.625%.
- 1 March 2027: mid-term GFI measures, if adopted at MEPC ES.2 in October 2025, enter into force.
- 2028: Z factor 16.250%.
- 2029: Z factor 18.875%.
- 2030: Z factor 21.500%.

entries.body:
# 1. Purpose and Scope of This Document

This document analyses the Green Credit Rules, 2023, notified by the Government of India on 12th October, 2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. It covers the programme's structure, eligible activities, registration and verification procedures, governance architecture, and operational requirements as enacted in the Official Gazette, for workspaces operating in freight forwarding, logistics, and transport-adjacent supply chains in India.

FACT: "MINISTRY OF ENVIRONMENT, FOREST AND CLIMATE CHANGE NOTIFICATION New Delhi, the 12th October, 2023 S.O. 4458 (E)." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Gazette of India Extraordinary. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**Convention notes:** all section references are to the Green Credit Rules, 2023 unless stated otherwise.

# 2. What This Regulation Is and Why It Applies to the Workspace

FACT: "in exercise of the powers conferred by section 3, section 6 and section 25 of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 (29 of 1986), the Central Government hereby makes the following rules" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, preamble. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The green credit programme shall incentivise environmental positive actions through market-based mechanism and generate green credit, which shall be tradable and made available for trading on a domestic market platform." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "the green credit generated or procured to fulfil any obligation in compliance of any law for the time being in force shall not be tradable." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 2(3) proviso. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "the Green Credit programme is independent of the carbon credit under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 made under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (52 of 2001), an environmental activity generating green credit may have climate co-benefits, such as reduction or removal of carbon emissions and an activity generating green credit under Green Credit programme may also get carbon credit from the same activity under the said Scheme" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, preamble. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Analytical inference:* for workspaces operating warehouses, freight stations, or transport hubs in India, or managing afforestation or water-conservation activities on operational landholdings, the programme creates a pathway to generate tradable credits from voluntary activities, distinct from any activity undertaken to satisfy a separate statutory compliance obligation.

# 3. Issues Requiring Immediate Action

*Operational implication:* the workspace should assess whether any India-based operational sites currently undertake any of the eight eligible activities named in Section 8, and monitor the GCP portal for the activity-specific methodology notifications (Section 6) that would make credit registration for those activities practically possible.

FACT: "In its initial phase, the GCP focuses on two key activities: water conservation and afforestation. Draft methodologies for awarding Green Credits have been developed and will be notified for stakeholder consultation." *Source: PIB Press Release, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, 13 October 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1967476

# 4. How the Workspace Sits in the Compliance Chain

FACT: "The participation to the Green Credit programme under these rules shall be based on voluntary participation." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 14(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, a Society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (21 of 1860) vide Registration No.596/1990-91, dated the 12th March, 1991 and an autonomous body as declared by the then Ministry of Environment and Forests, Government of India vide Resolution No.1-8/89-RT, dated the 22nd June, 1990, shall be the Administrator under these rules." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether a freight forwarding workspace, in its capacity as operator of Indian warehouses, freight stations, or transport hubs, constitutes a "person or entity" eligible to register activities and receive Green Credits, and whether specific site activities qualify under the enacted categories, requires verification against individual site operations and published methodologies once notified.

# 5. Authoritative Guidance Document Analysis

*No authoritative guidance documents (methodology notifications, designated agency guidelines, trading platform operating rules) have been enacted and published as of this generation date under Rule 5(3) or Rule 7(3); the enacted rules explicitly anticipate their future publication.*

FACT: "In its initial phase, the GCP focuses on two key activities: water conservation and afforestation. Draft methodologies for awarding Green Credits have been developed and will be notified for stakeholder consultation." *Source: PIB Press Release, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, 13 October 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1967476

*Analytical inference:* this is a government announcement describing the programme's initial implementation phase, not itself an enacted guidance instrument; the pending methodology notifications themselves are tracked in Section 6.

# 6. Anticipated Authoritative Guidance and Pending Regulatory Events

FACT: "The methodology for calculating the green credit in respect of any activity undertaken shall be such as may be notified by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Administrator." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 5(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Analytical inference:* logistics-relevant methodologies (waste management, air pollution reduction, sustainable buildings) are expected to follow the initial water-conservation and afforestation phase, though no published timeline exists for them.

FACT: "The Administrator shall designate such entities to act as designated agency in accordance with the guidelines approved by the Central Government." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 13(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The Administrator shall establish and maintain a trading platform with the approval of the Central Government." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 11(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The Steering Committee shall recommend measures to generate demand for green credit in the country." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 14(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

# 7. Threshold Questions

**Q1: Does the workspace's India-based operational activity fall within one of the eight eligible categories?**

FACT: "(i) tree plantation—to promote activities for increasing the green cover across the country; (ii) water management—to promote water conservation, water harvesting and water use efficiency or water savings, including treatment and reuse of wastewater; (iii) sustainable agriculture—to promote natural and regenerative agricultural practices and land restoration to improve productivity, soil health and nutritional value of food produced; (iv) waste management—to promote circularity, sustainable and improved practices for waste management, including collection, segregation, and environmentally sound management; (v) air pollution reduction—to promote measures for reducing air pollution and other pollution abatement activities; (vi) mangrove conservation and restoration—to promote measures for conservation and restoration of mangroves;" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether specific logistics-site activities qualify under the enacted categories requires verification against published methodologies when notified.

**Q2: Are Green Credits generated under mandatory compliance obligations tradable?**

FACT: "the green credit generated or procured to fulfil any obligation in compliance of any law for the time being in force shall not be tradable." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 2(3) proviso. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**Q3: Can the same activity generate both Green Credits and Carbon Credits?**

FACT: "the Green Credit programme is independent of the carbon credit under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme, 2023 made under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001 (52 of 2001), an environmental activity generating green credit may have climate co-benefits, such as reduction or removal of carbon emissions and an activity generating green credit under Green Credit programme may also get carbon credit from the same activity under the said Scheme" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, preamble. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**Q4: Is self-verification available for small projects?**

FACT: "with self-verification for small projects" *Source: PIB Press Release, MoEF&CC, 13 October 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1967476

FACT: "for self-certification or third-party certification for the registration of an activity for issuance of green credits and its inspection and verification by designated agency" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(3)(d). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

# 8. Substantive Requirements

**1. Eligible activities.** FACT: "(i) tree plantation—to promote activities for increasing the green cover across the country; (ii) water management—to promote water conservation, water harvesting and water use efficiency or water savings, including treatment and reuse of wastewater; (iii) sustainable agriculture—to promote natural and regenerative agricultural practices and land restoration to improve productivity, soil health and nutritional value of food produced; (iv) waste management—to promote circularity, sustainable and improved practices for waste management, including collection, segregation, and environmentally sound management; (v) air pollution reduction—to promote measures for reducing air pollution and other pollution abatement activities; (vi) mangrove conservation and restoration—to promote measures for conservation and restoration of mangroves;" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**2. Credit calculation basis.** FACT: "The calculation of green credit in respect of any activity undertaken shall be based on equivalence of resource requirement, parity of scale, scope, size and other relevant parameters required to achieve the desired environmental outcome." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 5(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**3. Credit calculation methodology.** FACT: "The methodology for calculating the green credit in respect of any activity undertaken shall be such as may be notified by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Administrator." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 5(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**4. Non-tradability of compliance credits (scope limit).** FACT: "the green credit generated or procured to fulfil any obligation in compliance of any law for the time being in force shall not be tradable." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 2(3) proviso. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**5. Administrator core responsibilities.** FACT: "develop guidelines, processes and procedures for the implementation of the green credit programme under these rules; (b) develop methodologies, registration process, guidelines and associated measurement, reporting and verification mechanism; (c) establish methodologies and processes for issuance of green credit (including issuance of digital green credit), and equivalence of green credit generated from each identified activity" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(3)(a)-(c). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**6. Administrator trading-oversight and fraud-prevention power (penalty-adjacent provision).** FACT: "regulate matters relating to trading of green credit certificates and to safeguard interest of sellers and buyers; and take preventive and corrective actions to prevent fraud or mistrust." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(3)(i). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**7. Central Government approval requirement.** FACT: "The Administrator shall seek approval of the Central Government for guidelines and methodologies under sub-rule (3)." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(4). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**8. Audit cycle (recurring primary deadline).** FACT: "The activities of the Administrator, designated agency, Registry, trading platform and knowledge and data platform shall be audited within a period of one year at the end of every third financial year by independent auditors to be appointed by the Central Government on the recommendation of the Steering Committee." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 15(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**9. Audit report submission.** FACT: "The auditor referred to in sub-rule (1) shall submit its audit report to the Administrator." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 15(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**10. Action-taken report deadline.** FACT: "The Administrator shall submit an action taken report on the audit report to the Central Government within a period of six months from the date of the receipt of the audit report." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 15(3). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**11. Activity registration.** FACT: "A person or entity desirous of obtaining green credit shall register the activity with the Administrator for any activity referred to in sub-rule (2) undertaken by him for grant of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(3). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**12. Application channel.** FACT: "An application for registration under sub-rule (3) shall be made to the Administrator electronically through a website established by the Central Government for that purpose." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(4). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**13. Verification by designated agency.** FACT: "On receipt of the application under sub-rule (4), the Administrator shall cause the activity to be verified by a designated agency." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(5). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**14. Verification report.** FACT: "The designated agency shall, after making such verification and inquiry as it may deem necessary, in accordance with the guideline made in this behalf, submit a report to the Administrator verifying the activities undertaken by the applicant." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(6). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**15. Certificate issuance.** FACT: "On receipt of the report under sub-rule (6) verifying the activities undertaken by the applicant, the Administrator shall grant the applicant a certificate of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(7). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**16. Annual returns by designated agency.** FACT: "The designated agency shall file annual returns to the Administrator in accordance with the guidelines." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 13(3). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**17. Registry establishment.** FACT: "The Administrator or designated agency shall establish and maintain a Green Credit Registry for the registration and issuance of each Green Credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 10(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**18. Registry database function.** FACT: "The Registry shall be an electronic database, which, inter alia, shall contain common data elements relevant to the registration and issuance of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 10(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**19. Trading platform establishment.** FACT: "The Administrator shall establish and maintain a trading platform with the approval of the Central Government." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 11(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**20. Trading platform function.** FACT: "The trading platform shall perform functions regarding the trading of green credit, in accordance with the guidelines made by the Administrator with the approval of the Central Government." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 11(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**21. Voluntary participation (scope limit).** FACT: "The participation to the Green Credit programme under these rules shall be based on voluntary participation." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 14(1). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

**22. Effective date.** FACT: "These rules may be called the Green Credit Rules, 2023. (2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 1. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Legal Confirmation Required:* whether the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986's general enforcement powers extend to Green-Credit-specific violations (for example, fraudulent credit claims or trading of non-tradable credits) beyond the Administrator's own fraud-prevention power (obligation 6) requires legal confirmation; no separate financial penalty quantum for non-participation or breach is stated anywhere in the enacted rules.

**Required-slot coverage.** `jurisdictional_scope` is covered above (Section 2, the preamble's own Environment (Protection) Act citation). `effective_date` is covered above (obligation 22, Rule 1's own commencement clause, and the Gazette notification's own "New Delhi, the 12th October, 2023" date in Section 1). `penalty_summary` is covered above (obligation 6): the enacted rules' own closest enforcement-adjacent provision is the Administrator's power to "take preventive and corrective actions to prevent fraud or mistrust," and this is the honest, sourced answer — the enacted text states no separate fine or sanction quantum. `primary_deadline` is covered above (obligation 8): the recurring statutory audit cycle, "within a period of one year at the end of every third financial year," is the one dated, recurring compliance deadline stated anywhere in the enacted rules' own text.

**Qualification accounting.** Per-year trajectory: CAPTURED via `metadata.requirement_trajectory` (non-null): the draft-consultation date, the Rules' own commencement date, and the recurring third-financial-year audit cycle. Exceptions and carve-outs: no unnegated exception/exemption/carve-out stem word is stated anywhere in the enacted rules' own text (the non-tradability proviso in obligation 4 is a scope limit on tradability, not an "exception" in the stem-word sense). No exceptions are stated in Sections covering the Green Credit Rules' registration, calculation, and trading provisions. Scope limits: CAPTURED via obligation 2's own source_span, which states the credit-calculation basis turns on "parity of scale, scope, size and other relevant parameters."

*Legal Confirmation Required (non-tradability qualifier):* Rule 2(3)'s own proviso that compliance-generated credits "shall not be tradable" (obligation 4 above) is a material qualification on the market-based mechanism described in obligation 21; whether a specific workspace activity was undertaken to satisfy a separate statutory obligation, and is therefore non-tradable, requires legal review of that activity's own regulatory basis.

Obligations surveyed: 22; workspace-adjacent: 14; extracted as FACT: 22.

# 9. Product-Specific Compliance Status

*Not addressed: the Green Credit Rules define no product, cargo, or commodity compliance category; they are an activity-based environmental-incentive programme, not a product regulation.*

# 10. Registration and Reporting Obligations

FACT: "A person or entity desirous of obtaining green credit shall register the activity with the Administrator for any activity referred to in sub-rule (2) undertaken by him for grant of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(3). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "An application for registration under sub-rule (3) shall be made to the Administrator electronically through a website established by the Central Government for that purpose." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(4). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "On receipt of the application under sub-rule (4), the Administrator shall cause the activity to be verified by a designated agency." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(5). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The designated agency shall, after making such verification and inquiry as it may deem necessary, in accordance with the guideline made in this behalf, submit a report to the Administrator verifying the activities undertaken by the applicant." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(6). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "On receipt of the report under sub-rule (6) verifying the activities undertaken by the applicant, the Administrator shall grant the applicant a certificate of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 4(7). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "The designated agency shall file annual returns to the Administrator in accordance with the guidelines." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 13(3). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Operational implication:* no annual-return obligation is imposed on credit-generating entities (applicants) in the enacted text; this recurring reporting obligation falls on the designated agency, not the workspace itself, unless the workspace is itself designated as a designated agency.

# 11. Operational System Requirements

*Operational implication:* to register activities under Rule 4(4), the workspace requires access to the central government portal and the ability to submit electronic applications; this requires identification of the responsible internal function (sustainability, operations, or compliance) and assignment of portal credentials.

FACT: "The Registry shall be an electronic database, which, inter alia, shall contain common data elements relevant to the registration and issuance of green credit." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 10(2). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Operational implication:* when the trading platform is established under Rule 11, workspaces holding Green Credit certificates will require platform access to execute sales; specific technology requirements are not yet published.

# 12. Exemptions and Edge Cases

FACT: "the green credit generated or procured to fulfil any obligation in compliance of any law for the time being in force shall not be tradable." *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 2(3) proviso. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

*Analytical inference:* for workspaces whose India operations already undertake environmental activities to comply with other environmental statutes, those compliance activities will not generate tradable Green Credits even if they would otherwise qualify under Rule 4(2); only genuinely voluntary, supra-compliance activities are eligible for tradable credits.

FACT: "for self-certification or third-party certification for the registration of an activity for issuance of green credits and its inspection and verification by designated agency" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Rule 7(3)(d). https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

FACT: "with self-verification for small projects" *Source: PIB Press Release, MoEF&CC, 13 October 2023. https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1967476

# 13. Adjacent Industry Research and Alternatives

FACT: "Freight transport is the backbone of India’s economy, but it is also one of the most emissions-intensive parts of the transport system." *Source: Institutionalizing Freight Emissions Accounting in India, TERI, 9 February 2026. https://www.teriin.org/policy-brief/institutionalizing-freight-emissions-accounting-india-pathways-clean-freight-programs

FACT: "India’s freight transport sector offers enormous potential for climate mitigation and sustainable economic development by increasing its efficiency, shift of road based freight to railway and ships and promoting modern technologies." *Source: Green Freight India, International Climate Initiative (IKI). https://www.international-climate-initiative.com/en/project/green-freight-india-18-i-361-ind-g-green-freight/

*Analytical inference:* both the TERI freight-emissions-accounting research and the IKI Green Freight India programme (National Integrated Logistics Plan coordination, climate-friendly logistics standards, and pilot corridors) are adjacent India-freight-decarbonisation efforts distinct from the Green Credit programme itself; a workspace tracking India's environmental-incentive landscape for freight should monitor these alongside the Green Credit Rules, since standardised freight-emissions accounting could eventually feed Green Credit methodology design for the waste-management and air-pollution-reduction activity categories.

# 14. Confirmed Regulatory Timeline

- 26th June 2023: draft Green Credit Programme Implementation Rules, 2023 published in the Gazette for public consultation, notification S.O. 2779(E).
- 12th October, 2023: Green Credit Rules, 2023 notified in the Gazette of India Extraordinary, S.O. 4458(E); rules enter into force on publication.
- 13 OCT 2023: PIB press release on the Green Credit Programme's initial phase.
- Every third financial year: recurring independent audit of the Administrator, designated agency, Registry, trading platform, and knowledge and data platform.

*Source for timeline entries: Green Credit Rules, 2023, Gazette of India Extraordinary (https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf); PIB Press Release, MoEF&CC, 13 October 2023 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=1967476).*

FACT: "the draft Green Credit Programme Implementation Rules, 2023 was published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (ii), vide notification number S.O. 2779(E), dated the 26th June 2023 inviting objections and suggestions from all persons" *Source: Green Credit Rules, 2023, preamble. https://egazette.gov.in/WriteReadData/2023/249377.pdf

metadata.what_is_it: India's Green Credit Rules, 2023, notified 12 October 2023 under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, a national voluntary market-based programme awarding tradable Green Credits for eight named environmental activities, administered by the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education.
metadata.why_matters: Waste management, air pollution reduction, sustainable building, and water management are named eligible activity categories that intersect with warehouse, depot, and freight-station operations in India, giving freight-forwarding workspaces a potential voluntary credit-generation pathway once activity methodologies are notified.
key_data: eight eligible activity categories under Rule 4(2)
rules came into force 12 October 2023 on Gazette publication
recurring independent audit every third financial year under Rule 15(1)
compliance-generated credits are not tradable under Rule 2(3)

steps.label: draft Green Credit Programme Implementation Rules published for public consultation
Green Credit Rules, 2023 notified and come into force
PIB press release; GCP portal activated
